This is an exquisite stone pavilion; the columns, lintels, roof tiles, drip tiles, rafters, and other structural elements are all made of stone, but the workmanship is exquisite, almost indistinguishable from wood. Only the two main doors of the entire pavilion are made of wood — this is also the origin of the name "Mumen Temple" (Wooden Gate Temple). To fully demonstrate the solemnity and preciousness of the pagoda pavilion, a timber main hall was built outside the stone pavilion to cover it. A pavilion built within a hall, a pagoda built within a pavilion — this form is truly rare, a rare treasure for architectural scholars and carving artists to study and appreciate.

projects.name: 卧佛院摩崖造像
projects.address: 资阳市安岳县八庙乡卧佛沟
projects.content_zh: 卧佛院摩崖造像位于资阳市安岳县，现如今卧佛院虽已被毁，但卧佛沟两侧精美的石刻还在向我们诉说着盛唐时期的辉煌。在卧佛沟两侧的崖壁上，唐代的能工巧匠们留下了传世佳作，凿有大大小小龛窟共138个，其中佛像造像84龛，总数量达到1593尊。在这些佛像之中，最壮观的莫过于释迦牟尼的横卧造像了。这座卧佛像全长23米，头长3米，肩宽3.1米，侧卧于崖壁之上。佛像双目微闭，嘴角微微翘起，形体修长，面部圆润，神情安详端庄。这座雕像用笔精练，寥寥数笔，生动形象地表现出释迦牟尼涅槃时的超脱景象。除了这座卧佛造像之外，卧佛沟的其他佛像也是精彩绝伦。卧佛像上部的诸弟子像，个个栩栩如生，呈现出肃穆的神情。值得一提的是，这里的造像充分利用了视觉因素，造像的上半身总是超出正常比例，这是因为虔诚的信徒们都是匍匐在造像前面，以仰视的视角观之，这个时候造像就呈现为正常的人体比例，十分威武。卧佛沟不仅有摩崖造像，还有大量宝贵的经书石刻。在卧佛像对面的崖壁上，就是卧佛院的藏经阁。崖壁之上，共凿有55个藏经龛窟。至今保存较为完整的经洞共15个，造字面积达131平方米，皆为大小规格在2~4厘米的端正楷书。藏经洞内所刻经目包括《大唐东京大敬爱寺一切经论目序》《大般涅槃经》《法华经》《妙法莲华经》《大方便佛报恩经》《般若波罗蜜多心经》《佛名经》《檀三藏经》等共16部，所刻经文不仅字迹工整，更为可贵的是记有确切的年代，是研究佛教文化的重要资料。
projects.content_en: Cliffside Statues of Wofo Temple are located in Anyue County, Ziyang City. Although Wofo Temple has now been destroyed, the exquisite stone carvings on both sides of Wofo Valley still tell us of the glory of the High Tang period. On the cliff walls on both sides of Wofo Valley, skilled Tang dynasty craftsmen left masterpieces handed down through generations, chiseling a total of 138 niches and caves large and small, among which 84 niches contain Buddha statues, with a total count reaching 1,593. Among these Buddha statues, the most spectacular is none other than the reclining statue of Shakyamuni. This reclining Buddha statue is 23m long overall, with a 3m head and 3.1m shoulder width, lying on its side on the cliff wall. The Buddha has eyes slightly closed, corners of the mouth slightly upturned, a slender body, a rounded face, and a serene and dignified expression. This statue uses concise carving strokes, with just a few strokes vividly expressing the transcendent scene of Shakyamuni at nirvana. Besides this reclining Buddha statue, the other Buddha statues in Wofo Valley are also superb. The disciple statues above the reclining Buddha are each lifelike, presenting solemn expressions. It is worth mentioning that the statues here fully utilize visual factors: the upper body of the statues always exceeds normal proportions, because devout believers all prostrate themselves in front of the statues, viewing from a仰视 perspective — at this time the statues present normal human proportions, very majestic. Wofo Valley has not only cliffside statues but also a large number of precious scripture stone carvings. On the cliff wall opposite the reclining Buddha statue is the scripture library of Wofo Temple. On the cliff wall, a total of 55 scripture-storage niches were chiseled. To date, 15 scripture caves are relatively well preserved, with a total carved character area of 131 sq m, all in neat regular script of 2-4cm size. The scripture catalogs carved inside the scripture caves include 16 works such as "Preface to the Catalog of All Sutras and Shastras at Daai Temple in Eastern Capital of Great Tang," "Mahaparinirvana Sutra," "Lotus Sutra," "Wonderful Dharma Lotus Sutra," "Great Expediency Buddha Repayment Sutra," "Prajnaparamita Heart Sutra," "Buddha Name Sutra," and "Sandalwood Three Basket Sutra." The carved scriptures are not only neatly written, but more valuably record exact dates — important material for studying Buddhist culture.

projects.name: 道林寺
projects.address: 资阳市安岳县姚市镇道林村
projects.content_zh: 安岳县姚市镇道林村本是一个平凡的小村落，但却拥有一座家家户户知晓并引以为豪的寺庙——道林寺。道林寺始建于元代，重修于明永乐年间，它能够保存至今，就不得不提起明代高僧无际禅师了。永乐五年(1407年)，明成祖朱棣召见全国著名高僧进京讲经说法，无际禅师的谈吐深得朱棣赏识，于是明成祖御赐重修道林寺无际禅师道场。明清年间，道林寺又经历了数次重修扩建，几经兴废，如今仅存大雄宝殿这一古代建筑了。道林寺最近重新修缮了一次，建筑焕然一新。走进道林寺的山门，就看见天王殿。天王殿是近代修建的建筑，从油漆剥落的情况来看，也有些年代了。走过天王殿之后，便是重修后的大雄殿了。大雄殿面阔三间，进深三间，单檐歇山顶形制。古代的建筑师们独具匠心，在殿内采取抬梁式承重、穿斗式梁架的混合结构。大雄殿占地面积虽然不大，但是斗拱数量众多，使建筑显得庄重威严，雄伟壮观。我们和村里人提起附近的古建筑的时候，村里人都指着道林寺的方向，非常自豪地向我们介绍这座古建筑。相信在村民们的爱护之下，道林寺一定会保存得很好，让更多后人们瞻仰古代工艺之精美。
projects.content_en: Daolin Village, Yaoshi Town, Anyue County was originally an ordinary small village, but it possesses a temple known to every household and a source of pride — Daolin Temple. Daolin Temple was founded in Yuan dynasty and rebuilt during the Ming Yongle era. That it can be preserved to this day must be attributed to the famous Ming dynasty monk Wuji Chan Master. In the 5th year of Yongle (1407), the Yongle Emperor Zhu Di summoned famous eminent monks from across the country to the capital to preach sutras and expound the Dharma; Wuji Chan Master's eloquence deeply impressed Zhu Di, so the Yongle Emperor bestowed an imperial decree to rebuild the Daolin Temple as the道场 (practice site) of Wuji Chan Master. During the Ming and Qing dynasties, Daolin Temple underwent several reconstructions and expansions, through many rises and falls; today only the Mahavira Hall, an ancient building, remains. Daolin Temple was recently renovated once more, and the building looks brand new. Entering the mountain gate of Daolin Temple, one sees the Heavenly Kings Hall. The Heavenly Kings Hall is a modern-era building; judging from the peeling paint, it also has some age. Passing through the Heavenly Kings Hall, one reaches the rebuilt Mahavira Hall. The Mahavira Hall is 3 bays wide and 3 bays deep, with a single-eave xieshan roof form. Ancient architects showed ingenuity by adopting a mixed structure of post-and-lintel load-bearing and chuan-dou frame inside the hall. Although the Mahavira Hall does not occupy a large area, it has numerous bracket sets, making the building appear solemn, majestic, and imposing. When we mentioned nearby ancient buildings to the villagers, they all pointed in the direction of Daolin Temple and introduced this ancient building to us with great pride. It is believed that under the villagers' care, Daolin Temple will surely be well preserved, allowing more future generations to admire the exquisite craftsmanship of antiquity.

projects.name: 兴禅寺
projects.address: 内江市资中县双龙镇骑龙庵村东南
projects.content_zh: 兴禅寺坐落在距资中县城23公里的骑龙村石坝山上，现为骑龙小学校。距离寺门不远有半亩大小土地，色如香灰，故名香灰土，传说寺里的香灰都倒在这里，才造成了这种情况。由此也可见历史上的兴禅寺规模之大和香火之旺。到达此地时，有大叔大娘两人正在地里劳作，见行人，便上前询问。待说明来意，大娘告诉我，寺现为小学校址，现已放假，并不对外开放。还道兴禅寺曾是蜀中最大的寺庙之一，有俗语大和尚二万五，小和尚不计数，说的就是此寺。不过如今该寺业已没落，除殿宇尚存，并无菩萨与僧人。听其言，不免感慨唏嘘良久。后幸有另一大叔说有车要入内，便要开门，大娘上前说了我的情况，才得以入寺参观。兴禅寺始建于明正德十年(1515年)，清乾隆年间(1736—1795年)、嘉庆年间(1796—1820年)、道光年间(1821—1850年)增修。坐西向东，占地面积1378平方米，为四合院布局，现存前殿、正殿、观音殿。寺庙规模宏大，殿宇庄严雄壮，雕梁画栋，飞檐斗拱，种种建筑无不体现建筑者高超的技艺。正殿面阔三间17.6米，进深三间13.4米，通高11米，素面台基高1米，踏道5级，歇山顶，穿斗式梁架。其后的观音殿面阔五间19.8米，进深五间16米，重檐歇山顶，穿斗式梁架。殿内有明万历十三年(1585年)广游兴禅寺次韵律碑、清嘉庆二十三年(1818年)重修兴禅寺院记碑。前殿大门檐柱上有清代名士伍士仁撰两联，一曰：心怀一部春秋，报主尽忠扶社稷；力挽三分汉鼎，成仁取义正乾坤。一曰：伐魏征吴，浩气长存塞天地；仁民爱物，芳名广播寿山河。新人下得车来，有新人入，想是曾有愿景，而今喜结连理，故此回寺了结前愿，个个情怀，引人遐思。新人下得车来，有新人入，想是曾有愿景，而今喜结连理，故此回寺了结前愿。男孩风度翩翩，姑娘娇艳如花，自是郎才女貌，好一段古寺姻缘。而古寺与新人，仿佛预示着破落的寺庙又将重焕生机，此事便敬请诸君拭目以待。
projects.content_en: Xingchan Temple is located on Shiba Mountain, Qilong Village, 23km from Zizhong County town, currently serving as Qilong Primary School. Not far from the temple gate is a half-mu plot of land with ash-colored soil, hence named Xianghuitu (Incense Ash Earth); legend says the temple's incense ash was all dumped here, creating this condition. This also shows the historical scale and flourishing incense of Xingchan Temple. Upon arrival, an uncle and aunt were working in the fields; seeing a pedestrian, they came forward to inquire. After explaining my purpose, the aunt told me the temple is now a primary school site, currently on vacation and not open to the public. She also said Xingchan Temple was once one of the largest temples in Sichuan, with the saying "25,000 great monks, countless small monks" referring to this temple. But now the temple has declined; apart from the surviving halls, there are no Buddhas or monks. Hearing her words, I could not help sighing with emotion for a long time. Fortunately, another uncle said a vehicle needed to enter and would open the gate; the aunt explained my situation, and I was allowed to enter and visit. Xingchan Temple was founded in the 10th year of Zhengde (1515), Ming dynasty, and expanded during Qing Qianlong (1736-1795), Jiaqing (1796-1820), and Daoguang (1821-1850) eras. Facing east, covering 1,378 sq m, with a siheyuan layout, currently preserving the front hall, main hall, and Guanyin Hall. The temple is large-scale, with solemn and majestic halls, carved beams and painted pillars, flying eaves and bracket sets — all buildings reflect the builders' superb craftsmanship. The main hall is 3 bays wide (17.6m), 3 bays deep (13.4m), 11m total height, with a plain platform base 1m high, 5 steps, xieshan roof, and chuan-dou frame. The Guanyin Hall behind it is 5 bays wide (19.8m), 5 bays deep (16m), with a double-eave xieshan roof and chuan-dou frame. Inside the hall are the "Guangyou Xingchan Temple Ciyunlu Stele" from the 13th year of Wanli (1585), Ming, and the "Record Stele of Rebuilding Xingchan Temple Courtyard" from the 23rd year of Jiaqing (1818), Qing. On the eave columns of the front hall gate are two couplets by Qing dynasty scholar Wu Shiren: one reads "With a heart for the Spring and Autumn Annals, serving the lord with utmost loyalty to support the state; with strength to turn back the three-part Han tripod, achieving benevolence and righteousness to uphold the universe." The other reads "Campaigning against Wei and Wu, noble spirit forever fills heaven and earth; loving the people and all creatures, fine name broadcasts long life across mountains and rivers." Newlyweds got off the car and entered; it seems they once made a vow and now, happily married, have returned to the temple to fulfill it. Each with their own feelings, evoking reverie. The young man is elegant and the young woman is beautiful as a flower — truly a talented man and a beautiful woman, a fine ancient temple marriage. And the ancient temple with the newlyweds seems to foreshadow that the dilapidated temple will regain vitality; this matter we shall wait and see.

projects.name: 盐神庙
projects.address: 内江市资中县罗泉镇东北
projects.content_zh: 盐神庙位于四川资中罗泉镇，建于清同治七年(1868年)，坐东向西，占地面积1869平方米，四合院布局。现存戏楼、正殿、左右厢房。戏楼面阔11.75米，进深11.2米。歇山顶，穿斗式梁架，梁上有清同治七年题记。正殿面阔三间14.5米，进深11.35米，通高13米，素面台基高2.7米，踏道13级，歇山顶，抬梁式梁架。左右厢房各面阔四间18米，进深4.1米。庙内供奉管仲为盐神，关羽和火神则是管仲的辅佐，民间传统信仰特征浓厚。罗泉镇因产盐而天下闻名，其产盐历史最早可追溯到秦代，到清朝时，罗泉镇盐业开发已达到顶峰，光绪年间已有盐井1500余眼，因此，才有此地所建如何规模的盐神庙了。总体看来，罗泉盐神庙布局规整，建筑类型丰富，并且随地形高低起伏，出檐高挑，形态生动。建筑采用与附近民居类似的材料与结构，与市镇纹理浑然一体。封火墙居上还有极为精美的民间故事雕刻，鲜明地体现了当地商业民俗文化特色。
projects.content_en: Shrine of Salt God is located in Luozhen Town, Zizhong County, Sichuan. Built in the 7th year of Tongzhi (1868), Qing dynasty, facing west from east, covering 1,869 sq m, with a siheyuan layout. Currently preserving the theater tower, main hall, and left and right wing rooms. The theater tower is 11.75m wide, 11.2m deep, with xieshan roof and chuan-dou frame; the beam bears an inscription from the 7th year of Tongzhi. The main hall is 3 bays wide (14.5m), 11.35m deep, 13m total height, with a plain platform base 2.7m high, 13 steps, xieshan roof, and post-and-lintel frame. The left and right wing rooms are each 4 bays wide (18m), 4.1m deep. Inside the temple, Guan Zhong is enshrined as the Salt God, while Guan Yu and the Fire God are his assistants — with strong characteristics of folk traditional beliefs. Luozhen Town is world-famous for salt production; its salt production history can be traced back to the Qin dynasty. By the Qing dynasty, salt development in Luozhen Town reached its peak; during the Guangxu era there were over 1,500 salt wells — hence the scale of the Salt God Shrine built here. Overall, Luozhen Salt God Shrine has a regular layout and rich building types, following the undulating terrain with high, projecting eaves and vivid forms. The buildings use materials and structures similar to nearby residences, integrating seamlessly with the town fabric. Above the fire-sealing walls are extremely exquisite folk story carvings, vividly reflecting the local commercial folk culture characteristics.

projects.name: 宁国寺
projects.address: 内江市资中县重龙镇北3.5公里
projects.content_zh: 宁国寺位于资中县重龙镇北3.5公里处，始建于东汉建安五年(200年)，原名德纯寺。唐代获武皇赐名菩提道场。唐初禅宗分为南北两派，智诜创建的保唐禅派，首将禅宗引入四川，宁国寺由此兴盛，人称巴蜀第一禅林。宋更名为宁国寺。后多次历经战火，近年再予重修，恢复原有五殿形制，再续千年香火传奇。宁国寺原有五重殿宇，僧人用房；古物、古墓集中，被州志记为县中各寺之冠。建筑仅存正殿，面阔三间12.7米，进深三间10.3米，素面台基高0.6米，通高7米，抬梁式梁架，歇山顶，檐下施如意斗拱32朵。梁上有大明天顺七年重修题记，证明建筑初建年代。宁国寺历史上高僧辈出，除了智诜禅师外，另有唐无相禅师，他本是新罗王子，于728年来到中国，师从于高僧玄奘，后入蜀在宁国寺修行，最终成为一代高僧，并在成都主持修建大慈寺。传说中，宁国寺也是释迦牟尼木棉袈裟的最终归宿，据说当年木棉袈裟随达摩来至中原，智诜为武则天讲授佛法，而获赐袈裟，智诜将其奉于德纯寺正殿，也就是今天宁国寺的前身。无论传说真实与否，都说明了今天宁国寺在禅宗文化传统中的特殊地位。也因为这一渊源，当地政府于2006年重建寺庙，恢复原有五殿形制，再续千年香火传奇。
projects.content_en: Ningguo Temple is located 3.5km north of Chonglong Town, Zizhong County. Founded in the 5th year of Jian'an (200), Eastern Han, originally named Dechun Temple. In Tang dynasty it received the imperial name "Bodhi Daochang" from Empress Wu. In early Tang, Chan Buddhism split into Northern and Southern schools; the Baotang Chan school founded by Zhi Shen first introduced Chan Buddhism to Sichuan, and Ningguo Temple flourished from this, known as the "First Chan Forest of Bashu." In Song it was renamed Ningguo Temple. Later it经历 multiple wars, and was recently rebuilt again, restoring the original five-hall form and continuing the thousand-year incense legend. Ningguo Temple originally had five layers of halls and monk quarters; with concentrated antiquities and ancient tombs, it was recorded in the prefectural gazetteer as the foremost among all temples in the county. Only the main hall survives, 3 bays wide (12.7m), 3 bays deep (10.3m), with a plain platform base 0.6m high, 7m total height, post-and-lintel frame, xieshan roof, with 32 ruyi bracket sets beneath the eaves. The beam bears an inscription "rebuilt in the 7th year of Tianshun, Great Ming," proving the building's initial construction date. Ningguo Temple has produced many eminent monks in history; besides Master Zhi Shen, there was Tang Master Wuxiang, originally a prince of Silla, who came to China in 728, studied under the eminent monk Xuanzang, later entered Sichuan to practice at Ningguo Temple, eventually becoming a generation of eminent monk, and presided over the construction of Daci Temple in Chengdu. According to legend, Ningguo Temple is also the final resting place of Shakyamuni's kapok (cotton) kasaya robe. It is said that the kapok kasaya came to the Central Plains with Bodhidharma; Zhi Shen lectured on Buddhism for Empress Wu Zetian and was bestowed the kasaya; Zhi Shen enshrined it in the main hall of Dechun Temple, the predecessor of today's Ningguo Temple. Whether the legend is true or not, it illustrates Ningguo Temple's special position in Chan Buddhist cultural tradition today. Also because of this origin, the local government rebuilt the temple in 2006, restoring the original five-hall form and continuing the thousand-year incense legend.

projects.name: 资中文庙和武庙
projects.name_en: Temple of Confucius and Emperor Guan's Temple in Zizhong
projects.address: 内江市资中县重龙镇文庙街
projects.content_zh: 始建于北宋雍熙年间(984—987年)的资中文庙原在东大街，清道光九年(1829年)迁建于城北今址。文庙坐北朝南，面积约6800平方米，整体呈四合院布局。现存建筑有万仞宫墙、华表、礼门、仪门、照壁、棂星门、乡贤祠、泮池，等等。大成门面阔五间，进深二间，歇山顶，穿斗式梁架。大成殿面阔五间21.4米，进深三间9.55米，台基高2.9米，重檐歇山顶，穿斗式梁架。建筑状态良好，是全省保存得最完整的一座文庙之一。资中文庙祀有孔子全身石像。因邑人甚弘曾为孔子师，故雕像以记其事，现头像尚存。庙内有清代康熙至光绪八位皇帝御书匾额，是难得的宝贵文物。武庙始建于明嘉靖间(1522—1566年)，经过清代数次补修建，目前占地面积3700平方米，四合院布局。前殿、正殿、武星殿、后院、西长廊保存完好。武星殿阔三间10.4米，进深二间7.6米，高8.5米，悬山顶，穿斗式梁架，梁上有同治十三年补修题记。久闻资中是文化古城，县内自古文风盛行，而今文物众多，而文武庙无疑是其中翘楚。行至文武庙，文庙大门紧闭，并不对外开放，不免心内黯然，料想白跑一趟。转思有通行证在手，何惧之有？但细观大门良久，再逡巡外围，红墙黄瓦，飞檐镂壁，屋顶雕龙刻凤，墙外柳枝窈窕，端庄典雅中透出些俏皮温柔。而传承千年的文化遗迹紧锁门内，就让它们安静一会儿，沉淀一会儿罢，也许明天，我们会见识一个更辉煌的文庙。武庙紧邻文庙，七星门堂皇壮观，矗立无碍，可见几分雄壮之意，门前开阔平坦，自是一番浩然的气派。而绿树掩映中的殿宇庄严中透出些历史的沧桑感，向人们默默地倾诉千年的文治武功。
projects.content_en: The Temple of Confucius in Zizhong, founded during the Northern Song Yongxi era (984-987), was originally on East Street; in the 9th year of Daoguang (1829), Qing dynasty, it was relocated and built at its current site north of the city. The Confucian Temple faces south, covering about 6,800 sq m, with an overall siheyuan layout. Existing buildings include Wanren Palace Wall, ornamental columns (huabiao), Ritual Gate, Ceremony Gate, screen wall, Lingxing Gate, Local Worthy Shrine, Pan Pool, etc. Dacheng Gate is 5 bays wide, 2 bays deep, with xieshan roof and chuan-dou frame. Dacheng Hall is 5 bays wide (21.4m), 3 bays deep (9.55m), with a 2.9m high platform base, double-eave xieshan roof, and chuan-dou frame. The building is in good condition, one of the best-preserved Confucian temples in the province. The Zizhong Confucian Temple enshrines a full-body stone statue of Confucius. Because a local person named Hong once was Confucius' teacher, the statue was carved to record this event; the head currently survives. Inside the temple are imperial calligraphy plaques by eight emperors from Kangxi to Guangxu of Qing — rare and precious cultural relics. The Temple of Emperor Guan (Wumiao) was founded during the Ming Jiajing era (1522-1566), and经过 several repairs and expansions in Qing, currently covering 3,700 sq m with a siheyuan layout. The front hall, main hall, Wuxing Hall, rear courtyard, and west long corridor are well preserved. Wuxing Hall is 3 bays wide (10.4m), 2 bays deep (7.6m), 8.5m tall, with overhanging gable roof and chuan-dou frame; the beam bears an inscription "repaired in the 13th year of Tongzhi." Having long heard that Zizhong is a cultural ancient city with a flourishing literary tradition since ancient times, and now with numerous cultural relics, the Confucian and Guan temples are undoubtedly the foremost among them. Arriving at the temples, the Confucian Temple gate was tightly closed and not open to the public — I could not help feeling dejected, thinking I had made a wasted trip. Then I thought, with a pass in hand, what is there to fear? But after carefully observing the gate for a long time and patrolling the perimeter — red walls and yellow tiles, flying eaves and carved walls, roof carved with dragons and phoenixes, willow branches graceful outside the wall — there is a touch of playfulness and tenderness amid dignity and elegance. And the thousand-year-old cultural heritage locked inside the gate — let them be quiet for a while, settle for a while; perhaps tomorrow we will witness an even more brilliant Confucian Temple. The Guan Temple is adjacent to the Confucian Temple; its Seven-Star Gate is grand and magnificent, standing unobstructed, showing a sense of majesty. The area in front of the gate is open and flat, naturally with a浩然 and imposing air. And the halls nestled among green trees exude a sense of historical vicissitudes amid solemnity, silently recounting a thousand years of civil and martial achievements to the people.

projects.name: 永庆寺
projects.address: 内江市资中县城东北隅重龙山上
projects.content_zh: 永庆寺在重龙山顶南侧，始建于唐宋，明洪武时重修，后又经明清两朝多次改修。目前寺庙坐北朝南，四合院布局，占地面积10260平方米，建筑面积2869平方米。主要建筑由山门石坊、木牌坊、天王殿、来鹤亭、普陀殿、大雄宝殿、罗汉堂、东西厢房等组成。沿着层层石阶向重龙山上走，行至数百步，即使年轻力壮，也颇有些气喘。终于来到一广场，这里游人颇多，中央是送子观音像，建在高台上，菩萨面含微笑，俯视众生。善男信女求子者纷至沓来，香火旺盛。送子观音，俗称送子娘娘，相传只要摸摸圣像，即可生儿育女、子孙满堂，就是人生最大的福气，该像系现代众信客集资所塑。山门石牌坊系重建，正面刻重龙古迹，两旁有联曰：双鹤横江，缅仙吏遗踪，百尺楼头寻鹤架；重龙绕郭，踵名贤旧址，三台渡口望龙门。背面刻西蜀名刹，两旁有联曰：倚汉凌云，洵是西方法界；闻香掬水，分明胜地曹溪。牌坊雕刻精美，古朴自然，庄严大方。禹王宫木牌坊原在城内大东街，本为禹王宫[建于明嘉靖六年(1527年)]的大门，1968年迁于永庆寺内，紧贴天王殿而建。楼上书文命诞敷及永庆寺字样，笔力敦厚有力，朴实无华，神采内敛。其后是永庆寺天王殿，雄伟壮观。来鹤亭为宋代所建，亭后有普陀殿。殿后有大旱不竭的天池，天池后是大雄宝殿，右侧有月池，近年新建碑亭，陈列苏轼、黄庭坚、米芾、文天祥、董其昌等名家墨迹。其中尤以黄庭坚所书唐韩伯庸《幽兰赋》最为珍贵。藏经阁造型独特，遍体通红，飞檐巨柱，蔚为大观。飞檐多为祥云状，直指苍穹，有凌天之势。碑林在寺庙后山，多刻名家书法，造句文雅，笔力精深，在深深树影下傲然矗立。玉虚宫石雕，在深深树影下傲然矗立。
projects.content_en: Yongqing Temple is on the south side of Chonglong Mountain summit. Founded in Tang-Song, rebuilt during Ming Hongwu, and later modified and repaired multiple times during Ming and Qing dynasties. Currently the temple faces south, with a siheyuan layout, covering 10,260 sq m with 2,869 sq m building area. Main buildings consist of mountain gate stone archway, wooden paifang, Heavenly Kings Hall, Laihe Pavilion, Putuo Hall, Mahavira Hall, Arhat Hall, and east and west wing rooms. Walking up layer upon layer of stone steps toward Chonglong Mountain, after several hundred steps, even the young and strong become somewhat breathless. Finally arriving at a plaza, there are many visitors here; in the center is a statue of Songzi Guanyin (Child-Giving Guanyin), built on a high platform, the Bodhisattva with a smiling face, looking down at all beings. Devout men and women seeking children come in droves, and incense flourishes. Songzi Guanyin, commonly called the Child-Giving Goddess, is said to grant children and a house full of descendants just by touching the sacred statue — the greatest blessing in life. This statue was funded and sculpted by modern believers. The mountain gate stone archway was rebuilt; the front is engraved "Chonglong Ancient Relics," with couplets on both sides: "Twin cranes span the river, recalling the immortal official's traces, seeking the crane frame at the hundred-foot tower top; Chonglong encircles the city, following the famous sage's former site, gazing at the Dragon Gate at the Three-Terrace ferry." The back is engraved "Famous Temple of Western Shu," with couplets: "Leaning against the clouds and piercing the sky, truly the Western Dharma realm; smelling incense and scooping water, clearly the sacred Caoxi land." The archway is exquisitely carved, simple and natural, dignified and generous. The wooden paifang of Yu Palace was originally on Dadong Street in the city, serving as the gate of Yu Palace [built in the 6th year of Jiajing (1527), Ming]. In 1968 it was moved into Yongqing Temple, built close to the Heavenly Kings Hall. On the tower are written "Wen Ming Dan Fu" and "Yongqing Temple" characters, with vigorous and powerful brushwork, simple and unadorned, with restrained spirit. Behind it is Yongqing Temple's Heavenly Kings Hall, majestic and spectacular. Laihe Pavilion was built in Song dynasty; behind the pavilion is Putuo Hall. Behind the hall is the Tianchi (Heavenly Pool) that never dries up even in great drought; behind Tianchi is the Mahavira Hall, and on the right is the Moon Pool. In recent years a new stele pavilion was built, displaying calligraphy by famous masters such as Su Shi, Huang Tingjian, Mi Fu, Wen Tianxiang, and Dong Qichang. Among them, the "Orchid Ode" by Tang Han Boyong, written by Huang Tingjian, is the most precious. The Scripture Library has a unique form, entirely red, with flying eaves and giant columns — a spectacular sight. The flying eaves are mostly in auspicious cloud shapes, pointing straight at the sky, with a heaven-piercing momentum. The stele forest is on the back hill of the temple, mostly engraved with famous calligraphy, with elegant phrasing and profound brushwork, standing proudly in deep tree shadows. The Yuxu Palace stone carvings stand proudly in deep tree shadows.

projects.name: 建春门、城墙
projects.address: 内江市资中县重龙镇东200米沱江畔
projects.content_zh: 资中古城建于西魏恭帝二年(555年)，始建土墙。明弘治年间(1488—1505年)复建石城墙，清代多次增修。现存大东门城楼、城墙。城墙以条石砌成，内填土石，现存东、南、西三段总长度约1459米，高4.2米，厚3.8米。现存唯一城门大东门，也叫建春门。南宋始建，清同治四年重修。城门墙体仍有条石砌筑，拱形门洞高7.5米，宽3.55米，城墙厚6.75米。城门之上建木城楼，面阔三间6.2米，进深3.4米，重檐歇山顶，穿斗式梁架。资中古城因街道布局如船，素有船城之称。建春门现横跨船城街道之上，其厚重墙体与高耸楼阁与两旁连绵的民居形成强烈反差，石板铺砌的街道穿越门洞而过。行人也在历史的岁月中漫步前行。
projects.content_en: The ancient city of Zizhong was built in the 2nd year of Gongdi of Western Wei (555), initially with earthen walls. During Ming Hongzhi (1488-1505), stone city walls were rebuilt, and expanded and repaired multiple times in Qing. Currently preserving the Great East Gate tower and city wall. The wall is built of dressed stones with rammed earth and stone fill; the existing east, south, and west sections total about 1,459m in length, 4.2m high, 3.8m thick. The only surviving city gate is the Great East Gate, also called Jianchun Gate. Founded in Southern Song, rebuilt in the 4th year of Tongzhi, Qing. The gate wall is still built of dressed stones; the arched gateway is 7.5m high, 3.55m wide, and the wall is 6.75m thick. Above the gate stands a timber gate tower, 3 bays wide (6.2m), 3.4m deep, with double-eave xieshan roof and chuan-dou frame. The ancient city of Zizhong has long been called the "Boat City" because its street layout resembles a boat. Jianchun Gate now spans across the Boat City street; its massive wall and towering gate tower form a strong contrast with the continuous folk houses on both sides, and the stone-paved street passes through the gateway. Pedestrians also stroll forward through the years of history.

projects.name: 圣水寺
projects.address: 内江市市中区壕志口街圣江路151号
projects.content_zh: 便览内江诸寺，圣水寺蔚为大观，独领风骚，不愧于川中第一禅林之称。圣水寺位于四川省内江市中城区区3公里处，沱江之滨，建于唐咸通年间(860—873年)，宋、清均曾增修，宋名兴慈院圣水兴慈寺，后复原名。因寺后山有泉水流出，水质清纯爽口，终年不竭，故得名圣水寺。圣水寺占地面积2万平方米，建筑面积8000多平方米，庙房200多间，现存古建筑主要为明、清所建五重大殿及一些附属建筑。寺庙由四进院落组成：中轴线上自西向东布局的圆觉楼、藏经楼、大雄宝殿、天王殿，均属明清风格；中轴两侧是回廊，有客堂、五观堂、禅堂、念佛堂等；寺院左侧有玉佛殿、三圣殿、药师殿；再向左侧是观音殿和地藏殿；寺院右侧以祖师殿为主体构成一个独立的院落。其中大雄宝殿面阔三间15.35米，进深三间14.65米，通高14米，重檐歇山顶，抬梁式梁架。藏经楼始建于清雍正四年(1726年)，殿前有月池拱桥一座。圣水寺是蜀中重要禅宗寺院，历史上名僧辈出，如明清之际的丈雪禅师曾著有《锦江传灯录》《青松集》《耆老篇》等书，是一代禅学大师。从驻地步行到圣水寺，话说我们远远地看见门前广场上有一位大叔在打太极，他身手矫健，动作张弛有度，优雅而标准，颇有些电视剧里张真人的风采。后来翻书了解，那位大叔许是圣水寺的方丈智海法师，也未可知。
projects.content_en: Surveying all the temples of Neijiang, Shengshui Temple stands out magnificently, leading the pack, worthy of its title as the "First Chan Forest in Central Sichuan." Shengshui Temple is located 3km from the central urban area of Neijiang City, Sichuan, on the bank of the Tuo River. Built during the Tang Xiantong era (860-873), it was expanded in both Song and Qing dynasties. In Song it was named Xingci Yuan Shengshui Xingci Temple, later restored to its original name. Because a spring flows from the mountain behind the temple, with pure, refreshing water that never dries up year-round, it is named Shengshui (Holy Water) Temple. Shengshui Temple covers 20,000 sq m with over 8,000 sq m of building area and over 200 temple rooms. The existing ancient buildings are mainly five major halls built in Ming-Qing and some auxiliary buildings. The temple consists of four courtyards: along the central axis from west to east are the Yuanjue Tower, Scripture Library, Mahavira Hall, and Heavenly Kings Hall, all in Ming-Qing style; on both sides of the axis are cloisters with guest halls, Wuguan Hall, Chan Hall, Buddha Recitation Hall, etc.; on the left side of the temple are Jade Buddha Hall, Three Sages Hall, and Medicine Master Hall; further left are Guanyin Hall and Ksitigarbha Hall; on the right side of the temple, the Patriarch Hall forms an independent courtyard as the main body. Among them, the Mahavira Hall is 3 bays wide (15.35m), 3 bays deep (14.65m), 14m total height, with double-eave xieshan roof and post-and-lintel frame. The Scripture Library was founded in the 4th year of Yongzheng (1726), Qing, with a moon pool and arch bridge in front of the hall. Shengshui Temple is an important Chan Buddhist temple in Sichuan, with many famous monks throughout history; for example, Master Zhangxue at the Ming-Qing transition authored works such as "Jinjiang Lantern Transmission Record," "Pine Collection," and "Elders Chapter," a generation of Chan master. Walking from our accommodation to Shengshui Temple, we saw from afar an uncle practicing tai chi in the square in front of the gate. He was agile and vigorous, with movements relaxed and controlled, elegant and standard, quite like the style of Master Zhang in TV dramas. Later, looking it up in books, that uncle might have been the abbot of Shengshui Temple, Master Zhihai — who knows.

projects.name: 般若寺及石刻
projects.address: 内江市东兴区高桥镇般若村西南1.3公里
projects.content_zh: 般若寺位于四川省内江市东兴区三溪乡松柏寨，建于唐肃宗和代宗年间，宋咸淳时扩建，明万历重修，到清代具有七大殿、两偏殿的雄伟规模。因曾珍藏全国仅三部《般若经》之一而得名。历史上的般若寺，规模宏大，僧人多达上百人，后因各种原因，寺庙损毁严重。正门为朱漆高墙，中间处高近10米，颇为壮观，上有书法家晏纪元所书古般若寺字样。两边对联是书法家李果青用隶书所写，字形古朴，笔力深厚。寺庙第一殿是天王殿，藏经楼高大威严，红漆柱子，黑漆正门，门前松柏苍翠，绿树成荫。有鱼池建于中庭一方，池外壁呈蛇形，蜿蜒盘旋，恍惚自然。池子里金鱼悠然游戏，闻游客声而无动于衷，似通佛理。庭院中间还有假山、花台，山水相谐，花草不断，香气四溢，满庭芬芳。游人沉醉于此不能自拔，有钟声忽入耳际，才始觉驻足良久，前途尚待，流连前行。殿正中塑金释迦牟尼佛；背为西方三圣，文殊普贤菩萨、地藏王菩萨；两旁有十八罗汉，表情各异，栩栩如生，似与游者相述。东边是金碧辉煌的观音殿，西边是祖师殿。寺外还改建了灵芝崖，现出了原来的造像、石刻。寺内有佛耳岩62尊造像，多数成于唐代，高的达6.5米，小的仅数寸。徜徉般若寺之中，古寺庄严，殿宇精妙，雕像奇绝，花草繁茂，其中韵味，令人回味悠长。
projects.content_en: Bore (Prajna) Temple is located at Songbai Village, Sanxi Township, Dongxing District, Neijiang City, Sichuan. Built during the reigns of Emperor Suzong and Daizong of Tang, expanded in Song Xianchun, rebuilt in Ming Wanli, and by Qing dynasty it had the grand scale of seven major halls and two side halls. It was named because it once treasured one of only three copies of the Prajna Sutra in the country. Historically, Bore Temple was large-scale with up to a hundred monks; later, for various reasons, the temple was severely damaged. The main gate is a vermilion-painted high wall, nearly 10m high in the center, quite spectacular, with the characters "Ancient Bore Temple" written by calligrapher Yan Jiyuan. The couplets on both sides were written in clerical script by calligrapher Li Guoqing, with ancient forms and profound brush strength. The first hall of the temple is the Heavenly Kings Hall; the Scripture Library is tall and majestic, with red-lacquered columns and black-lacquered main gate; in front of the gate, pines and cypresses are verdant, with green trees forming shade. A fish pond is built in the center of the courtyard; the outer wall of the pond is snake-shaped, winding and coiling, vaguely natural. Goldfish play leisurely in the pond, unmoved by the sound of tourists, as if understanding Buddhist principles. In the middle of the courtyard there are also rockeries and flower terraces, with mountains and water in harmony, flowers and plants continuous, fragrance overflowing, filling the courtyard with sweetness. Visitors become intoxicated here and cannot tear themselves away; when the sound of a bell suddenly reaches the ears, they realize they have stopped for a long time, with the road ahead still waiting, and reluctantly move forward. In the center of the hall is a gilded statue of Shakyamuni Buddha; behind are the Three Sages of the West, Manjushri and Samantabhadra Bodhisattvas, and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva; on both sides are the Eighteen Arhats, each with different expressions, lifelike, as if conversing with visitors. To the east is the resplendent Guanyin Hall, to the west is the Patriarch Hall. Outside the temple, Lingzhi Cliff was also renovated, revealing the original statues and stone carvings. Inside the temple there are 62 statues at Fo'er Rock, mostly from Tang dynasty, with the tallest reaching 6.5m and the smallest only a few inches. Wandering within Bore Temple, the ancient temple is solemn, the halls are exquisite, the statues are marvelous, and the flowers and plants are lush — the charm within lingers long in memory.

projects.name: 西林寺
projects.address: 内江市东兴区西林街道东桐路
projects.content_zh: 位于内江市东兴区沱江岸边的西林寺居高临下，于夏日里上西林寺，川中酷暑灼人眼眸，走上宝寺山门已是大汗淋漓。门外香火缭绕，信善善人多不畏酷暑，纷至沓来。古西林寺四个大字端庄古朴，笔力遒劲，山门上雕刻精美，盘龙卧龙，蜿蜒啸天，门额上的两头石狮子张开血盆大口相迎，颇为骇人。而门前的劲柏苍翠，则体现了人工与自然的和谐共存，相得益彰。寺内金壁宏宇肃穆庄严，殿外石刻绝美，所篆《般若波罗蜜多心经》，笔力苍劲，手法娴熟。巨型香火上的一点即发字样又让人忍俊不禁，不过这充分表达了人们追求财富的美好愿望，殊不可晒。西林寺始建于南宋咸淳五年(1269年)，明代增修，嘉庆三年(1798年)重修。寺庙坐西向东，占地面积2218平方米，多重合院布局，有弥勒殿、大雄宝殿、观音殿、左右厢房等建筑。寺庙中最重要的是观音殿、文昌殿和大雄殿三殿。最大的观音殿面阔五间18.29米，进深五间12.9米，高10.4米，重檐歇山顶，穿斗式梁架。1976年以后，内江市人民政府在山上新添花圃，培植树木，维修庙宇，开辟公园，令西林胜景焕然一新，现为市文物保护单位。寺内有明代石坊一座，单门两柱。寺前有明代照壁一幅，正面刻有紫霞境三字，侧面刻有万历壬午年夏古字样，说明其建造年代。寺庙背山面水，景色清幽。唐代大诗人李白的著名诗句青山横北郭，白水绕东城，据说就是描写的这里，足见西林寺的绝妙景致与丰富人文历史。
projects.content_en: Xilin Temple, located on the bank of the Tuo River in Dongxing District, Neijiang City, commands a view from above. Visiting Xilin Temple in summer, the scorching heat of central Sichuan burns the eyes; by the time one climbs to the temple gate, one is already drenched in sweat. Incense smoke curls outside the gate; devout believers, undaunted by the heat, come in droves. The four large characters "Ancient Xilin Temple" are dignified and simple, with vigorous brushwork. The mountain gate is exquisitely carved, with coiling dragons winding and roaring to the sky; the two stone lions on the gate lintel open their blood-red mouths to welcome visitors, quite frightening. Meanwhile, the sturdy cypresses in front of the gate are verdant, embodying the harmonious coexistence of human craft and nature, complementing each other. Inside the temple, the golden halls are majestic and solemn; the stone carvings outside the halls are exquisite, with the engraved "Prajnaparamita Heart Sutra" showing vigorous brushwork and skilled technique. The words "ignite at a touch" on the giant incense sticks are amusing, but this fully expresses people's good wishes for pursuing wealth — not to be ridiculed. Xilin Temple was founded in the 5th year of Xianchun (1269), Southern Song, expanded in Ming, and rebuilt in the 3rd year of Jiaqing (1798). The temple faces east from west, covering 2,218 sq m, with a multi-courtyard layout, including Maitreya Hall, Mahavira Hall, Guanyin Hall, and left and right wing rooms. The most important buildings in the temple are the Guanyin Hall, Wenchang Hall, and Mahavira Hall. The largest Guanyin Hall is 5 bays wide (18.29m), 5 bays deep (12.9m), 10.4m tall, with double-eave xieshan roof and chuan-dou frame. After 1976, the Neijiang Municipal People's Government added flower beds on the mountain, cultivated trees, repaired the temple, and opened a park, giving Xilin's scenic beauty a completely new look. It is now a municipal cultural relic protection unit. Inside the temple there is a Ming dynasty stone archway with a single gate and two columns. In front of the temple there is a Ming dynasty screen wall, with the three characters "Zixia Realm" engraved on the front and "Summer of the Renwu year of Wanli" on the side, indicating its construction date. The temple backs onto mountains and faces water, with serene scenery. The famous poem by Tang dynasty poet Li Bai — "Green mountains span the northern wall, white water winds around the eastern city" — is said to describe this place, testifying to Xilin Temple's exquisite scenery and rich humanistic history.

projects.name: 高峰寺塔及石刻
projects.name_en: Pagoda of Gaofeng Temple and Stone Sculptures
projects.address: 内江市东兴区新江街道南720米
projects.content_zh: 高峰塔在内江市沱江左岸清流河与沱江交汇之处的狮子山上。寺庙最初始建于宋代，后殿房损毁，仅余八角九层楼阁式石塔，建于清嘉庆九年(1804年)。此塔坐东向西，高33.3米，塔基边长3.9米，往上塔身层层内收，并出短檐，各层均有开窗。塔身以石块砌筑，极为厚重有力，八角之上有仿圆柱造型，更加增进了石塔挺拔之感。塔内有八角形塔心柱，可沿蹬道盘旋而上到达第五层。在其上可一瞰沱江与内江市井，景致极为壮阔。1992年9月11日，塔尖遭雷击破坏，但塔身完好无损，后经2007年再度维修，恢复原貌。登高见塔，并无想象中般精致，反是一股质朴的沧桑与厚重感引人入胜，孔子云：登泰山则小天下。今见此塔，个中情怀，不外如是。
projects.content_en: Gaofeng Pagoda is on Lion Mountain at the confluence of the Qingliu River and Tuo River on the left bank of the Tuo River in Neijiang City. The temple was originally founded in Song dynasty; later the halls were destroyed, leaving only an octagonal nine-story pavilion-style stone pagoda, built in the 9th year of Jiaqing (1804), Qing. This pagoda faces west from east, 33.3m tall, with a pagoda base 3.9m per side; the pagoda body tapers inward layer by layer upward, with short eaves projecting out, and each story has windows. The pagoda body is built of stone blocks, extremely solid and powerful; above the octagons are imitation cylindrical shapes, further enhancing the pagoda's upright feeling. Inside the pagoda is an octagonal central pillar; one can spiral up the stairway to reach the fifth story. From above, one can take in a panoramic view of the Tuo River and the streets of Neijiang — the scenery is extremely magnificent. On September 11, 1992, the pagoda spire was damaged by lightning, but the pagoda body remained intact; after further repairs in 2007, its original appearance was restored. Climbing high to see the pagoda, it is not as exquisite as imagined, but rather a sense of质朴 vicissitudes and solidity is fascinating. Confucius said: "Climbing Mount Tai makes the world seem small." Seeing this pagoda today, the feelings within are no different.

projects.name: 威远古城墙
projects.address: 内江市威远县严陵镇东北400米
projects.content_zh: 威远城墙始建于明正德七年(1512年)。此后历经各朝数次损毁、改建等，最后重建于清乾隆三十五年(1770年)并保存至今。据称，原城墙全长约1700米，总高6米，城墙上通道宽3.3米，按东南西北方向各设大门。近年来，县政府曾数次斥资加固、维修，现存东门、北门及部分城墙，总长532米，高约4米，均用长1.1米、宽0.3米、厚0.25米条石砌成，极为雄壮古朴。城墙保留最完整的是北门地段，2002—2004年修复由北向东城墙200米，并重建北门城楼北拱宸，为重檐歇山二层楼阁。北门横跨重要道路，人流如织、摊点密布，场面如赶场。而所有摊点最让人记忆犹新的是花摊了，姹紫嫣红的花儿怒放在古老的城墙下，场面充溢着历史的厚重感与现实的勃勃生机，传承千年的古城墙在这一刻又重放异彩，焕发出不一样的年轻与朝气。公园段的城墙更为高大，几株大树从城墙里长出，发达有力的根须紧紧抓握着墙壁，如城墙一样阐述着风雨不变的坚强。墙下有安静读书的老先生，有悠闲休憩的老人，有甜蜜私语的恋人。历史与现代在这里交融，安静与喧嚣在这里和谐共存，这就是威远古城墙。美丽而顽强的威远古城墙，她用古老述说着历史，她用坚韧表达着年轻。
projects.content_en: Weiyuan City Wall was first built in the 7th year of Zhengde (1512), Ming dynasty. Thereafter it经历 several instances of damage and reconstruction by various dynasties, and was finally rebuilt in the 35th year of Qianlong (1770), Qing, and preserved to this day. It is said the original city wall was about 1,700m long, 6m total height, with a 3.3m wide passage on top, and gates set in each of the southeast, northwest directions. In recent years, the county government has invested several times to reinforce and repair it; currently the East Gate, North Gate, and parts of the wall survive, totaling 532m in length, about 4m high, all built of dressed stones 1.1m long, 0.3m wide, and 0.25m thick — extremely majestic and simple. The best-preserved section of the wall is the North Gate area; from 2002 to 2004, 200m of wall from north to east was repaired, and the North Gate tower "Beigongchen" was rebuilt as a two-story pavilion with double-eave xieshan roof. The North Gate spans an important road, with streams of people and dense stalls — the scene is like a market day. And among all the stalls, the most memorable is the flower stall: colorful flowers bloom in full glory beneath the ancient city wall; the scene is filled with the weight of history and the vibrant vitality of reality; the thousand-year-old city wall shines again at this moment, radiating a different kind of youth and vigor. The park section of the wall is even taller; several large trees grow out from within the wall, their developed and powerful roots tightly gripping the wall, like the wall itself expounding the unchanging strength through wind and rain. Beneath the wall are old gentlemen reading quietly, elderly people resting leisurely, and lovers whispering sweetly. History and modernity blend here, quiet and noise coexist harmoniously here — this is the Ancient City Wall of Weiyuan. Beautiful and tenacious Ancient City Wall of Weiyuan, she recounts history with antiquity, and expresses youth with resilience.

projects.name: 隆昌石牌坊
projects.address: 内江市隆昌县金鹅镇、响石镇、石燕镇、渔箭镇
projects.content_zh: 隆昌石牌坊位于中国四川省隆昌县境内，现存石牌坊17座，其中13座一字排列在贯穿金鹅镇的长约600米的道路之上，蔚为壮观，是我国现存最密集的牌坊群落之一。从北到南依次排列的是郭陈氏节孝坊、禹王宫山门坊(锄莠安良碑)、牛树梅德政坊、孝子总坊；刘光第德政坊、肃庆德政坊、郭玉峦功德坊、舒承湜百岁坊、节孝总坊(除暴安良碑，政通人和碑)、李吉寿德政坊、觉罗国欢德政坊、郭王氏功德坊。另有四座单独的牌坊分别位于响石镇、石燕镇、渔箭镇。隆昌牌坊数量众多，类型丰富，其中计有德政坊5座，节孝坊4座，功德坊2座，贞节坊、孝子坊、百寿坊、山门坊、镇山坊、嵌瓷玩赏坊各1座。这些牌坊均为四柱三间，平面面阔约9米，高约11米。牌坊均以青石建造，仿木结构而不施粉饰。其中建造时间最早的石燕镇山坊建于明弘治九年(1496年)，最晚的是建于光绪年间的嵌瓷赏花牌坊。隆昌牌坊虽然以集群为特色，但每个单独的牌坊也值得关注，它们形态古朴，材质醇厚，保留有很好的文字雕刻与各式花草动物雕刻，惟妙惟肖，引人入胜。保存如此完好，形态如此统一，排列如此密集的牌坊群落世间罕有，也成为隆昌历史与文化传统的永久记载。隆昌石牌坊造型精美，牌坊上所雕花鸟虫鱼、龙风祥云，尽是神韵充溢，叫人赞叹。至于书法字种，无不遒劲有力，或端庄、或俊逸，或中正平和、种种风格，都成其艺术精品之谓。2001年6月25日，隆昌石牌坊被国务院批准列入第五批全国重点文物保护单位名单。
projects.content_en: Longchang Stone Memorial Archways are located within Longchang County, Sichuan Province, China. Currently 17 stone archways survive, 13 of which are arranged in a single line along a road about 600m long running through Jin'e Town — a spectacular sight, one of the densest surviving archway groups in China. Arranged from north to south are: Guo Chen's Chastity-Filial Piety Archway, Yu Palace Mountain Gate Archway (Eliminating Evil and Securing Good Stele), Niu Shumei's Virtuous Governance Archway, General Filial Son Archway; Liu Guangdi's Virtuous Governance Archway, Su Qing's Virtuous Governance Archway, Guo Yuluan's Merit Archway, Shu Chengshi's Centenarian Archway, General Chastity-Filial Piety Archway (Eliminating Evil and Securing Good Stele, Smooth Governance and Harmonious People Stele), Li Jishou's Virtuous Governance Archway, Jueluo Guohuan's Virtuous Governance Archway, and Guo Wang's Merit Archway. Another four separate archways are located in Xiangshi Town, Shiyan Town, and Yujian Town respectively. Longchang archways are numerous in quantity and rich in type: among them are 5 Virtuous Governance archways, 4 Chastity-Filial Piety archways, 2 Merit archways, and 1 each of Chastity archway, Filial Son archway, Centenarian archway, Mountain Gate archway, Town Mountain archway, and Inlaid Porcelain ornamental archway. These archways all have four columns and three bays, with a planar width of about 9m and height of about 11m. The archways are all built of bluestone, imitating timber structure without plaster decoration. Among them, the earliest built is the Shiyan Town Mountain archway, built in the 9th year of Hongzhi (1496), Ming; the latest is the Inlaid Porcelain Flower-Viewing archway, built during the Guangxu era. Although Longchang archways are characterized by their clustering, each individual archway also deserves attention: they are simple in form, rich in material, and preserve excellent text carvings as well as various flower, plant, and animal carvings — lifelike and fascinating. Archway groups so well-preserved, so uniform in form, and so densely arranged are rare in the world, and have become a permanent record of Longchang's history and cultural traditions. Longchang Stone Memorial Archways are exquisitely shaped; the flowers, birds, insects, fish, dragons, phoenixes, and auspicious clouds carved on the archways are all full of spirit, awe-inspiring. As for the calligraphy styles, all are vigorous and powerful — some dignified, some elegant, some balanced and harmonious — each style becoming an artistic masterpiece. On June 25, 2001, Longchang Stone Memorial Archways were approved by the State Council to be included in the 5th batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units.

projects.name: 南溪城墙
projects.address: 宜宾市南溪区南溪镇南长江畔
projects.content_zh: 到过万里长江第一城宜宾的人，如果你不到闻名遐迩的南溪城墙参观一番，那么即便你游遍宜宾也枉然了。南溪县距宜宾市40多公里，唐乾符二年(875年)建土城墙，明天顺年间(1457—1464年)改建为石墙，清乾隆二十九年(1764年)整修，加高城墙，增建城门2座。现存有城墙1480米和文明门等城楼3座。南溪城墙高约4~8米，整体以大块石块砌筑，浑厚坚固，端庄古朴，大气磅礴。文明门高大雄伟，门洞上文明门三字为清嘉庆十一年(1807年)知县邵兆禄所书，笔势雄劲。墙上城楼为木结构，面阔三间10.9米，进深三间7.5米，通高二层17.35米，重檐歇山顶，抬梁式梁架，出檐飞跳，脊上塑二龙戏珠等丰富饰物。除了文明门，现存望瀛门和广福门，尺度稍小，但也都保存完好，各具气象。南溪城墙背靠闹市，俯瞰长江，巨石与木构相得益彰，伴随着江水流淌，城墙也见证着这片土地的风雨沧桑。
projects.content_en: For anyone who has visited Yibin, the "First City on the Ten-Thousand-Li Yangtze River," if you do not visit the renowned Nanxi City Wall, then even if you tour all of Yibin it would be in vain. Nanxi County is over 40km from Yibin City. In the 2nd year of Qianfu (875), Tang dynasty, an earthen city wall was built; during the Ming Tianshun era (1457-1464), it was converted to a stone wall; in the 29th year of Qianlong (1764), Qing dynasty, it was renovated, the wall was heightened, and 2 additional city gates were built. Currently 1,480m of wall and 3 gate towers including Wenming Gate survive. Nanxi City Wall is about 4-8m high, entirely built of large stone blocks — solid and sturdy, dignified and simple, grand and majestic. Wenming Gate is tall and majestic; the three characters "Wenming Gate" above the gateway were written by County Magistrate Shao Zhaolu in the 11th year of Jiaqing (1807), with vigorous brushwork. The gate tower on the wall is timber structure, 3 bays wide (10.9m), 3 bays deep (7.5m), two stories total (17.35m), with double-eave xieshan roof and post-and-lintel frame, with projecting flying eaves and rich ornaments such as two dragons playing with a pearl on the ridge. Besides Wenming Gate, the surviving Wangying Gate and Guangfu Gate are slightly smaller in scale but also well preserved, each with its own character. Nanxi City Wall backs onto the bustling city and overlooks the Yangtze River; the giant stones and timber structures complement each other, and as the river flows, the wall also witnesses the vicissitudes of this land.

projects.name: 南溪镇南塔
projects.address: 宜宾市南溪区江南镇红林村
projects.content_zh: 南溪镇南塔位于江南镇红林村山顶，俗称老塔，民国《南溪县志》载：镇南塔，在县城对岸镇南山顶，挺秀如笔，其高插天。建筑年代无考，相传始于元明间。该塔为砖石结构，密檐式八角七层攒尖顶，通高24米，设螺旋式蹬道，塔壁均设佛龛，塔刹原为穹隆顶，1986年维修时改为攒尖顶。该塔古朴粗犷，颇有元、明风韵。位于该镇新塔村的映南塔俗称新塔，与镇南塔，相映成趣，双塔互映遂成南溪胜景。江南镇与南溪县城隔江相望，长江之水在此开阔浩荡，气势滔天。以前并无大桥相通，从县城到江南镇须乘船渡江，现因建宜宾至泸州高速，在开阔长江上修建了南溪大桥。为方便民众，特在高速大桥一侧辟有一米多宽的人行道，从此可渡长江。南溪镇南塔与南溪县城隔江相望，城内看去，镇南塔雄峙高山之上，极为雄壮。到达塔前，该塔正在维修，周围围满了钢筋梁架，镇南塔的英姿犹能分辨一二。其所筑有长条石重达数吨，而该塔处于山上，要把大石运上山顶，古人之意志与耐力，由此可见一斑。只叹所至非时，不然其英姿古迹，当一览无余。
projects.content_en: Zhennan Pagoda of Nanxi is located on the hilltop of Honglin Village, Jiangnan Town, commonly called the Old Pagoda. The Republican-era "Nanxi County Annals" record: "Zhennan Pagoda, on the summit of Zhennan Mountain opposite the county town, stands gracefully like a brush, its height piercing the sky." The construction date is unknown; legend says it began in the Yuan-Ming period. This pagoda is a brick-stone structure, a multi-eaved octagonal seven-story pyramidal-roof pagoda, 24m tall overall, with a spiral stairway, Buddhist niches set into the pagoda walls, and the finial originally a dome, changed to a pyramidal roof during repairs in 1986. The pagoda is simple and rugged, quite in the Yuan-Ming style. Yingnan Pagoda, located in Xinta Village of this town and commonly called the New Pagoda, forms a delightful contrast with Zhennan Pagoda; the twin pagodas reflecting each other became a scenic spot of Nanxi. Jiangnan Town faces Nanxi County town across the river; the Yangtze River water here is broad and mighty, overwhelming in momentum. Previously there was no bridge connecting them; from the county town to Jiangnan Town one had to cross the river by boat. Now, due to the construction of the Yibin-Luzhou Expressway, the Nanxi Bridge was built across the broad Yangtze. For the convenience of the people, a sidewalk over a meter wide was specially opened on one side of the expressway bridge, allowing crossing of the Yangtze from then on. Zhennan Pagoda of Nanxi faces Nanxi County town across the river; viewed from inside the city, Zhennan Pagoda stands majestically on the high mountain, extremely imposing. Arriving before the pagoda, it was under repair, surrounded by steel reinforcement frames, but the heroic bearing of Zhennan Pagoda could still be discerned somewhat. The long stones used in its construction weigh several tons each, and since the pagoda is on a mountain, transporting the large stones to the hilltop — the will and endurance of the ancients can be seen from this. One can only sigh that the timing of the visit was not right; otherwise its heroic bearing and ancient relics would be fully visible.

projects.name: 旋螺殿
projects.address: 宜宾市李庄镇南2.5公里石牛山上
projects.content_zh: 旋螺殿位于宜宾市李庄镇南2.5公里石牛山上，因殿内曾供祀文昌帝君(世称梓潼帝君)，故又名文昌宫。此殿初建于明万历二十四年(1596年)，后曾多次维修，方成今日的状态。此殿坐北向南，占地面积508平方米，外观呈八角形，殿高12.5米，进深、面阔均约8.3米，从外看去为两层三重檐，内部实际上仅有两层。除了一层八角采用石柱支撑外，其余部分均为木结构，梁架采用抬梁支柱法，檐下遍施斗拱，但三重檐下又各有区别。入殿内可见顶部藻井天花，以复杂的斗拱交错堆叠而成，结构之精细，令人称奇。因整个藻井结构整体向右旋转，形如旋螺，故得名旋螺殿。旋螺殿造型优美，结构精妙，比例匀称端庄，风格独特，是我国木质殿阁建筑中的精品。20世纪40年代，著名古建筑学家梁思成、莫宗江对此殿考察后，曾在《中国营造学社》上撰文称该殿梁柱结构之优，颇足傲于当世之作。是为此殿重要建筑历史价值的明证。旋螺殿屹立于巨石山上，周遭别无人家喧嚣，自有一番遗世独立的孤高气质。而其四周是繁荫草木，鸟音虫鸣略闻一二，这样看来，它真是隐于世的闲云野鹤了。任众生熙熙攘攘，我自独守内心的那一份清明，这正是忙碌的现代人梦里求之而不得的生活态度啊。殿前不远有一小屋，室内是守殿的老奶奶，奶奶年事颇高，精神颇好，她说你们随便看，很好的，我就问好在哪里，她微微一笑：你看了就知道。然后我静心细看，完了坐在石凳上休息，这时凉风徐来，好不快意快活。我看看殿宇，再看看老奶奶，她安静地坐在凳子上打盹。不知道她在这儿守了多久但我感觉真真好，好在哪里呢？你看了就知道。
projects.content_en: Xuanluo Hall is located on Shiniu Mountain, 2.5km south of Lizhuang Town, Yibin City. Because the hall once enshrined the Emperor Wenchang (commonly called the Emperor Zitong), it is also named Wenchang Palace. This hall was first built in the 24th year of Wanli (1596), Ming dynasty, and later repaired multiple times, reaching its current state. The hall faces south, covering 508 sq m, with an octagonal exterior, 12.5m tall, and both depth and width about 8.3m. From outside it appears as two stories with triple eaves, but internally there are actually only two stories. Except for the first-story octagon supported by stone columns, the rest is all timber structure; the beam frame uses the post-and-lintel column method, with bracket sets applied throughout under the eaves, but with differences under each of the three eaves. Entering the hall, one can see the caisson ceiling at the top, formed by the intricate interleaving and stacking of complex bracket sets — the precision of the structure is amazing. Because the entire caisson structure rotates to the right as a whole, shaped like a spiral (xuanluo), it is named Xuanluo (Spiral) Hall. Xuanluo Hall has a beautiful form, exquisite structure, well-proportioned and dignified proportions, and a unique style — a masterpiece among China's timber hall-pavilion architecture. In the 1940s, after investigating this hall, famous ancient architecture scholars Liang Sicheng and Mo Zongjiang wrote in the "China Society for Research in Chinese Architecture" that the excellence of this hall's beam-column structure is sufficient to stand proudly among contemporary works. This is clear evidence of the hall's important architectural and historical value. Xuanluo Hall stands on Giant Stone Mountain, with no noise from other households around it, naturally possessing a detached and lofty气质. And all around it are lush shaded plants and trees, with the sounds of birds and insects faintly heard — in this light, it truly is a recluse hidden from the world. Let the multitudes bustle; I alone guard the clarity within my heart — this is precisely the life attitude that busy modern people seek in dreams but cannot obtain. Not far in front of the hall is a small cottage; inside is the grandmother who guards the hall. The grandmother is quite advanced in age but in good spirits. She said, "Look around as you please, it's very good." I asked what was good about it; she smiled slightly and said, "You'll know when you see it." Then I looked carefully with a calm mind, and after finishing sat on a stone bench to rest; at this moment a cool breeze came slowly — extremely pleasant and joyful. I looked at the hall, then at the grandmother, who sat quietly on the bench dozing. I don't know how long she has guarded this place, but I feel it is truly good; where is it good? You'll know when you see it.

projects.name: 东山白塔
projects.address: 宜宾市翠屏区白沙湾街道东山村
projects.content_zh: 东山白塔，古称东雁塔，建成于明隆庆三年(1569年)，为八角八层楼阁式砖石塔，顶部八角攒尖。塔身通高35.8米，矗立在边长4.45米的弥座式塔基之上，往上逐层缩进，以砖砌密檐挑出，每层均设有开窗。可顺塔内蹬道盘旋攀登至塔顶，此处有平台约六七平方米，可供人站立鸟瞰宜宾城及远近山水。有清代诗人杨端所留诗句为证：欲登白塔穷秋望，且泛扁舟荡日斜。沿着山路上去，迎面是巨大的山门，上书东山寺三字，山门右后方可见掩映在苍翠林木间的白塔。沿山门直上数十步，即是东山寺天王殿，再后方是大雄宝殿，东山寺建筑不多但雄伟异常。山回路转，行到山穷处，就是东山白塔了，白塔处中山顶处，巍然矗立，俯瞰河山，有帝王之姿。
projects.content_en: Dongshan White Pagoda, anciently called Dongyan Pagoda, was completed in the 3rd year of Longqing (1569), Ming dynasty. It is an octagonal eight-story pavilion-style brick-stone pagoda with an octagonal pyramidal top. The pagoda body is 35.8m tall overall, standing on a lotus-seat-style pagoda base 4.45m per side, tapering inward layer by layer upward, with brick-built dense eaves projecting out, and each story has windows. One can spiral up the stairway inside the pagoda to the top; here there is a platform of about 6-7 sq m, allowing people to stand and get a bird's-eye view of Yibin City and the surrounding mountains and rivers near and far. There is evidence in a poem left by Qing dynasty poet Yang Duan: "Desiring to climb the White Pagoda to exhaust the autumn view, I shall row a small boat as the sun slants." Going up the mountain path, facing you is a huge mountain gate inscribed with the three characters "Dongshan Temple"; to the right rear of the gate, the White Pagoda can be seen half-hidden among verdant trees. Going straight up dozens of steps from the mountain gate is the Dongshan Temple Heavenly Kings Hall, and further behind is the Mahavira Hall; Dongshan Temple has few buildings but they are exceptionally majestic. As the mountain path winds and turns, arriving at the end of the mountain, there is Dongshan White Pagoda. The White Pagoda stands at the mountain summit, towering majestically, overlooking rivers and mountains, with the bearing of an emperor.

projects.name: 真武山古建筑群
projects.name_en: Ancient Building Complex at Zhenwu Mountain
projects.address: 宜宾市城北500米真武山
projects.highlights: 道家文化、山势、院落、石坊
projects.content_zh: 真武山古建筑群是一组以道教宫观为主体，同时融合了释、儒、道三教文化特征的建筑物，位于宜宾市北郊的真武山上。建于明万历年间(1573—1620年)，清代曾多次维修。庙群占地面积约3.3万平方米，建筑面积约4000平方米。庙宇以明代建筑为主，现存望江楼、斗姆宫、三府宫、祖师殿、玄祖殿，石牌坊为明代建筑；无量殿、三府宫、斗姆宫后殿及厢房、文昌宫、地姆宫、牌坊为清代建筑。驱车行闹市中，忽见古山门真武山，不由停车驻足，顺石梯而上，始觉山门之古朴宏伟。沿着蜿蜒向上的石梯再行数百步，便到了望江楼，始建于明代，为二层楼阁。面阔三间14.8米，进深三间11.4米，通高11.8米，重檐歇山顶，抬梁式梁架，檐下施如意斗拱。门前双石狮惟妙惟肖，壮硕威严。望江楼，顾名思义，在此楼上举目远眺，繁华的宜宾城、浩荡奔腾的岷江一览无余。其居高临下之势犹胜岳阳楼，若骚人迁客于此，少不得又是几多人生感怀。绕望江楼向后再行数百步，可见明代建筑祖师殿和玄祖殿。祖师殿面阔三间8.67米，进深二间7.6米，通高7.8米，重檐歇山顶，抬梁式梁架，檐下施斗拱。玄祖殿面阔三间12.15米，进深二间11.75米，通高8.9米，重檐歇山顶，抬梁式梁架，檐下施斗拱。二殿庄严肃穆，香火鼎盛。踏着青石板继续前行，可看到一大门牌坊，上书斗姆宫三个大字。斗姆宫由前殿、中殿和后殿构成。前殿建于明万历四十六年(1618年)，面阔三间11.7米，进深三间10.8米，通高8.2米，重檐歇山顶，抬梁式梁架，檐下施斗拱。中殿与后殿为清代建筑，中殿面阔三间11.6米，进深三间10米，通高8米，硬山顶，穿斗式梁架。后殿面阔三间11.5米，进深三间9.8米，通高8米，硬山顶，穿斗式梁架。中殿前有明万历石牌坊1座，四柱三间，高4.5米，宽6.2米。左右次间额枋间分别刻万天帝主。而最让人难忘的是斗姆宫前石墙上刻的返璞归真四个赤字，笔力遒劲而洒脱，端庄而随性，观此可见道家恣意洒脱、追求自然的思想。周围绿树掩映间朱墙碧瓦更显一番安谧静美的姿态，游人驻足于此，宛若流连世外，殊忘物我。辗转良久，行至三府宫，三府宫建于清道光年间(1821—1850年)。为二进四合院。前殿面阔五间22.2米，进深四间18.6米，通高10.8米，歇山顶，穿斗式梁架。后殿面阔五间22.1米，进深四间10.45米，通高8.5米，硬山顶，穿斗式梁架。飞檐赤壁，庄严肃穆。及见玉皇殿，想天上琼楼玉宇应如是，凌霄殿辉煌宏伟，不外如是。玉皇大帝端坐其间，纵览三界万事万物，自有一般帝王气象。文昌宫前香火鼎盛。三重大殿均为硬山顶，穿斗式梁架。前殿面阔五间24米，进深五间19米，通高9米。中殿面阔三间15.4米，进深七间13.8米，通高8.75米。后殿面阔三间15.2米，进深三间约14.2米，通高8.3米。外有壁画，仙人仙气，仙山仙鹤，栩栩如生。真武山古建筑群宏大而精美，各建筑依山而建，顺势而为，庭院深深，林壑幽幽，山光鸟语引人情思，实是人间盛景。
projects.content_en: The Ancient Building Complex at Zhenwu Mountain is a group of buildings with Daoist palaces and temples as the main body, while also integrating the cultural characteristics of Buddhism, Confucianism, and Daoism. It is located on Zhenwu Mountain in the northern suburbs of Yibin City. Built during the Ming Wanli era (1573-1620), it was repaired multiple times in Qing dynasty. The temple complex covers about 33,000 sq m, with a building area of about 4,000 sq m. The temples are mainly Ming dynasty buildings; currently surviving are Wangjiang Tower, Doumu Palace, Sanfu Palace, Zushi Hall, Xuanzu Hall, and a stone archway — Ming dynasty buildings; Wuliang Hall, Sanfu Palace, the rear hall and wing rooms of Doumu Palace, Wenchang Palace, Dimu Palace, and archways are Qing dynasty buildings. Driving through the bustling city, suddenly seeing the ancient mountain gate "Zhenwu Mountain," one cannot help but stop the car and pause. Going up the stone steps, one begins to feel the simplicity and grandeur of the mountain gate. Walking another few hundred steps along the winding upward stone steps, one reaches Wangjiang Tower, founded in Ming dynasty, a two-story pavilion. 3 bays wide (14.8m), 3 bays deep (11.4m), 11.8m total height, with double-eave xieshan roof, post-and-lintel frame, and ruyi bracket sets under the eaves. The pair of stone lions in front of the gate are lifelike, sturdy and majestic. Wangjiang Tower, as the name suggests, from this tower looking into the distance, the bustling Yibin City and the mighty, surging Min River are all visible. Its commanding position surpasses even Yueyang Tower; if poets and exiled officials were here, there would inevitably be many reflections on life. Walking several hundred steps further back around Wangjiang Tower, one can see the Ming dynasty buildings Zushi Hall and Xuanzu Hall. Zushi Hall is 3 bays wide (8.67m), 2 bays deep (7.6m), 7.8m total height, with double-eave xieshan roof, post-and-lintel frame, and bracket sets under the eaves. Xuanzu Hall is 3 bays wide (12.15m), 2 bays deep (11.75m), 8.9m total height, with double-eave xieshan roof, post-and-lintel frame, and bracket sets under the eaves. The two halls are solemn and majestic, with flourishing incense. Stepping on bluestone slabs and continuing forward, one can see a large gate archway inscribed with the three large characters "Doumu Palace." Doumu Palace consists of a front hall, middle hall, and rear hall. The front hall was built in the 46th year of Wanli (1618), Ming; 3 bays wide (11.7m), 3 bays deep (10.8m), 8.2m total height, with double-eave xieshan roof, post-and-lintel frame, and bracket sets under the eaves. The middle and rear halls are Qing dynasty buildings; the middle hall is 3 bays wide (11.6m), 3 bays deep (10m), 8m total height, with flush gable roof and chuan-dou frame. The rear hall is 3 bays wide (11.5m), 3 bays deep (9.8m), 8m total height, with flush gable roof and chuan-dou frame. In front of the middle hall is a Ming Wanli stone archway, four columns and three bays, 4.5m high, 6.2m wide. Between the architraves of the left and right side bays are engraved "Heavenly Emperor Lord" respectively. And the most unforgettable is the four red characters "Fan Pu Gui Zhen" (Return to Simplicity and Truth) carved on the stone wall in front of Doumu Palace — the brushwork is vigorous and free, dignified and spontaneous; viewing this, one can see the Daoist thought of unrestrained freedom and pursuit of nature. Surrounded by green trees, the red walls and green tiles show an even more tranquil and beautiful posture; visitors stopping here feel as if lingering beyond the world, forgetting self and surroundings. After wandering for a long time, arriving at Sanfu Palace, Sanfu Palace was built during the Qing Daoguang era (1821-1850). It is a two-courtyard siheyuan. The front hall is 5 bays wide (22.2m), 4 bays deep (18.6m), 10.8m total height, with xieshan roof and chuan-dou frame. The rear hall is 5 bays wide (22.1m), 4 bays deep (10.45m), 8.5m total height, with flush gable roof and chuan-dou frame. With flying eaves and red walls, it is solemn and majestic. Upon seeing the Jade Emperor Hall, one thinks that the heavenly jade towers and marble palaces should be like this; the Lingxiao Palace's brilliance and grandeur is no more than this. The Jade Emperor sits upright among them, surveying all things in the three realms, naturally with an imperial aura. In front of Wenchang Palace, incense flourishes. The three major halls all have flush gable roofs and chuan-dou frames. The front hall is 5 bays wide (24m), 5 bays deep (19m), 9m total height. The middle hall is 3 bays wide (15.4m), 7 bays deep (13.8m), 8.75m total height. The rear hall is 3 bays wide (15.2m), 3 bays deep (about 14.2m), 8.3m total height. Outside there are murals of immortals and immortal aura, immortal mountains and immortal cranes — lifelike. The Ancient Building Complex at Zhenwu Mountain is grand and exquisite; each building is built according to the mountain, following the terrain, with deep courtyards, serene valleys and forests, mountain light and bird songs evoking emotion — truly a scenic wonder on earth.

projects.name: 宜宾大观楼
projects.address: 宜宾市翠屏区西街与商业街交汇口
projects.content_zh: 大观楼，位于宜宾市中区西街口，始建于明嘉靖年间(1522—1566年)，初名谯楼。明末毁于兵火，清乾隆三十年(1765年)部分重修。相传此楼为震楼楼下阴传河恶龙所修，现为三重檐歇山顶城楼式建筑。底部为高5.5米的石砌台基，南北宽25.5米，东西22米。台基四面开有洞口，形成十字通道，西侧设石梯登楼。上部楼阁为木结构，底层面阔七间23.5米，进深五间16.15米，楼高三层共22.5米，因在高台之上，加之体量硕大，更是显得极为雄伟。三重屋檐角部均高高翘起，挺拔有力，檐下施如意斗拱，装饰华丽。三楼东面檐下悬大观楼匾额，为清代书法家冀宣明所书。大观楼雄踞闹市，气势巍峨，因此在当地有小天安门之称，足见民众对其尊重和喜爱。作为宜宾市区标志性建筑，近年来得到广发修缮，城楼焕然一新。沿石梯上得楼去，室内是宜宾历史文化展览，详细介绍了宜宾的历史人文风情，精美华丽的少数民族服饰、屹立天地的白塔、黑塔等都可在此观瞻瞭望。
projects.content_en: Daguan Gate Tower is located at the intersection of West Street and Commercial Street in the central area of Yibin City. It was first built during the Ming Jiajing era (1522-1566), initially named Qiaolou (Watchtower). It was destroyed by war fire at the end of Ming, and partially rebuilt in the 30th year of Qianlong (1765), Qing. According to legend, this tower was built to subdue an evil dragon in the underground river beneath the tower. It is now a city-gate-tower-style building with a triple-eave xieshan roof. The base is a stone-masonry platform 5.5m high, 25.5m wide north-south, 22m east-west. The platform has openings on all four sides, forming a cross passage; on the west side, stone steps lead up to the tower. The upper pavilion is timber structure; the ground floor is 7 bays wide (23.5m), 5 bays deep (16.15m), and the tower is three stories totaling 22.5m high. Because it sits on a high platform and has a massive volume, it appears extremely majestic. The corners of the three layers of eaves all soar high, upright and powerful; under the eaves are ruyi bracket sets with ornate decoration. Under the east eave of the third floor hangs the "Daguan Tower" plaque, written by Qing dynasty calligrapher Ji Xuanming. Daguan Tower dominates the bustling city with towering momentum, hence it is locally called the "Little Tiananmen," sufficient to show the people's respect and affection for it. As a landmark building in downtown Yibin, it has received extensive repairs in recent years, and the tower has taken on a completely new look. Climbing up the stone steps to the tower, the interior is the Yibin History and Culture Exhibition, detailing Yibin's history, humanities, and customs; exquisite and gorgeous ethnic minority costumes, and the White and Black Pagodas standing between heaven and earth can all be viewed and observed from here.

projects.name: 七星山黑塔
projects.address: 宜宾市南广镇七星村北700米
projects.type: 宗教建筑 砖石结构
projects.content_zh: 七星山黑塔，为宜宾东山白塔的兄弟塔，位于宜宾市南广镇七星村北。此塔建于明隆庆年间(1567—1572年)，后经多次维修，因外表近黑色，故名黑塔。此塔为砖石砌筑，八角七层，坐东向西，通高30.7米。底部为八角须弥坐式塔基，高1.7米，边长4.4米。往上塔身逐层内收，每层设龛，并有窗洞开启。塔内有实心柱，浮雕二龙戏珠及斗拱，有蹬道可盘旋攀登至顶，顶部为宝珠塔刹。黑塔距市区10公里。打摩的时，司机说路不好，还不以为意，一路却是颠簸流离。远观黑塔傲然屹立在山顶上，便沿着小路寻去，距塔越近，却是失去了塔的踪影，只因林木遮蔽了双眼。这正是一叶障目不见泰山，抑或是不识庐山真面目，只缘身在此山中。幸见一老奶奶，近前一问，原来就在前方数百米处。到得塔前，芳草萋萋，野径无人，想是许久没人到此地了。而由黑塔观宜宾胜景，则山河不过方寸之间耳。也许黑塔更像一位超脱世外的智者，俯视着渺小的众生，孤傲地顶天立地，不愿与纷扰污浊的世俗再有干系。
projects.content_en: The Black Tower at Qixing Mountain is the brother tower of Dongshan White Pagoda in Yibin, located north of Qixing Village, Nanguang Town, Yibin City. This pagoda was built during the Ming Longqing era (1567-1572), and later repaired multiple times. Because its exterior is nearly black, it is named the Black Tower. This pagoda is built of brick and stone, octagonal with seven stories, facing west from east, 30.7m tall overall. The base is an octagonal xumi (Sumeru) seat-style pagoda base, 1.7m high, 4.4m per side. The pagoda body tapers inward layer by layer upward, with niches set on each story and window openings. Inside the pagoda is a solid column with relief carvings of two dragons playing with a pearl and bracket sets; there is a stairway that can spiral up to the top, and the top is a jewel finial. The Black Tower is 10km from the city center. When taking a motorized rickshaw, the driver said the road was bad; I didn't think much of it, but the journey was bumpy and rough all the way. Viewing the Black Tower from afar standing proudly on the hilltop, I followed a small path to search for it; the closer I got to the tower, the more I lost sight of it, simply because the trees and forest obscured my eyes. This is precisely "a leaf before the eye blocks the view of Mount Tai," or perhaps "not knowing the true face of Mount Lu, only because one is within this mountain." Fortunately I saw an old grandmother; approaching to ask, it turned out to be just a few hundred meters ahead. Arriving before the tower, fragrant grass was lush, the wild path was deserted — it seemed no one had come to this place for a long time. And viewing Yibin's scenic beauty from the Black Tower, mountains and rivers are but a few inches apart. Perhaps the Black Tower is more like a wise man detached from the world, looking down upon the insignificant multitudes, proudly standing between heaven and earth, unwilling to have any further relation with the troubled and filthy secular world.

projects.name: 旧州塔
projects.address: 宜宾市翠屏区安阜街道岷江西路200米
projects.content_zh: 旧州塔耸立在浩荡奔腾的岷江河岸，与宜宾东山白塔、七星山黑塔并称为宜宾三塔。此塔始建于北宋崇宁元年至大观三年(1102—1109年)，明代以后多次维修。旧州塔是方形十三级密檐式砖塔，造型非常古朴。塔高29.5米，底部南北长7.35米，东西宽7.4米。底层较高，墙面平直，自第二层起，塔身逐层向内收缩，到第十三层收分成两重梯形平台。塔内共有五层，每一层都有心室，所供佛像已损毁，但壁画尚有留存。室顶是藻井天花，四角均有斗拱。塔壁铭文刻有大观四年中元日设水陆大会斋等字样。据当地人讲，传说曾经塔的顶上有一颗耀眼的宝石，夜晚时便能看到宝石发出的美丽光芒，但今天并无宝石，据称那宝石是随清江而消失的，不知其真是假。但可观渔舟唱晚时分的古塔斜阳，浩浩江水，脉脉斜阳，悠悠古城，且看那白塔英姿，如年轻挺拔的壮小伙心系远方，更如历经沧桑的智者含笑不语。游人观之，莫不有酾酒临江，横槊赋诗的情怀志气。
projects.content_en: Jiuzhou Pagoda stands on the bank of the mighty, surging Min River, and together with Yibin's Dongshan White Pagoda and Qixing Mountain Black Tower is known as the Three Pagodas of Yibin. This pagoda was first built from the 1st year of Chongning to the 3rd year of Daguan (1102-1109), Northern Song, and repaired multiple times after Ming. Jiuzhou Pagoda is a square thirteen-level dense-eave brick pagoda, with a very simple and ancient form. The pagoda is 29.5m tall, with the base 7.35m long north-south and 7.4m wide east-west. The bottom story is relatively high with flat wall surfaces; from the second story onward, the pagoda body tapers inward layer by layer, and at the thirteenth story it narrows into a double trapezoidal platform. Inside the pagoda there are five stories, each with a central chamber; the enshrined Buddha statues have been damaged, but murals still remain. The chamber top is a caisson ceiling, with bracket sets at all four corners. Inscriptions on the pagoda wall are engraved with characters such as "On the Zhongyuan Day of the 4th year of Daguan, a Water-Land Great Assembly vegetarian feast was held." According to local people, legend says there was once a dazzling gem on top of the pagoda, and at night one could see the beautiful light emitted by the gem, but today there is no gem; it is said that the gem disappeared with the Qingjiang River — whether this is true or false is unknown. But one can view the ancient pagoda in the setting sun at the time of fishing boats singing in the evening: the vast river water, the gentle setting sun, the leisurely ancient city — and behold the heroic bearing of the White Pagoda, like a young and upright strong lad with his heart set on distant places, and even more like a wise man who has experienced vicissitudes, smiling without speaking. Visitors who view it all feel the sentiment and aspiration of pouring wine by the river and composing poetry with a spear across the lap.

projects.name: 万寿寺、万寿观
projects.name_en: Wanshou Temple and Wanshou Taoist Temple
projects.address: 宜宾市屏山县屏山镇东新街
projects.content_zh: 万寿寺与万寿观均于屏山县城东1公里，锦屏山前，金沙江后，相互毗邻。一为佛寺，一为道观，和谐并存。万寿寺始建于金大定时(1161—1189年)，明正德十年(1515年)扩建，改名万寿寺。另说始建于北宋熙宁二年(1069年)，其中真伪，尚待考证。现存建筑为明代修建，主要遗存为大雄宝殿与观音殿。大雄宝殿面阔三间12.5米，进深三间11.8米，通高12米，重檐歇山顶，抬梁式梁架，上下檐各施五铺作斗拱24朵，装饰华丽。观音殿面阔三间，进深三间12.2米，通高11.5米，重檐歇山顶，抬梁式梁架，外檐施斗拱28朵。殿中有铜镜1面，为明成化二年(1466年)铸。两殿内柱及梁架均有丰富雕刻与彩绘，图案精致，雕工精湛。万寿观始建年代不详，明成化弘治年间重建。原有宫殿五座：天师殿、天王殿、玄帝宫、通明殿，现仅存玄帝宫，明代建筑，面阔三间11.5米，进深三间11.5米，通高12米，重檐歇山顶，抬梁式梁架；上下檐均施斗拱。殿内椽柱巨大，柱径0.7米，上部斗拱梁檐做工精致，雕饰细腻，随色彩暗淡，仍能看出极高的工艺水准。
projects.content_en: Both Wanshou Temple and Wanshou Taoist Temple are located 1km east of Pingshan County town, in front of Jinping Mountain and behind the Jinsha River, adjacent to each other. One is a Buddhist temple and one is a Daoist temple, coexisting harmoniously. Wanshou Temple was founded during the Jin Dading era (1161-1189), expanded in the 10th year of Zhengde (1515), Ming, and renamed Wanshou Temple. Another account says it was founded in the 2nd year of Xining (1069), Northern Song; the truth of which remains to be verified. The existing buildings were built in Ming dynasty, with the main remains being the Mahavira Hall and Guanyin Hall. The Mahavira Hall is 3 bays wide (12.5m), 3 bays deep (11.8m), 12m total height, with double-eave xieshan roof and post-and-lintel frame; the upper and lower eaves each have 24 five-tier bracket sets, with ornate decoration. The Guanyin Hall is 3 bays wide, 3 bays deep (12.2m), 11.5m total height, with double-eave xieshan roof and post-and-lintel frame; the outer eaves have 28 bracket sets. Inside the hall there is 1 bronze mirror, cast in the 2nd year of Chenghua (1466), Ming. The inner columns and beam frames of both halls have rich carvings and polychrome paintings, with exquisite patterns and superb carving craftsmanship. The founding date of Wanshou Taoist Temple is unknown; it was rebuilt during the Ming Chenghua-Hongzhi era. Originally there were five palaces: Tianshi Hall, Heavenly Kings Hall, Xuandi Palace, and Tongming Hall; currently only Xuandi Palace survives, a Ming dynasty building, 3 bays wide (11.5m), 3 bays deep (11.5m), 12m total height, with double-eave xieshan roof and post-and-lintel frame; both upper and lower eaves have bracket sets. The rafters and columns inside the hall are huge, with a column diameter of 0.7m; the upper bracket sets, beams, and eaves are exquisitely crafted with delicate carvings; despite the faded colors, an extremely high level of craftsmanship can still be seen.

projects.name: 夕佳山民居
projects.address: 宜宾市江安县夕佳山镇坝上村西南1.5公里
projects.content_zh: 夕佳山民居位于宜宾江安县东南坝上村夕佳山境内，是一处保存完好的庄园民居建筑，1996年被列入第四批全国重点文物保护单位。夕佳山民居始建于明万历四十年(1612年)，清顺治年间(1644—1661年)、乾隆、嘉庆年间(1736—1820年)先后进行扩建，咸丰己未年(1859年)重修。经数百年修茸扩建，规模不断扩大，形制完整。现有民居建筑坐东南向西北，占地6.8万平方米，建筑面积1万余平方米，房舍123间。民居采用传统院落布局，主要由4个院落组成，每个院均围合完整，轴线明确。民居以木结构建筑为主，青瓦白墙，绿树掩映。几道圆形门洞将院落与厅堂相互连接，平添更多活跃气氛。凭借多年经营，夕佳山民居的主人给庄园留下大量绘图雕饰，内涵丰富，工艺精美，堪称民居建筑中的精品。1988年，经省、市、县编委批准，成立四川省夕佳山民俗博物馆，开设有内容丰富反映川南汉民族生活习俗的民俗展览。
projects.content_en: Xijiashan Vernacular Dwellings are located within Xijiashan, Bashang Village, southeast of Jiang'an County, Yibin. They are a well-preserved manor residence complex, listed in the 4th batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units in 1996. Xijiashan Vernacular Dwellings were first built in the 40th year of Wanli (1612), Ming dynasty, and expanded successively during the Qing Shunzhi era (1644-1661), Qianlong, and Jiaqing eras (1736-1820), and rebuilt in the Jiwei year of Xianfeng (1859). After hundreds of years of renovation and expansion, the scale continuously grew and the form became complete. The existing residential buildings face northwest from southeast, covering 68,000 sq m, with a building area of over 10,000 sq m and 123 rooms. The dwellings adopt a traditional courtyard layout, mainly consisting of 4 courtyards, each fully enclosed with clear axes. The dwellings are mainly timber structure buildings, with grey tiles and white walls, shaded by green trees. Several round doorways connect the courtyards and halls to each other, adding more lively atmosphere. Through years of management, the owners of Xijiashan Vernacular Dwellings left the manor with a large number of painted and carved decorations, rich in connotation and exquisite in craftsmanship — truly masterpieces among residential architecture. In 1988, with the approval of the provincial, municipal, and county editorial committees, the Sichuan Xijiashan Folk Customs Museum was established, opening rich folk custom exhibitions reflecting the life customs of the Han nationality in southern Sichuan.

projects.name: 隘口石牌坊
projects.address: 宜宾市珙县玉和苗族乡隘口村
projects.content_zh: 珙县隘口石牌坊建于清道光二十八年(1848年)，是当地贡生谢正业为其母建立的节孝牌坊，坐落于珙县城南玉和乡境内，距县城约70公里。牌坊坐北向南，四柱三门，高14.63米，面阔12.34米，整体形态高耸挺拔，造型优美。牌坊以黄色石块砌筑而成，表面未施粉饰，经雨露多年冲刷，黄黑两色之间更见厚重。石坊迄今保存良好，各处雕刻完好如初，除了各种神兽、动物、花草雕刻之外，各式字体的诗赋也遍布各处。北面顶层檐下竖龛内嵌有圣旨二字，以牡丹、云纹围绕，再往下为不负所天四字楷书匾额，明间南北两面浮雕二十四孝故事，左右次间多有戏曲人物故事雕刻。明间两边坊柱上刻有对联誓欲捐躯且念半龄孤子在，心怀养志能分七衮老亲忧，可知建坊初衷，一旁另有石碑一块，记载了建此石牌坊的原因：何慈惠青年丧夫，含辛茹苦将谢正业抚养成人，考取功名，为此受道光皇帝赏赐节孝牌坊。到达珙县时阴雨不断，石牌坊就笼罩在绵绵细雨中，在阴冷的空气中观牌坊，更觉一股莫名的沧桑。历史的车轮滚滚向前，我们总想于忙碌的生活中找到自我，看着古人精心准备的建筑、雕刻的艺术作品，你的心会感到莫名的宁静。
projects.content_en: The Stone Memorial Archway in Aikou, Gong County, was built in the 28th year of Daoguang (1848), Qing dynasty. It is a chastity-filial piety archway established by local provincial graduate Xie Zhengye for his mother, located within Yuhe Township, south of Gong County town, about 70km from the county town. The archway faces south, with four columns and three gates, 14.63m high, 12.34m wide. Its overall form is tall and upright, with a beautiful shape. The archway is built of yellow stone blocks, with no plaster decoration on the surface; after years of冲刷 by rain and dew, the yellow and black colors show even more solidity. The stone archway has been well preserved to this day, with all carvings as good as new. Besides carvings of various mythical beasts, animals, flowers, and plants, poems and odes in various typefaces are everywhere. In the vertical niche under the top eave on the north side, the two characters "Imperial Decree" are embedded, surrounded by peonies and cloud patterns. Further down is a four-character regular-script plaque "Bu Fu Suo Tian" (Not Failing Heaven). On the north and south faces of the central bay are relief carvings of the Twenty-Four Filial Piety Stories, and the left and right side bays mostly have carvings of opera character stories. On the archway columns on both sides of the central bay is engraved a couplet: "Vowing to give up life, yet thinking of the half-aged orphan son; with a heart to nurture aspirations, able to share the worries of the seven-robed old parent" — from which the original intention of building the archway can be known. Beside it there is another stone stele recording the reason for building this stone archway: He Cihui lost her husband while young, and through hardships raised Xie Zhengye to adulthood, who achieved official success; for this she was bestowed a chastity-filial piety archway by Emperor Daoguang. Upon arriving at Gong County, the rain was continuous, and the stone archway was enveloped in continuous drizzle. Viewing the archway in the cold and damp air, one feels an inexplicable sense of vicissitudes. The wheel of history rolls forward; we always want to find ourselves in busy life. Looking at the buildings and carved artworks carefully prepared by the ancients, your heart will feel an inexplicable tranquility.

projects.name: 泸州城垣
projects.address: 泸州市江阳区滨江路1—3段、三星街、白招牌、太平街、小北街
projects.content_zh: 泸州历史悠久，夏商时期，泸州隶属梁州，西汉时期，正式设置江阳郡。南宋时期，老泸州神臂城名扬天下，现今江阳区的泸州城墙，只剩下些断壁残垣。泸州城垣的称谓由此得来。泸州城垣位于江阳区城区，现存东、北、西三段，多为明代所建。其中东城垣包括凝光门、仁和城垣、会津城垣三段；北城垣包括三圣城垣、大北街城垣、小北街城垣三段；西城垣仅存枇杷沟城垣。全长1088.1米，均条石砌成。其中东城墙长246米，宽4米，高4.4米。西城墙长325.6米，宽4米，高6.5米。东城门，即凝光门，是仅存的城门。关于凝光门的由来，据当地的老人说，在城楼上观长江，月光洒在风平浪静的江面上，江面就像凝结成了一面镜子，由此得凝光门一名。拱形门洞跨度3米，高2.8米，进深10.25米。因城市发展变迁，原有城垣被拓宽成马路，凝光门门洞反倒成了马路下的洞口，看起来仿佛是桥洞一般。泸州城垣属古城、堡寨遗址，见证着自宋代以来泸州城的发展，极具历史、人文和科学研究价值。1992年，市政府将泸州城垣公布为市级文物保护单位；2007年，泸州城垣被省政府公布为省级文物保护单位。
projects.content_en: Luzhou has a long history. During the Xia and Shang periods, Luzhou belonged to Liangzhou; in the Western Han period, Jiangyang Commandery was formally established. During the Southern Song period, the old Luzhou Shenbi City was famous throughout the land. Today, the Luzhou city wall in Jiangyang District has only some broken walls and ruins left. Luzhou City Wall is located in the urban area of Jiangyang District; currently the east, north, and west sections survive, mostly built in Ming dynasty. Among them, the east city wall includes Ningguang Gate, Renhe City Wall, and Huijin City Wall sections; the north city wall includes Sansheng City Wall, Dabei Street City Wall, and Xiaobei Street City Wall sections; the west city wall only preserves the Pipagou City Wall. The total length is 1088.1m, all built of dressed stones. The east city wall is 246m long, 4m wide, 4.4m high. The west city wall is 325.6m long, 4m wide, 6.5m high. The East City Gate, i.e., Ningguang Gate, is the only surviving city gate. Regarding the origin of Ningguang Gate, according to local elders, viewing the Yangtze River from the city gate tower, moonlight spills on the calm river surface, and the river surface seems to condense into a mirror, hence the name Ningguang Gate. The arched gateway spans 3m, is 2.8m high, and 10.25m deep. Due to urban development and changes, the original city wall was widened into a road, and the Ningguang Gate gateway has instead become an opening under the road, looking like a bridge opening. Luzhou City Wall belongs to ancient city and fortress ruins, witnessing the development of Luzhou City since Song dynasty, with great historical, humanistic, and scientific research value. In 1992, the municipal government designated Luzhou City Wall as a municipal cultural relic protection unit; in 2007, Luzhou City Wall was designated as a provincial cultural relic protection unit by the provincial government.

projects.name: 报恩塔
projects.address: 泸州市江阳区江阳中路白塔文化广场
projects.content_zh: 报恩塔坐落于泸州市江阳区江阳中路的白塔文化广场，始建于南宋绍兴十三年至二十二年间(1143—1152年)。该塔之所以取名为报恩塔，是因为相传此塔是由南宋泸南安抚使冯楫为了报答慈母的恩情而建造的。据民国《泸县志》记载：泸州安抚使冯楫，幼年丧父离母，及长，官居于泸。诞日，在乞食群丐中寻得老母，遂建塔以报母恩，故名报恩塔。报恩塔传承的不仅是一种杰出的建筑文化，更彰显了中华民族自古以来的孝敬尊长的传统美德，因而它于2013年被列为全国重点文物保护单位。报恩塔八边形的形状和层层内收的塔身，让人印象深刻，其洁白的一身也赋予了它白塔这另一个称谓。远观报恩塔，它就像一位历经沧桑的老者仔细审视着这座历史悠久的城市，如今矗立在城中心，以塔为中心开辟成游人休闲的广场，与周围的繁华景象形成鲜明的对比，别有一番闹中取静的风味。走近报恩塔，其丰富的装饰砖雕便尽收眼底。无论是塔身还是外围的栏杆上，都随处可见精致的雕刻。这些雕刻排列整齐优雅，造型活泼灵动，犹如一幅幅上好的画作，展现在世人面前。无论是白塔外的鸟类雕塑，还是檐上的镀铜力士，都是那么的栩栩如生，让人赞不绝口。报恩塔内中心柱仍呈八边形的形状，内部原来存有南宋的石刻造像，遗憾的是这些石刻造像已经全部被毁坏掉了。而报恩塔的壮观、魅力，使得周遭的亭台也耀眼夺目。放眼望去，八角亭、望月亭和牡丹亭坐落其中，倒有一种众星捧月的奇妙韵味。温柔的阳光使得白塔与亭台相映成晖，置身其中仿佛给人一种仙境般的美妙感受。而一旁的石柱也起到画龙点睛之效，其上的图案不仅刻艺精美，更重要的是它忠实地记录着白塔的典故，时刻提醒着人们报答父母之恩。
projects.content_en: Bao'en Pagoda is located in the White Pagoda Cultural Plaza on Jiangyang Middle Road, Jiangyang District, Luzhou City. It was first built between the 13th and 22nd years of Shaoxing (1143-1152), Southern Song. The reason this pagoda is named Bao'en Pagoda is because, according to legend, it was built by Feng Ji, the Southern Song Luban Pacification Commissioner, to repay his loving mother's kindness. According to the Republican-era Luzhou County Annals: Feng Ji, Pacification Commissioner of Luzhou, lost his father and was separated from his mother in childhood; when he grew up, he served as an official in Luzhou. On his birthday, he found his old mother among a group of begging beggars, and then built the pagoda to repay his mother's kindness, hence the name Bao'en Pagoda. Bao'en Pagoda inherits not only an outstanding architectural culture, but also demonstrates the traditional Chinese virtue of respecting and honoring elders since ancient times; therefore it was listed as a National Key Cultural Relics Protection Unit in 2013. The octagonal shape and the tapering pagoda body of Bao'en Pagoda leave a deep impression, and its pure white appearance also gives it the alternative name White Pagoda. Viewing Bao'en Pagoda from afar, it is like an old man who has experienced vicissitudes carefully examining this historic city. Now standing in the city center, with the pagoda as the center, a plaza for visitors' leisure has been opened, forming a sharp contrast with the bustling scene around it, with a unique flavor of tranquility amid noise. Approaching Bao'en Pagoda, its rich decorative brick carvings come into full view. Whether on the pagoda body or the surrounding railings, exquisite carvings can be seen everywhere. These carvings are neatly and elegantly arranged, with lively and dynamic forms, like excellent paintings displayed before the world. Whether the bird sculptures outside the White Pagoda or the gilded copper guardians on the eaves, they are all so lifelike, making people praise them endlessly. The central column inside Bao'en Pagoda still has an octagonal shape; the interior originally preserved Southern Song stone carvings, but unfortunately these stone carvings have all been destroyed. And the grandeur and charm of Bao'en Pagoda make the surrounding pavilions also dazzling. Looking around, the Octagonal Pavilion, Moon-Gazing Pavilion, and Peony Pavilion are situated among them, creating a wonderful charm of stars surrounding the moon. The gentle sunlight makes the White Pagoda and pavilions reflect each other's radiance; being among them feels like a wonderful experience in a fairyland.
