And the stone pillar beside also serves as the finishing touch; the patterns on it are not only exquisitely carved, but more importantly, it faithfully records the story of the White Pagoda, constantly reminding people to repay their parents' kindness.

projects.name: 泸县屈氏庄园
projects.address: 泸州市泸县方洞乡石牌坊村
projects.type: 地主家族庄园，砖木结构
projects.content_zh: 屈氏庄园始建于清朝道光年间(1809—1845年)，由当时任知事的屈应选建造。历经几代人的建筑营造，到屈应选孙辈屈恒升时(1912—1916年)扩建碉楼、戏楼、佛堂，整体已趋完善。庄园坐西南向东北，其后倚五仙山，左依濑溪河，其整体布局为一艘大船，它的后花园花山就像船尾，前花园就如船头，此船正扬帆起航，乘风破浪之势。整座庄园总占地面积约2万平方米，现存部分8千平方米，庄园整体采用四合院布局，中轴线上由大门至花厅、正厅，左右厢房居于两侧。通院计有房87间，天井10个，戏台1座。庄园四周建围墙，墙高约3.5米。川南诸庄园中，该庄园独以其规模宏大，建造豪华而领衔风骚。2009年12月15日，石牌坊村境内的屈氏庄园正式升级为国家级文物保护单位。夏日至庄园，绿树掩映中两座碉楼巍然屹立，高墙坚壁贯通其间，俨然有不怒自威之态。庄园外观是高8米的石围墙，第二层是高8米的火砖围墙，四周修建了高达22米的北极楼、东平楼、南极楼、西平楼四座碉楼，今存北极楼、东平楼两座。两楼正对，俯瞰山河，正是两个兢兢业业守卫家园的英雄卫士。到得正门前，大门上书醒庐两个大字，此二字是前清翰林御史、伪总统顾问高蔚然书写，笔力遒劲；门两侧有大军阀谭颜楷书写的人和出明辉光照国；执义秉德安息康居两联，横批是泽绍灵均；两侧另有福禄寿喜等字样。进入庄园内部，雕梁画栋美不胜收，左右花厅，拱门圆窗间衬绿树银花，颇有些江南园林的风情，想此情景，应是待字闺中佳人，对月弄花不语，个中情思，道与谁人听？而青砖、黛瓦、白墙，更添些清新淡雅的气质，细观雕梁景致，莲叶亭亭，花草欣欣，飞鸟啾啾，其歌其语，仿在耳畔。种种风景，集巴蜀之地的婉约与内敛之美于一身而又匠心独运，各处空间设置的运用手法在总体上营造了一种和谐自然之美，令人赞叹。庄园内有井名枯井，传为地主淹死不听话丫头的地方，这又让人唏嘘不已。而各种设置中最让人难忘的是其中透露出来的深深的文化气息。石刻题记文辞优美、书法娴熟，视之观摩良久，逸兴遄飞，仿佛顷刻间胸有诗书千万卷，不吐不快。屈氏尊屈原为祖，其各辈人物，皆不乏优美诗书传世，观之有益。诸多绘画，今以鹤立江山意图凭人观瞻，作者睥睨江山之旷达胸襟，窥此可得一斑。沿北极楼木梯层层上去，可到碉楼上部。据记载，庄园是因盗匪四起而筑碉自卫。碉楼高大，墙体坚固厚实，防卫设备齐全，处处体现了防御的理念。碉楼上的瞭望口、炮口至今保存完好，犹能起到防御作用。建筑本身仅为砖木结构，经百年风雨枪炮而屹立不倒，足见其建筑水平之高超。身临碉楼之上，庄园全貌尽收眼底，其宏大之景象又再令人赞叹一番。而溯碉楼历史，一段解放军英勇剿匪的历史浮现眼前，这又为这座精美的庄园增添了红色旅游纪念地的背景。
projects.content_en: Qu's Mansion in Lu County was first built during the Qing Daoguang era (1809-1845), constructed by Qu Yingxuan, who served as a county magistrate at the time. After several generations of building and construction, by the time of Qu Hengsheng, the grandson of Qu Yingxuan (1912-1916), watchtowers, a theater tower, and a Buddhist hall were expanded, and the overall structure had become complete. The mansion faces northeast from southwest, backed by Wuxian Mountain and with the Laixi River on its left. Its overall layout is like a large ship: the back garden Huashan is like the stern, and the front garden is like the bow, this ship is setting sail with hoisted sails, braving the wind and waves. The entire mansion covers about 20000 sq m, with the existing portion being 8000 sq m. The mansion overall adopts a siheyuan layout, with the central axis running from the main gate to the flower hall and main hall, with left and right wing rooms on both sides. The entire compound has 87 rooms, 10 courtyards, and 1 theater stage. A surrounding wall is built around the mansion, about 3.5m high. Among the various mansions in southern Sichuan, this mansion uniquely leads with its large scale and luxurious construction. On December 15, 2009, Qu's Mansion within Shipaifang Village was officially upgraded to a National Key Cultural Relics Protection Unit. Arriving at the mansion in summer, two watchtowers stand majestically amid green tree shade, with high walls and solid fortifications running through, naturally possessing an imposing air without anger. The exterior of the mansion is an 8m high stone wall; the second layer is an 8m high fire-brick wall; around it are built four watchtowers, the North Pole Tower, East Peace Tower, South Pole Tower, and West Peace Tower, up to 22m high; today the North Pole Tower and East Peace Tower survive. The two towers face each other, overlooking mountains and rivers, truly two heroic guardians diligently defending their home. Arriving at the main gate, the two large characters Xing Lu are written on the gate; these two characters were written by Gao Weiran, a former Qing Hanlin censor and advisor to the puppet president, with vigorous brushwork. On both sides of the gate are couplets written by the great warlord Tan Yankai, with the horizontal inscription Ze Shao Ling Jun. On both sides are also the characters Fu Lu Shou Xi. Entering the mansion interior, the carved beams and painted pillars are a feast for the eyes; the left and right flower halls, with arched doorways and round windows set off by green trees and silver flowers, have quite the charm of Jiangnan gardens. And the blue bricks, black tiles, and white walls add a fresh and elegant temperament. Carefully observing the carved beam scenery: lotus leaves stand gracefully, flowers and plants flourish, birds chirp, their songs and words seem to be at one's ears. All these scenes combine the graceful and restrained beauty of the Bashu land with ingenious craftsmanship; the application of spatial settings throughout creates an overall harmonious and natural beauty, admirable. There is a well in the mansion named the Withered Well; legend says it was where the landlord drowned disobedient maidservants, this makes one sigh with emotion. And among all the settings, the most unforgettable is the deep cultural atmosphere revealed within. The stone inscriptions have elegant wording and skilled calligraphy; viewing and observing them for a long time, one's spirits soar, as if suddenly possessing thousands of volumes of poetry and books in one's chest, eager to express them. The Qu family revered Qu Yuan as their ancestor; people of each generation all had beautiful poetry and books passed down, beneficial to view. Climbing up the wooden ladder of the North Pole Tower layer by layer, one can reach the upper part of the watchtower. According to records, the mansion built watchtowers for self-defense because bandits rose everywhere. The watchtowers are tall, with solid and thick walls, complete defense equipment, and everywhere reflects the concept of defense. The lookout openings and cannon openings on the watchtowers are still well preserved today, still able to serve a defensive function. The building itself is only of brick-timber structure, yet has stood firm through a hundred years of wind, rain, and gunfire, sufficient to show its superb architectural level. Standing atop the watchtower, the entire mansion comes into full view; its grand scene makes one admire once again. And tracing back the history of the watchtowers, a history of the People's Liberation Army bravely suppressing bandits comes to mind, this adds the background of a red tourism memorial site to this exquisite mansion.

projects.name: 圆通寺
projects.address: 泸州市泸县喻寺镇贡献村西南100米
projects.content_zh: 位于泸州市泸县喻寺镇贡献村的圆通寺，始建于明朝正德元年(1506年)。该寺坐东南向西北，属合院布局，面积约为966.5平方米。于2002年被四川省人民政府列为第六批省级文物保护单位。有趣的是，在列为县级、市级和省级文物保护单位的石碑上，圆通寺的写法均不同。圆通寺是座木石结构的古寺庙，现在只有前殿、中殿和石厢房保存了下来。走近圆通寺，一种经过岁月洗练的氛围扑面而来。圆通寺的大门采用重檐式屋顶，正中木匾上书有圆通禅林四个大字，端正文雅。周围的白墙似乎已被雨水冲刷尽显沧桑本色，虽然有部分现代公示牌的装点，但也毫不削弱其独特的历史印记。圆通寺的前殿为石木结构，采用二重檐歇山式屋顶，抬梁穿斗混合屋架。中殿也采用二重檐歇山式屋顶，抬梁式屋架，共用4抬梁，为11檩构架前后双步梁，设9椽袱前后搭牵。殿内中柱、角柱、檐柱、山柱为石质，方形截面，原有雕刻已损毁。石柱之上各式梁架与斗拱极为精美。中殿的脊桁、上金桁、下金桁及中柱穿枋上有多处题记，表明中殿始建于明，清代经多次维修。圆通寺内陈列着各式各样的佛像和雕塑，姿态繁多，颜色各异。无论是佛祖，还是观音，抑或是罗汉甚至其他雕像，都能够给人以肃穆或安然的感受。这些雕像造型独特、表情丰富、设计精美、刻工精湛、色彩丰富、用色协调，深刻反映了当时社会的审美文化与宗教信仰。
projects.content_en: Yuantong Temple, located in Gongxian Village, Yusi Town, Lu County, Luzhou City, was first built in the 1st year of Zhengde (1506), Ming dynasty. The temple faces northwest from southeast, with a courtyard layout, covering about 966.5 sq m. In 2002 it was listed as the 6th batch of provincial cultural relic protection units by the Sichuan Provincial People's Government. Interestingly, on the stone steles listing it as county-level, municipal-level, and provincial-level cultural relic protection units, the writing of Yuantong Temple is all different. Yuantong Temple is an ancient temple of timber-stone structure; now only the front hall, middle hall, and stone wing rooms have been preserved. Approaching Yuantong Temple, an atmosphere tempered by years comes over one. The main gate of Yuantong Temple uses a double-eave roof; on the central wooden plaque are written the four large characters Yuantong Chan Lin, upright and elegant. The surrounding white walls seem to have been washed by rain, fully showing their vicissitudes; although decorated with some modern public notice boards, this does not weaken its unique historical imprint at all. The front hall of Yuantong Temple is of stone-timber structure, adopting a double-eave xieshan roof with a mixed post-and-lintel and chuan-dou roof truss. The middle hall also adopts a double-eave xieshan roof with a post-and-lintel roof truss, using 4 main beams in total, an 11-purlin frame with front and rear double-step beams, and 9 rafter ties with front and rear tie beams. The central columns, corner columns, eave columns, and gable columns inside the hall are of stone, with square cross-sections; the original carvings have been damaged. Above the stone columns, the various beam frames and bracket sets are extremely exquisite. There are multiple inscriptions on the ridge purlin, upper golden purlin, lower golden purlin, and central column through-tie of the middle hall, indicating that the middle hall was first built in Ming and repaired multiple times in Qing. Yuantong Temple displays various Buddha statues and sculptures, with numerous postures and different colors. Whether it is the Buddha, Guanyin, Arhats, or even other statues, they can all give people a feeling of solemnity or peace. These statues have unique shapes, rich expressions, exquisite designs, superb carving, rich colors, and coordinated color use, deeply reflecting the aesthetic culture and religious beliefs of the society at that time.

projects.name: 龙脑桥
projects.address: 泸州市泸县龙脑桥镇龙华村东南1.5公里
projects.content_zh: 泸州市泸县龙脑桥镇，以其龙脑桥而闻名。该桥建于明洪武十一至三十一年(1378—1398年)，是一座建筑造型和石雕艺术俱佳的古石桥建筑。整座石桥没有使用任何黏合物或榫卯衔接，因此龙脑桥作为我国古代桥梁的罕见之作，在建筑技术上具有极高的参考价值。又由于其石雕艺术精湛，具有极高的欣赏价值和历史价值，因此作为全国重点文物保护单位一点儿也不为过。龙脑桥横跨在九曲河上，远远望去，桥面扁平笔直。经过岁月的洗礼，桥上隐约露着点点青苔，绿油油的，与周围的田园风光相得益彰，仿佛与生俱来似的，桥已然和自然融为一体。而最引人注目的还数中间的八座桥墩，桥墩的墩首均刻有工艺极其精湛的石雕，其中中间四座为龙形石雕，与之相邻的两侧分别刻有象形石雕和狮形石雕，最外面的两侧则是麒麟形的石雕。一眼望去，石雕栩栩如生，仿佛活了一样，依靠在石板桥边，与周遭形成一幅无比生动的图画。仔细观察八座石雕，它们形态各异，但又活灵活现，个个炯炯有神，气宇轩昂。其中最为精美的当属龙形雕刻。细细看来，巨龙神采飞扬，清秀飘逸；口衔宝珠，妙趣横生。旁边的巨象、青狮、麒麟也毫不示弱，它们纹理清晰，神情自若。象鼻圆润卷曲，青狮雄姿英发，而旁边的麒麟更是怒目张口，好不威风！这大气磅礴的场面，在这座看似平凡的石桥上彰显得淋漓尽致。而这精雕细琢、巧夺天工之技，正是我国古代匠人技艺的卓越见证。
projects.content_en: Longnao Bridge Town in Lu County, Luzhou City, is famous for its Longnao Bridge. This bridge was built from the 11th to the 31st year of Hongwu (1378-1398), Ming dynasty. It is an ancient stone bridge building with excellent architectural form and stone carving art. The entire stone bridge does not use any adhesive or mortise-and-tenon joints; therefore, as a rare masterpiece of ancient Chinese bridges, Longnao Bridge has extremely high reference value in architectural technology. And because of its exquisite stone carving art, it has extremely high appreciation value and historical value, therefore it is entirely fitting as a National Key Cultural Relics Protection Unit. Longnao Bridge spans across the Jiuqu River; viewed from afar, the bridge deck is flat and straight. After the baptism of years, spots of green moss faintly show on the bridge, lush green, complementing the surrounding pastoral scenery, as if born with it, the bridge has already merged with nature. And the most eye-catching are the eight bridge piers in the middle; the pier heads are all carved with extremely exquisite stone carvings. Among them, the middle four are dragon-shaped stone carvings; the adjacent sides on both sides are respectively carved with elephant-shaped and lion-shaped stone carvings; the outermost sides are qilin-shaped stone carvings. At a glance, the stone carvings are lifelike, as if alive, leaning against the stone slab bridge, forming an incomparably vivid picture with the surroundings. Carefully observing the eight stone carvings, they have different forms but are all vivid, each with bright eyes and imposing bearing. Among them, the most exquisite must be the dragon carvings. Looking closely, the giant dragon is full of spirit, elegant and graceful; holding a jewel in its mouth, full of wit and charm. The giant elephant, green lion, and qilin beside are also not to be outdone; their textures are clear and their expressions composed. The elephant's trunk is round and curled, the green lion is majestic and valiant, and the qilin beside is even more glaring with mouth open, truly awe-inspiring! This grand and majestic scene is fully displayed on this seemingly ordinary stone bridge. And this exquisitely carved, wondrous craftsmanship is precisely the outstanding testimony of ancient Chinese artisans' skills.

projects.name: 泸县龙桥群
projects.name_en: Bridges with Carved Stone Dragons in Lu County
projects.address: 泸州市泸县境内
projects.highlights: 苦桥子桥、万寿桥、永济桥、顺对大桥等
projects.content_zh: 说起龙桥，大家或许并不陌生。在四川省泸州市的泸县境内，至今保存有明清时期共141座龙桥，保存完好，蔚为大观，这也是我国现存唯一的明清龙桥群。绝无仅有的龙桥文化，使得这座历史之城更加地具有历史韵味。这些龙桥分散在泸县的不同地点，如苦桥子桥、万寿桥位于福集镇，永济桥、顺对大桥位于云龙镇，龙灯桥位于方洞镇，金龙桥位于嘉明镇，另一座万寿桥、白鹤桥位于毗卢镇等等，数不胜数。其实，从这些桥中就已然对泸县的龙桥群可见一斑，其工程量之浩大，简直难以想象。走访这些龙桥建筑，便可发现各类龙雕之龙头统一朝向上游，而龙尾则统一朝向下游，有一种群龙将出之感。泸县龙桥群另一个独特之处在于桥上的巨龙全部都雕刻在桥墩之上，从桥面上观望，又有一种藏龙伏蛟之感，一种敬畏之情油然而生。巨龙虽形态各异，但是它们有一个共同的特点，那就是气势磅礴，栩栩如生，仿佛在各个角落保护着这座文明古城似的，不禁令人对其肃然起敬。仔细观察这些龙桥，你就会发现不单单只是其数量巨大深深地震撼着你，各座石桥上巨龙的雕刻更是巧夺天工，让人赞不绝口。这些龙刻造型别致、气度不凡，略带夸张手法的雕刻技巧不仅使得这些巨龙更加生动形象，还造就了其无与伦比的艺术张力。龙刻线条流畅、意境独特，更让其在我国桥梁建造史以及石刻艺术史上抹上了浓墨重彩的一笔。这不仅反映了当时我国具有鲜明特色的龙文化现象，还反映出了当时人们精神文化生活的多彩与丰富。
projects.content_en: Speaking of dragon bridges, everyone may not be unfamiliar. Within Lu County of Luzhou City, Sichuan Province, there are still 141 dragon bridges preserved from the Ming and Qing dynasties, all well preserved and spectacular. This is also the only surviving Ming-Qing dragon bridge group in China. The unique dragon bridge culture makes this historic city even more historically charming. These dragon bridges are scattered in different locations of Lu County, such as Kuqiaozi Bridge and Wanshou Bridge in Fuji Town, Yongji Bridge and Shundui Bridge in Yunlong Town, Longdeng Bridge in Fangdong Town, Jinlong Bridge in Jiaming Town, another Wanshou Bridge and Baihe Bridge in Pilu Town, and so on, countless. In fact, from these bridges one can already get a glimpse of the dragon bridge group of Lu County; the vastness of its engineering quantity is simply unimaginable. Visiting these dragon bridge buildings, one can find that the dragon heads of various dragon carvings all uniformly face upstream, while the dragon tails uniformly face downstream, giving a feeling of a group of dragons about to emerge. Another unique feature of the Lu County Dragon Bridge Group is that the giant dragons on the bridges are all carved on the bridge piers; viewing from the bridge deck, there is a feeling of hidden dragons and crouching flood dragons, and a sense of awe arises spontaneously. Although the giant dragons have different forms, they share one common characteristic: they are majestic and lifelike, as if protecting this ancient civilized city from every corner, making one cannot help but respect them. Carefully observing these dragon bridges, you will find that it is not just their huge quantity that deeply shocks you; the dragon carvings on each stone bridge are even more wondrous, making people praise them endlessly. These dragon carvings have unique shapes and extraordinary bearing; the carving technique with slightly exaggerated methods not only makes these giant dragons more vivid and lifelike, but also creates their unparalleled artistic tension. The dragon carvings have smooth lines and unique artistic conception, further adding a brilliant chapter to the history of bridge construction and stone carving art in China. This not only reflects the distinctive dragon cultural phenomenon in China at that time, but also reflects the colorful and rich spiritual and cultural life of the people at that time.

projects.name: 福宝古建筑群
projects.address: 泸州市合江县福宝镇
projects.content_zh: 福宝古镇始建于明代，初名新场，又名佛保。康熙年间扩建，因镇境状如一龙盘三龟，为发福宝地，故得名福宝，1949年后沿用此名。福宝镇是我国山地民居聚落的杰出范例，已被列入第七批全国重点文物保护单位。古镇依山傍水而建，因地制宜，建筑随山势起伏曲折，形态极为丰富。民居多为明清时期修建，其中清代为多。建筑为木结构或砖木结构，临街面多为商铺，以木质材料形成界面，视觉形象非常统一。现镇中有三街八巷，最长的回龙街由青石板铺就，宽度1.5米至8米不等，随山势蔓延1.6千米，串联镇中最主要的建筑如宫庙、宗祠、天主教堂、茶馆、酒肆、饭庄、客栈、盐号、钱庄、当铺、帮会会馆等。回龙街上南街石梯也因其独特场景成为福宝镇的标志性景观。镇中最重要的建筑是三宫六庙，即清源宫、万寿宫、天后宫、土地庙、五祖庙、张爷庙、禹王庙、火神庙、王爷庙。建筑多为清代，穿斗与抬梁结构并用，合院布局为多。小镇中如此多的宫庙建筑，是因为这里的剧名多为康熙末年湖广填四川运动中从楚、粤、闽、赣等地迁入，移民群体均建设各自家庙，承托对故乡的怀念。再加上此地为三水相汇之处，商贾众多，较为繁华，因此造就相当丰富的建筑类型。镇外另有惜字塔与回龙桥，均为清代所建。位于栗子河与大漕河交汇口南缘的西河渡保存完好，过去是福宝盐马古道水上交通的要道，至今仍保留拉纤河渡，吸引游人参加。佛宝镇最大的特点，是山势造就的建筑群高低起伏，传统穿斗民居层层叠叠，虽密集复杂却也不失其内在秩序，一条回龙街穿镇而过，上下转乘之间，形成变化多端的建筑景观，在我国传统民居建筑中独树一帜，因而声名远播。
projects.content_en: Fubao Ancient Town was first built in Ming dynasty, initially named Xinchang, also known as Fobao. It was expanded during the Kangxi era; because the town's terrain resembles a dragon coiled around three turtles, and it is a land of fortune and treasure, it was named Fubao (Fortune Treasure), and this name has been used since 1949. Fubao Town is an outstanding example of mountain residential settlements in China, and has been listed in the 7th batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units. The ancient town is built against mountains and beside water, adapting to local conditions; the buildings rise and fall and wind with the mountain terrain, with extremely rich forms. Most residences were built during the Ming and Qing dynasties, with the majority from Qing. The buildings are of timber structure or brick-timber structure; the street-facing sides are mostly shops, forming interfaces with timber materials, with a very unified visual image. Currently the town has three streets and eight alleys; the longest, Huilong Street, is paved with bluestone slabs, varying in width from 1.5m to 8m, spreading 1.6km along the mountain terrain, connecting the most important buildings in the town such as palaces and temples, ancestral halls, Catholic churches, teahouses, wine shops, restaurants, inns, salt shops, money shops, pawnshops, and guild halls. The Nanjie stone steps on Huilong Street have also become a landmark landscape of Fubao Town due to their unique scene. The most important buildings in the town are the Three Palaces and Six Temples: Qingyuan Palace, Wanshou Palace, Tianhou Palace, Tudi Temple, Wuzu Temple, Zhangye Temple, Yuwang Temple, Huoshen Temple, and Wangye Temple. The buildings are mostly from Qing, using both chuan-dou and post-and-lintel structures, mostly with courtyard layouts. The reason there are so many palace and temple buildings in the small town is that most of the local surnames were migrants from Chu, Yue, Min, Gan and other places during the Huguang-Fill-Sichuan movement in the late Kangxi era; migrant groups all built their own family temples, bearing their longing for their hometowns. In addition, this place is where three rivers meet, with many merchants and relative prosperity, hence creating quite rich building types. Outside the town there are also the Xizi Pagoda and Huilong Bridge, both built in Qing. The Xihe Ferry, located at the southern edge of the confluence of the Lizi River and Dacao River, is well preserved; in the past it was a key water transport route on the Fubao Salt-Horse Ancient Road, and to this day it still retains towpath river ferries, attracting tourists to participate. The greatest feature of Fobao Town is the undulating building complex created by the mountain terrain; traditional chuan-dou residences are layered upon each other, dense and complex yet without losing their internal order. A Huilong Street passes through the town, and between going up and down and transferring, a varied architectural landscape is formed, standing out uniquely among traditional residential architecture in China, hence its far-reaching fame.

projects.name: 尧坝镇古建筑群
projects.name_en: Ancient Building Complex in Yaoba Town
projects.address: 泸州市合江县尧坝镇
projects.highlights: 古镇布局、进士牌坊、古镇街道、东岳庙、大鸿米店
projects.content_zh: 尧坝镇古建筑群位于泸州市合江县，该镇历史悠久。据记载，北宋皇佑年间(1049—1053年)设有军事要塞，名曰尧坝寨，至明洪武中期始建城镇。尧坝古镇融合了川黔两省不同的文化和风俗，形成特色鲜明的川黔古镇文化。尧坝镇古建筑群于2013年被列入全国重点文物保护单位。走近尧坝镇，入口处映入眼帘的便是著名的进士牌坊。该牌坊坐西北向东南，保存完好。仔细观察，牌坊上题写有赐进士第等字样。虽然经过岁月的冲刷，但那字体依然苍劲有力，使得牌坊整体气势宏伟，文化底蕴显著，是名副其实的尧坝古镇标志性建筑。进入尧坝镇，漫步其中，感受来自遥远古镇带给自己的惬意与畅快。这里恬静闲适，节奏缓慢，没有车马的喧嚣，没有人声的鼎沸。仿佛一切都是那么怡然自得，让人心旷神怡。古街道上，旧式民居错落有致，青瓦房诉说着当地独特的风土人情。甚至在一些房梁或木门上，都能够看到一些精美的木雕作品，古色古香，灵动新奇。尧坝镇古建筑群的核心建筑要数始建于万历年间的东岳庙了。临近古街道的东岳庙，以红墙围城，门前书有对联，寓意深刻，令人回味无穷。古庙共分三级，分别是戏台、灵官殿和东皇殿。值得注意的是戏台前端护栏上有两块保存完好的大型木雕，其中一块名曰群仙图，整个画面布局合理，刻艺精湛，雕梁画栋，美不胜收。而大鸿米店、凌子风旧居、王朝闻故居等均作为古镇的形象建筑，显得古色古香，于古镇的魅力更是锦上添花。回头再看那悠闲的古镇，那浓厚的生活气息，那淳朴的民风，像一股清泉涌上心头，让人心向往之。或许生活在这里，恰有一番世外桃源的风味吧。
projects.content_en: The Ancient Building Complex in Yaoba Town is located in Yaoba Town, Hejiang County, Luzhou City; this town has a long history. According to records, during the Northern Song Huangyou era (1049-1053), a military fortress was established here, named Yaoba Fortress, and the town was first built in the mid-Hongwu period of Ming. Yaoba Ancient Town integrates the different cultures and customs of Sichuan and Guizhou provinces, forming a distinctive Sichuan-Guizhou ancient town culture. The Ancient Building Complex in Yaoba Town was listed as a National Key Cultural Relics Protection Unit in 2013. Approaching Yaoba Town, what comes into view at the entrance is the famous Jinshi (Presented Scholar) Archway. This archway faces southeast from northwest and is well preserved. Careful observation reveals inscriptions such as Ci Jinshi Di (Bestowed Presented Scholar Residence) on the archway. Although washed by years, the calligraphy remains vigorous and powerful, making the archway overall majestic with significant cultural heritage, a veritable landmark building of Yaoba Ancient Town. Entering Yaoba Town and strolling through it, one feels the comfort and delight brought by the distant ancient town. Here it is tranquil and leisurely, with a slow pace, no noise of carriages and horses, no clamor of voices. Everything seems so contented and at ease, making one feel relaxed and happy. On the ancient streets, old-style residences are well-arranged, and the grey-tile houses tell of the unique local customs and traditions. Even on some beams or wooden doors, one can see some exquisite woodcarving works, antique and quaint, lively and novel. The core building of the Ancient Building Complex in Yaoba Town must be the Dongyue Temple, first built during the Wanli era. The Dongyue Temple, adjacent to the ancient street, is enclosed by red walls, with couplets written in front of the gate, with profound meaning that lingers in memory. The ancient temple is divided into three levels: the theater stage, Lingguan Hall, and Donghuang Hall. It is worth noting that on the front guardrail of the theater stage there are two well-preserved large woodcarvings, one of which is called the Group of Immortals Picture; the entire picture has a reasonable layout, exquisite carving craftsmanship, with carved beams and painted pillars, a feast for the eyes. And the Dahong Rice Shop, former residence of Ling Zifeng, former residence of Wang Zhaowen, etc., all serve as image buildings of the ancient town, appearing antique and quaint, adding to the charm of the ancient town. Looking back at the leisurely ancient town, its strong atmosphere of life, its simple folk customs, like a clear spring surging into the heart, making people yearn for it. Perhaps living here is just like having a taste of a paradise beyond the world.

projects.name: 春秋祠
projects.address: 泸州市叙永县叙永镇盐店街
projects.highlights: 布局、结构、大厅、正殿、木雕、石刻
projects.content_zh: 位于泸州市叙永县叙永镇盐店街的春秋祠，建于清光绪二十六年(1900年)。之所以取名春秋祠，是因为与之所供奉的关羽酷爱阅读《春秋》一书有关。春秋祠具有典型的园林风格，淳朴自然，美不胜收，它也曾作为富有盐商的会所之所。因此，作为典型的清代古建筑，春秋祠于2006年被国务院列入全国重点文物保护单位名单。春秋祠的历史价值和观赏价值如此重要，一是有悠久的历史文物，时刻提醒着后人这里所蕴含的点点滴滴；二是有自然的山水风光，给人以恬静舒适惬意之感。而春秋祠恰好满足这两点特征，时空交融，韵味十足，所谓印象深刻流连忘返当然也不在话下。春秋祠长方形的布局，由四个封闭式的四合院构成，从前往后依次为乐楼、大厅、正殿、三官殿。春秋祠内许多处的建筑或景色都映衬出其具有对称格局之美的特点。在对称性之外，春秋祠的建筑历史韵味飘散。保存完好的建筑结构配合精美的琉璃瓦屋顶，绿意盎然，夺目至极。置身于这赏心悦目的隽秀园林中，仿佛身心都经过了洗礼，静谧畅快之感油然而生。或许春秋祠建筑的巧夺天工，更以精湛的木雕著称。无论是门楣窗棂，还是坊额斜衬，无处不体现着其木雕技艺的完美。这流畅的纹路、精细的刻工，无论是圆雕、浮雕或是镂空都显得那么游刃有余，其中尤以八扇百鸟梅花窗最为著名。而在春秋祠中随处可见的石刻艺术，与木雕艺术相辅相成、相得益彰。无论是石桌、石凳，抑或是盆景石座，几乎均有巧妙的镂空技术贯穿其中。漫步祠中，精心观赏这些木雕石刻，或许所谓的心旷神怡，也大抵如此吧。
projects.content_en: Chunqiu Shrine, located on Yandian Street, Xuyong Town, Xuyong County, Luzhou City, was built in the 26th year of Guangxu (1900), Qing dynasty. The reason it is named Chunqiu (Spring and Autumn) Shrine is because it is related to Guan Yu, whom it enshrines, being fond of reading the Spring and Autumn Annals. Chunqiu Shrine has a typical garden style, simple and natural, a feast for the eyes; it also once served as a clubhouse for wealthy salt merchants. Therefore, as a typical Qing dynasty ancient building, Chunqiu Shrine was included in the list of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units by the State Council in 2006. The historical value and ornamental value of Chunqiu Shrine are so important: first, it has long-standing historical relics, constantly reminding later generations of the bits and pieces contained here; second, it has natural mountain and water scenery, giving people a feeling of tranquility, comfort, and coziness. And Chunqiu Shrine恰好 satisfies both of these characteristics, with time and space blending, full of charm; so-called deep impression and lingering reluctance to leave are of course out of the question. Chunqiu Shrine has a rectangular layout, composed of four enclosed siheyuan courtyards, arranged from front to back as the Music Tower, Great Hall, Main Hall, and Sanguan Hall. Many buildings or scenes within Chunqiu Shrine reflect its characteristic of symmetrical layout beauty. Beyond symmetry, the architectural historical charm of Chunqiu Shrine wafts in the air. The well-preserved building structure, combined with exquisite glazed tile roofs, is full of greenery, extremely eye-catching. Being in this delightful and graceful garden, as if body and mind have been baptized, a feeling of tranquility and joy arises spontaneously. Perhaps the wondrous craftsmanship of Chunqiu Shrine's architecture is even more famous for its exquisite woodcarvings. Whether it is the lintels and window frames, or the architraves and diagonal brackets, nowhere does it not reflect the perfection of its woodcarving technique. These smooth patterns and fine carving, whether round carving, relief carving, or openwork carving, all appear so effortless; among them, the eight panels of Hundred Birds and Plum Blossom windows are the most famous. And the stone carving art seen everywhere in Chunqiu Shrine complements and enhances each other with the woodcarving art. Whether it is stone tables, stone stools, or bonsai stone bases, almost all have ingenious openwork technology running through them. Strolling in the shrine, carefully admiring these woodcarvings and stone carvings, perhaps the so-called carefree and joyful feeling is roughly like this.

projects.name: 德阳文庙
projects.address: 德阳市旌阳区文庙街
projects.content_zh: 德阳文庙也称德阳孔庙，位于德阳市旌阳区文庙街，是中国西部地区保存完整、规模宏大的孔庙建筑群，素有德阳文庙甲西川之名，于2001年由国务院宣布成为全国重点文物保护单位。德阳文庙始建于南宋开禧年间(约为1216年)，后损毁。明洪武年由知县温文改建于城南，经成化到万历年间的多次修缮，初具规模，但明末毁于战乱。现有文庙为清顺治年间重建(1661年)，经乾隆、嘉庆、道光年间的多次修葺，终有现今留存的建筑。德阳文庙有30余处古建筑，占地面积达2.07万平方米，坐北朝南，四合院落沿着中轴线对称布置。在中轴线上，从广场的宫墙起依次为棂星门、泮池、戟门、大成殿、启圣殿(殿后为后花园)。两侧则为对称的道贯古今坊、德配天地坊、东西庑、东西配殿等。文庙主体建筑为大成殿，坐落于中院，上覆精美雕饰，恢宏阔大，是文庙庭院建筑中最为高大、保存较为完好的一座古建筑。除大成殿以外，雕刻精美的棂星门，优雅石拱桥，独具特色的德配天地坊、道贯古今坊都具有鲜明的特色，这也是德阳文庙在西南地区独树一帜，在全国文庙中占有重要地位的原因。文庙至今香火依然鼎盛，也是弘扬儒学文化的圣地。
projects.content_en: Deyang Confucian Temple, also known as Deyang Confucius Temple, is located on Wenmiao Street, Jingyang District, Deyang City. It is a well-preserved, large-scale Confucian temple building complex in western China, known as the finest Confucian temple in western Sichuan. In 2001 it was declared a National Key Cultural Relics Protection Unit by the State Council. Deyang Confucian Temple was first built during the Southern Song Kaixi era (around 1216), later destroyed. In Ming Hongwu it was rebuilt south of the city by County Magistrate Wen Wen, and after multiple repairs from Chenghua to Wanli, it began to take shape, but was destroyed by war at the end of Ming. The existing temple was rebuilt during Qing Shunzhi (1661), and after multiple renovations during Qianlong, Jiaqing, and Daoguang, it finally has the buildings preserved today. Deyang Confucian Temple has over 30 ancient buildings, covering 20,700 sq m, facing south, with siheyuan courtyards arranged symmetrically along the central axis. On the central axis, starting from the palace wall of the square, are依次 Lingxing Gate, Pan Pool, Ji Gate, Dacheng Hall, and Qisheng Hall (with a back garden behind the hall). On both sides are the symmetric Daoguan Gujin Archway, Depei Tiandi Archway, east and west corridors, east and west side halls, etc. The main building of the temple is Dacheng Hall, located in the central courtyard, covered with exquisite carvings, grand and spacious — the tallest and best-preserved ancient building among the temple courtyard buildings. Besides Dacheng Hall, the exquisitely carved Lingxing Gate, elegant stone arch bridge, and the unique Depei Tiandi Archway and Daoguan Gujin Archway all have distinctive features — this is also why Deyang Confucian Temple stands out in the southwest region and occupies an important position among Confucian temples nationwide. The temple still has flourishing incense to this day, and is also a sacred place for promoting Confucian culture.

projects.name: 上庸长阙
projects.address: 德阳市旌阳区黄许镇三合村
projects.content_zh: 上庸长阙位于德阳市旌阳区黄许镇三合村，所在的位置较为隐蔽，几经周折，在黄许镇种猪场内可找到这座汉代古阙。上庸长阙始建于汉代，现存右阙的母阙，阙身整体置于清朝所修砖亭的保护之中。上庸长阙是四川境内保存较为完好的汉代古阙，被列为四川省省级文物保护单位。在砖亭之中的上庸长阙显得分外质朴庄重。阙身之外放置有一石碑，其上阴刻隶书上庸长三字，字体沉稳舒展，非常雅观。阙有三层结构，向外呈飞斜倒梯形状，在砖龛内部略显拘束。上有花草雕纹，精美雅致。阙身刻有铭文，但经岁月剥蚀，已不复清晰。在顶部的砖龛之中，横嵌有石碑，以楷体书汉上庸长司马孟台之神道碑，隽逸秀美。石碑上有一小樽观音塑像，应该为村民祭拜所用。在砖龛背部上方，亦嵌有横碑楷书清光绪九年九月中瀚培修，应该为砖亭修建时的记录。上庸长阙的阙主为司马孟台，生前于上庸(今湖北房县)为官，由于其为官清廉爱民如子，造福了上庸一代的人民，为了纪念他的功德，家乡的人民为其镌立了上庸长阙。从此，他的清廉贤德便与这不世出的汉代雕刻珍品一起，传世千年，不由得令人感慨。
projects.content_en: Shangyonglong Tower is located in Sanhe Village, Huangxu Town, Jingyang District, Deyang City. Its location is relatively hidden; after several twists and turns, this Han dynasty ancient tower can be found within the Huangxu Town breeding pig farm. Shangyonglong Tower was first built in Han dynasty; currently the right mother tower survives, with the tower body entirely placed under the protection of a brick pavilion built in Qing dynasty. Shangyonglong Tower is a relatively well-preserved Han dynasty ancient tower within Sichuan, listed as a Sichuan provincial cultural relic protection unit. Shangyonglong Tower inside the brick pavilion appears particularly simple and solemn. Outside the tower body there is a stone stele, on which the three characters Shang Yong Chang are engraved in intaglio clerical script, with steady and舒展 calligraphy, very elegant. The tower has a three-layer structure, outward in a flying slanted inverted trapezoid shape, appearing slightly constrained inside the brick niche. Above there are flower and plant carving patterns, exquisite and elegant. The tower body is engraved with inscriptions, but after years of erosion, they are no longer clear. In the brick niche at the top, a stone stele is horizontally embedded, written in regular script as Han Shangyong Chang Sima Mengtai zhi Shendao Bei (Spirit Way Stele of Sima Mengtai, Magistrate of Shangyong, Han), graceful and elegant. On the stone stele there is a small Guanyin statue, presumably for villagers to worship. Above the back of the brick niche, a horizontal stele is also embedded with regular script reading Repaired in the middle of the 9th month of the 9th year of Guangxu, Qing — presumably a record from when the brick pavilion was built. The owner of Shangyonglong Tower was Sima Mengtai, who served as an official in Shangyong (present-day Fangxian, Hubei) during his lifetime. Because he was an honest official who loved the people as his own children and brought benefit to the people of Shangyong, to commemorate his merits and virtues, the people of his hometown erected Shangyonglong Tower for him. From then on, his honesty and virtue, together with this rare Han dynasty carving treasure, have been passed down for a thousand years — one cannot help but sigh with emotion.

projects.name: 姜公坟、姜孝祠
projects.name_en: Tomb of Jiang and Shrine Devoted to Jiang's Filial Piety
projects.address: 德阳市孝泉镇德孝城
projects.content_zh: 孝泉古镇位于四川省德阳市西北，据历史记载，此地以孝道闻名传世，是二十四孝中一门三孝故事的发生地，同时也是德孝文化的发源地。而在孝泉古镇最能反映德孝文化的建筑便是姜公坟与姜孝祠。姜公坟是孝泉人为了纪念孝子姜诗所建，始建于明正德年间。整个姜公坟面积约100平方米，为石砌圆形丘，共有墓4座，在墓前有三座石碑并排而立，碑旁有荷花池。整个姜公坟布局幽雅、古朴。姜孝祠同样也是为了纪念孝子姜诗夫妇。相传姜孝祠建于汉朝，后毁于战火，在宋治平年间重建，今日所见大多为清代修整之后的状况。如今的姜孝祠包括正殿、左殿以及右殿，各殿都采用斗拱、飞檐、镂空雕花木窗装饰。在正殿门柱上刻有第一芳名泛汉代；无双正气属姜家的对联，殿内也还保存着姜氏夫妇的塑像。从清代开始，为弘扬德孝文化，当地民众每年自发修缮扩建姜孝祠，并在此举行大型的姜公祭祀活动，吸引了大批民众参加，德孝文化也因此广泛传播。
projects.content_en: Xiaoquan Ancient Town is located northwest of Deyang City, Sichuan Province. According to historical records, this place is famous for filial piety passed down through generations, and is the birthplace of the Three Filial Piety in One Family story among the Twenty-Four Filial Exemplars, as well as the birthplace of De-Xiao (Virtue-Filial Piety) culture. And in Xiaoquan Ancient Town, the buildings that best reflect De-Xiao culture are Jiang Gong Tomb and Jiang Xiao Shrine. Jiang Gong Tomb was built by the people of Xiaoquan to commemorate the filial son Jiang Shi, first built during the Ming Zhengde era. The entire Jiang Gong Tomb covers about 100 sq m, a stone-built circular mound with 4 tombs in total; in front of the tombs there are three stone steles standing side by side, with a lotus pond beside the steles. The entire layout of Jiang Gong Tomb is elegant and simple. Jiang Xiao Shrine was likewise built to commemorate the filial son Jiang Shi and his wife. According to legend, Jiang Xiao Shrine was built in Han dynasty, later destroyed by war, and rebuilt during the Song Zhiping era; what is seen today is mostly the condition after Qing dynasty renovations. Today's Jiang Xiao Shrine includes the main hall, left hall, and right hall; each hall is decorated with bracket sets, flying eaves, and openwork carved wooden windows. On the main hall door pillars is engraved a couplet: The first fine name spans the Han dynasty; the unparalleled righteous spirit belongs to the Jiang family. Inside the hall, statues of Mr. and Mrs. Jiang are also preserved. Starting from Qing dynasty, to promote De-Xiao culture, local people spontaneously repair and expand Jiang Xiao Shrine every year, and hold large-scale Jiang Gong memorial activities here, attracting large numbers of people to participate — De-Xiao culture has thus spread widely.

projects.name: 龙护舍利塔
projects.address: 德阳市旌阳区孝泉镇北
projects.content_zh: 龙护舍利塔位于德阳市旌阳区孝泉镇北，为方形砖塔，始建于元朝顺帝时期。塔身通高34.75米，整个修建过程耗时12年方才竣工。龙护舍利塔挺拔壮丽，为孝泉的最高点，在塔顶可以俯视孝泉美景。龙护舍利塔为四川现存的唯一一座元代砖塔，具有珍贵的历史研究价值，现被列入第七批全国重点文物保护单位。龙护舍利塔整体坐北朝南，为十三级方形密檐砖塔。塔基方形，以砖砌筑，上刻龙饰，塔身自下而上层层内缩，顶部攒尖，设双重葫芦形塔刹，四周檐角上挑。塔内中空，设五层塔心室，每层塔心室内皆供有佛像，精巧非凡。自元代建造至今，龙护舍利塔在历史上先后遭遇过多次地震而屹立不倒，特别是经历汶川5.12严重的大地震后，塔身残破不堪的情况下仍然矗立，展现出极富韧性的结构强度。后经过修葺，古塔又重复雄伟挺拔之势，其不仅是孝泉地区的标志性古建筑，更是孝泉古镇两千多年的历史文化缩影。
projects.content_en: Longhu Sarira Pagoda is located north of Xiaoquan Town, Jingyang District, Deyang City. It is a square brick pagoda, first built during the Yuan Shundi period. The pagoda body is 34.75m tall overall, and the entire construction process took 12 years to complete. Longhu Sarira Pagoda is tall and magnificent, the highest point of Xiaoquan; from the pagoda top one can overlook the beautiful scenery of Xiaoquan. Longhu Sarira Pagoda is the only surviving Yuan dynasty brick pagoda in Sichuan, with precious historical research value, and is currently listed in the 7th batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units. Longhu Sarira Pagoda overall faces south, a thirteen-level square dense-eave brick pagoda. The pagoda base is square, built of bricks, carved with dragon decorations; the pagoda body tapers inward layer by layer from bottom to top, with a pyramidal top and a double gourd-shaped finial, with eave corners upturned on all sides. The pagoda is hollow inside, with five levels of pagoda chambers; each pagoda chamber enshrines Buddha statues, exquisitely extraordinary. Since its construction in Yuan dynasty to today, Longhu Sarira Pagoda has withstood multiple earthquakes in history without falling; especially after the severe Wenchuan 5.12 earthquake, despite the pagoda body being in tatters, it still stood, demonstrating extremely resilient structural strength. After later repairs, the ancient pagoda regained its majestic and upright posture. It is not only a landmark ancient building in the Xiaoquan area, but also a microcosm of the over two thousand years of history and culture of Xiaoquan Ancient Town.

projects.name: 绵竹关帝庙
projects.name_en: Shrine of Guan Gong in Mianzhu
projects.address: 绵竹市剑南镇大南路342号
projects.content_zh: 关帝庙位于绵竹市剑南镇，始建于明朝的天启年间，由大学士刘宇亮所修建，后于同治年间再次维修并修建了拜殿。现为绵竹一处著名的文化旅游胜地。绵竹关帝庙整体坐西朝东，气势雄浑。庙门楹联神盈宇宙，气肃千秋，彰显着武圣的威仪。进门迎首可见一尊关羽读卷的坐像，只见关帝所持《春秋》，赤面长髯，颇有一番威武气度。往内拜殿之处一座高大的壁画，描绘着美髯公单刀赴会的故事，画艺精湛，人物栩栩如生。正殿内供奉着关帝塑像，上覆牌匾，书有忠义常昭，以表对关羽忠义的敬仰。正殿的建筑艺术风格具有典型的明清特色，其后为乾隆时期修建的启圣殿，内奉关帝圣像。此外，殿内还有很多描述关云长英勇事迹的壁画，着实引人入胜。
projects.content_en: Guan Di Temple is located in Jiannan Town, Mianzhu City. It was first built during the Ming Tianqi era, constructed by Grand Secretary Liu Yuliang, and later repaired again during the Tongzhi era with a worship hall added. It is now a famous cultural tourism destination in Mianzhu. Mianzhu Guan Di Temple overall faces east from west, with vigorous and imposing momentum. The couplet on the temple gate reads Spirit fills the universe, awe肃 for a thousand autumns, demonstrating the majesty of the Martial Saint. Entering the gate, one first sees a seated statue of Guan Yu reading a scroll; the Guan Di holds the Spring and Autumn Annals, with a red face and long beard, quite a majestic bearing. Inside, at the worship hall, there is a tall mural depicting the story of the beautiful-bearded man going to a meeting alone with a sword; the painting skill is exquisite and the figures are lifelike. The main hall enshrines a statue of Guan Di, covered with a plaque inscribed Loyalty and Righteousness Ever Shining, to express respect for Guan Yu's loyalty and righteousness. The architectural art style of the main hall has typical Ming-Qing characteristics; behind it is the Qisheng Hall built during the Qianlong era, enshrining the sacred image of Guan Di. In addition, there are many murals inside the hall describing Guan Yunchang's heroic deeds, truly fascinating.

projects.name: 三溪寺
projects.address: 德阳市土门镇梅子沟
projects.content_zh: 三溪寺位于德阳土门镇梅子沟，始建于北宋年间，原名广安寺，现为德阳市重点文物保护单位。寺庙坐落于青山碧水之间，甚是幽静。据说在之前5.12汶川地震中，三溪寺周围的民居都遭到了较为严重的损毁，而三溪寺却毫发未伤，由此可见寺庙创立者的眼光非凡，选择了一块风水宝地。三溪寺主要建筑有弥勒殿、观音殿、大雄宝殿等处。弥勒殿内香火鼎盛，莲台上的弥勒佛面怀微笑，神采奕奕，让人顿时有亲近之感。弥勒殿后为观音殿，观音殿殿顶点缀着几座精美的雕塑，殿内则供奉千手观音塑像。殿内的两壁上至今尚存元代手书龙虎二字，笔力雄伟遒劲。观音殿后的大雄宝殿历史最为悠久，据考证为明代建筑，距今约有600多年历史。殿顶佛像雕刻繁多而精美，栩栩如生，内所供奉佛像也令人心生崇敬。此外，三溪寺内还有文殊殿与客房等建筑，格局宏大开阔。
projects.content_en: Sanxi Temple is located in Meizigou, Tumen Town, Deyang. It was first built during the Northern Song dynasty, originally named Guang'an Temple, and is now a Deyang municipal key cultural relic protection unit. The temple is situated among green mountains and clear waters, extremely tranquil. It is said that during the previous 5.12 Wenchuan earthquake, the residential buildings around Sanxi Temple all suffered relatively severe damage, while Sanxi Temple was completely unharmed — from this one can see the extraordinary vision of the temple's founder, who chose a treasured fengshui site. The main buildings of Sanxi Temple include the Maitreya Hall, Guanyin Hall, and Mahavira Hall. Incense flourishes in the Maitreya Hall; the Maitreya Buddha on the lotus platform has a smiling face and bright spirit, making one immediately feel a sense of closeness. Behind the Maitreya Hall is the Guanyin Hall; the top of the Guanyin Hall is adorned with several exquisite sculptures, and inside the hall is enshrined a Thousand-Armed Guanyin statue. On the two walls inside the hall, the two characters Dragon and Tiger handwritten in Yuan dynasty still survive to this day, with vigorous and powerful brushwork. The Mahavira Hall behind the Guanyin Hall has the longest history; according to research it is a Ming dynasty building, about 600 years old to date. The top of the hall has numerous and exquisite Buddha statue carvings, lifelike; the Buddha statues enshrined inside also make one feel reverence. In addition, Sanxi Temple also has buildings such as the Manjushri Hall and guest rooms, with a grand and open layout.

projects.name: 祥符寺
projects.address: 绵竹市城关小西门外
projects.content_zh: 祥符寺是一座驰名川西的寺庙，始建于唐代，被毁后重建于北宋大中祥符年间。这便是祥符之名的由来。据文献载，华严宗五祖圭峰宗密禅师曾经入蜀，在今绵竹祥符寺开坛讲法，后来圭峰圆寂后，绵竹寺僧为了纪念他，遂在今祥符寺侧造衣冠墓。寺门楹联称寺经炎宋题名在，僧有圭峰卓锡来说的就是祥符寺的历史沿革。今夕经过不断地修整，祥符寺愈发庄严雄伟，清太史李元曾赞誉祥符寺为天下第一禅林。祥符寺现存建筑有玉佛殿、金刚殿、武圣殿、大雄宝殿、观音殿、藏经楼、东西罗汉堂、祖师殿、弥勒殿、药师殿及左古厢房等，轴线严谨，其间穿插各色植物，雅致幽深。其中值得一提的是罗汉堂800余尊罗汉及诸天善神的塑像，形态各异、法相庄严，数罗汉也成为了这里的有趣活动之一。祥符寺的镇寺之宝包括省内最大的两尊缅甸玉佛，另外其中收藏的《大藏经》更是世上所存四部中最为完整的一套，具有极高的价值。此外寺内还有洪武十七年留存的古井、颇具风情的白塔之类小品，都为这里点缀出些许新意。此外祥符寺还有一大人文看点，即各代名士所题的楹联，比如于右任题于绵竹祥符寺祖堂的绵延山势钟九龙，应识回峰顾祖；静密河声灌双耳，还来微笑拈花。，一副一副细细读来，教人心境澄明，顿悟禅机。
projects.content_en: Xiangfu Temple is a temple famous in western Sichuan. It was first built in Tang dynasty, and after being destroyed was rebuilt during the Northern Song Dazhong Xiangfu era — this is the origin of the name Xiangfu. According to documents, Master Guifeng Zongmi, the fifth patriarch of the Huayan sect, once entered Sichuan and opened an altar to preach the Dharma at today's Mianzhu Xiangfu Temple. Later, after Guifeng passed away, the monks of Mianzhu Temple, to commemorate him, built a clothes-and-hat tomb beside today's Xiangfu Temple. The couplet on the temple gate reads The temple named in the fiery Song dynasty remains; the monk Guifeng once dwelt here — this refers to the historical evolution of Xiangfu Temple. Today, after continuous renovations, Xiangfu Temple has become increasingly solemn and majestic; Qing dynasty Grand Secretary Li Yuan once praised Xiangfu Temple as the foremost Chan forest under heaven. The existing buildings of Xiangfu Temple include the Jade Buddha Hall, Vajra Hall, Martial Sage Hall, Mahavira Hall, Guanyin Hall, Scripture Library, east and west Arhat Halls, Patriarch Hall, Maitreya Hall, Medicine Master Hall, and left ancient wing rooms, etc., with rigorous axes, interspersed with various plants, elegant and deep. Among them, it is worth mentioning the over 800 statues of Arhats and various heavenly good deities in the Arhat Hall, with different forms and solemn Dharma appearances; counting Arhats has also become one of the interesting activities here. The town-protecting treasures of Xiangfu Temple include the two largest Burmese jade Buddhas in the province; in addition, the Tripitaka collected therein is the most complete set among the four surviving copies in the world, with extremely high value. In addition, there are small items inside the temple such as the ancient well preserved from the 17th year of Hongwu and the charming White Pagoda, all adding some novelty here. Furthermore, Xiangfu Temple has another major humanistic highlight: the couplets inscribed by famous scholars of various dynasties. For example, Yu Youren inscribed at the ancestral hall of Mianzhu Xiangfu Temple: The stretching mountain form gathers nine dragons, one should recognize the returning peak looking back at its ancestor; the quiet and dense river sound fills both ears, yet comes again the smile holding a flower. Reading them one by one carefully, one's mind becomes clear, and one suddenly realizes the Chan mechanism.

projects.name: 慧剑寺
projects.address: 德阳市什邡市回澜镇慧剑村的慧剑公司内部
projects.content_zh: 慧剑寺位于德阳市什邡市回澜镇慧剑村的慧剑公司内部，这座与国企现代建筑相结合的千年古寺令人印象深刻，因其较为完整地保留了寺庙建筑格局，于2013年成为第七批全国重点文物保护单位。慧剑寺始建于唐代贞观年间，主体在明末几乎毁坏殆尽，仅剩觉皇殿。经过清朝顺治和嘉庆等朝代的重修扩建，留存为我们今日所见的布局与规模。慧剑寺的整体布局为坐北朝南的四合院样式，中轴线上的建筑依次为觉皇殿、观音殿、大佛殿、藏经楼，两边对称分布着罗汉堂和厢房。觉皇殿具有明显的明代风格特征，大佛殿与藏经楼则为清代的典型建筑。殿中有古井名为慧剑，这也是慧剑寺这一寺庙名称的来源。此外，慧剑寺内还留有金鸭池、应梦楼等充满传奇色彩的历史遗迹，浓郁的历史文化氛围令人心怀思古之情。
projects.content_en: Huijian Temple is located inside Huijian Company in Huijian Village, Huilan Town, Shifang City, Deyang. This thousand-year-old ancient temple combined with modern state-owned enterprise buildings is impressive; because it relatively completely preserves the temple building layout, it became the 7th batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units in 2013. Huijian Temple was first built during the Tang Zhenguan era; the main body was almost completely destroyed at the end of Ming, leaving only the Juehuang Hall. After reconstruction and expansion during dynasties such as Qing Shunzhi and Jiaqing, it remains as the layout and scale we see today. The overall layout of Huijian Temple is a siheyuan style facing south, with buildings on the central axis依次 being Juehuang Hall, Guanyin Hall, Great Buddha Hall, and Scripture Library; on both sides symmetrically distributed are the Arhat Hall and wing rooms. Juehuang Hall has obvious Ming dynasty style characteristics, while the Great Buddha Hall and Scripture Library are typical Qing dynasty buildings. Inside the hall there is an ancient well named Huijian (Wisdom Sword), which is also the source of the temple name Huijian Temple. In addition, Huijian Temple also retains legendary historical relics such as the Golden Duck Pond and Yingmeng (Dream-Responding) Tower; the rich historical and cultural atmosphere makes one feel nostalgic for the past.

projects.name: 中江南塔
projects.address: 四川省德阳市中江县朝阳南路铜鱼山
projects.content_zh: 中江南塔位于中江县城南区朝阳南路的铜鱼山上，与中江北塔不同，南塔坐落的铜鱼山并不甚高，大约只有30米。顺着青石板路走上石台，便可近距离地感受中江南塔庄严巍峨的仪态。中江南塔始建于明神宗年间，坐南朝北，与中江北塔遥相呼应。南塔塔身呈正八边形，共有九层，由方砖堆垒而成，古韵十足。塔的基座坚固而厚重，基座之上塔身逐层递缩，每层均有砖砌重檐，阳光照射下形成强烈的明暗对比。各层也皆设有门洞与窗洞，顶上为攒尖铁质塔顶，富有质感。塔底有座拱形门。资料记载，中江南塔为中江古八景之一，颇为有名。且据当地人讲述，在汶川地震之前，中江南塔至今几乎未曾修葺，保存基本完好，可见古人在南塔的修建方面确实匠心独运。
projects.content_en: South Pagoda of Zhongjiang is located on Tongyu Mountain, Chaoyang South Road, in the southern area of Zhongjiang County town. Unlike the North Pagoda of Zhongjiang, the Tongyu Mountain where the South Pagoda sits is not very high, only about 30m. Following the bluestone slab path up to the stone platform, one can closely feel the solemn and majestic bearing of the South Pagoda of Zhongjiang. South Pagoda of Zhongjiang was first built during the reign of Emperor Shenzong of Ming, facing north from south, echoing the North Pagoda of Zhongjiang from afar. The South Pagoda body is a regular octagon, with nine stories in total, built of square bricks stacked together, full of ancient charm. The pagoda base is solid and heavy; above the base, the pagoda body tapers layer by layer, each story with brick-built double eaves, forming a strong light-dark contrast under sunlight. Each story also has door openings and window openings; the top is a pyramidal iron pagoda top, rich in texture. At the bottom of the pagoda there is an arched gate. According to records, South Pagoda of Zhongjiang is one of the Eight Ancient Scenes of Zhongjiang, quite famous. And according to local people, before the Wenchuan earthquake, the South Pagoda of Zhongjiang had almost never been repaired to this day, and was basically well preserved — showing that the ancients were indeed ingenious in the construction of the South Pagoda.

projects.name: 中江北塔
projects.address: 德阳市中江县北塔山顶
projects.content_zh: 中江北塔位于德阳市中江县北塔山顶，山下的入口为一座寺庙，名为白塔圣寺。进入寺庙，经过天王殿、大雄宝殿、观音殿三大殿等仿古建筑以及一座高达九米的露天大佛坐，拾级而上，便可看到北塔山顶巍峨耸立的中江北塔。在北塔山巅，高十三级的中江北塔直指苍穹，高耸入云，其恢宏壮阔之势，实在难以用语言描述。中江北塔始建于北宋神宗时期，嘉庆、光绪年间经过维修，目前保存完好，是四川不可多得的北宋砖塔，于2013年被国务院宣布成为第七批全国重点文物保护单位。中江北塔为方形十三级密檐式砖塔，通高30米，南向与中江南塔遥相呼应。宝塔通身由红砖堆垒而成，实心构造。塔身独特，第一层很高，二层以上则间距较小，自第七层开始塔身明显内缩，形成强烈的塔身曲线。塔顶饰有宝珠，显得很有仪式感。整座北塔地势高耸，塔身挺拔，密檐精细完整，砖石坚固厚重，气势雄健。
projects.content_en: North Pagoda of Zhongjiang is located on the summit of North Pagoda Mountain, Zhongjiang County, Deyang City. The entrance at the foot of the mountain is a temple named White Pagoda Holy Temple. Entering the temple, passing through the antique buildings of the three major halls — Heavenly Kings Hall, Mahavira Hall, and Guanyin Hall — as well as a 9m-tall open-air seated Great Buddha, and climbing up the steps, one can see the towering North Pagoda of Zhongjiang standing majestically on the summit of North Pagoda Mountain. At the peak of North Pagoda Mountain, the thirteen-level North Pagoda of Zhongjiang points straight at the sky, soaring into the clouds; its grand and magnificent momentum is truly difficult to describe in words. North Pagoda of Zhongjiang was first built during the Northern Song Shenzong period, repaired during the Jiaqing and Guangxu eras, and is currently well preserved. It is a rare Northern Song brick pagoda in Sichuan, and was declared by the State Council as the 7th batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units in 2013. North Pagoda of Zhongjiang is a square thirteen-level dense-eave brick pagoda, 30m tall overall, facing south and echoing the South Pagoda of Zhongjiang from afar. The entire pagoda is built of red bricks stacked together, with a solid structure. The pagoda body is unique: the first story is very high, while the spacing above the second story is smaller; starting from the seventh story, the pagoda body明显 tapers inward, forming a strong pagoda body curve. The pagoda top is decorated with a jewel, appearing very ceremonial. The entire North Pagoda sits on high terrain, with an upright pagoda body, fine and complete dense eaves, solid and heavy brick and stone, and vigorous momentum.

projects.name: 寿宁寺
projects.address: 德阳市中江县南华镇西山乡
projects.content_zh: 寿宁寺位于中江县城西侧，寺庙始建于隋，原名圣寿寺，一说雷神庙。后为纪念于此处出家的高僧正果法师——前佛教协会副会长、北京广济寺住持，将其更名为寿宁寺，现为四川省文物保护单位。进入寿宁寺，便可看见一块镌刻着寿宁寺的牌匾，书法圆润而美观。寿宁寺先后经过数次重修，现存建筑多为明清时期所遗留。正殿大雄宝殿保存着典型的明清建筑特色。殿顶有祥龙、白象、瑞兽等众多精美的雕刻，殿内供奉着一尊工艺精巧的缅甸玉佛，此外还供有阿弥陀佛和释迦佛，皆庄严而慈祥。大雄宝殿后为观音殿，供奉着西方三圣像，别具一格。观音殿后为新翻修的天王殿，结构与现代建筑更为接近。此外，寿宁寺还是中江八大美景之一的楼妙飞霞所在之地，云霞汇聚，晨光照射之下，会出现五彩胜景，极富魅力。
projects.content_en: Shouning Temple is located on the west side of Zhongjiang County town. The temple was first built in Sui dynasty, originally named Shengshou Temple, also said to be Leishen (Thunder God) Temple. Later, to commemorate the eminent monk Master Zhengguo — former vice president of the Buddhist Association and abbot of Beijing Guangji Temple — who became a monk here, it was renamed Shouning Temple. It is now a Sichuan provincial cultural relic protection unit. Entering Shouning Temple, one can see a plaque engraved with Shouning Temple, with round and beautiful calligraphy. Shouning Temple has undergone several reconstructions successively; the existing buildings are mostly remnants from the Ming and Qing periods. The main hall, Mahavira Hall, preserves typical Ming-Qing architectural features. On the hall top there are numerous exquisite carvings such as auspicious dragons, white elephants, and auspicious beasts; inside the hall is enshrined a Burmese jade Buddha with exquisite craftsmanship, in addition to Amitabha Buddha and Shakyamuni Buddha, all solemn and kind. Behind the Mahavira Hall is the Guanyin Hall, enshrining the Three Sages of the West, with a unique style. Behind the Guanyin Hall is the newly renovated Heavenly Kings Hall, with a structure closer to modern architecture. In addition, Shouning Temple is also the location of Lou Miao Fei Xia, one of the Eight Great Scenes of Zhongjiang; where clouds and rosy clouds gather, under the morning light, a five-colored scenic view appears, extremely charming.

projects.name: 中江玄武观
projects.address: 德阳市中江县朝阳南路铜鱼山乡
projects.content_zh: 中江玄武观坐落于中江县玄武山顶，与中江南塔隔着东江遥相呼应。玄武观始建于东晋，现存的建筑应为明清时期重修所遗留，现为四川省文物保护单位。玄武观大门为一座优雅精致的牌坊，进门之后，沿着山间石道拾级而上，便可看到山顶之上充满道教特色的四合院式建筑。玄武观的主要建筑为真武殿、三清殿与玉皇殿三座大殿，分别为前殿、正殿与后殿。大殿左右两侧设有厢房和望楼，格局甚是开阔。正殿三清殿雕梁画栋，檐顶雕有精美的瑞兽。殿内供奉着道教最高尊神——玉清、上清、太清这三清祖师的泥塑塑像，画工精湛，仪态非凡。
projects.content_en: Xuanwu Taoist Temple in Zhongjiang is located on the summit of Xuanwu Mountain, Zhongjiang County, echoing the South Pagoda of Zhongjiang across the East River from afar. Xuanwu Taoist Temple was first built in Eastern Jin; the existing buildings should be remnants from reconstruction during the Ming-Qing period, and are now a Sichuan provincial cultural relic protection unit. The main gate of Xuanwu Taoist Temple is an elegant and exquisite archway; after entering the gate, following the mountain stone path and climbing up the steps, one can see the Daoist-featured siheyuan-style building on the mountain summit. The main buildings of Xuanwu Taoist Temple are three major halls: Zhenwu Hall, Sanqing Hall, and Yuhuang Hall, respectively the front hall, main hall, and rear hall. On the left and right sides of the major halls are wing rooms and watchtowers, with a very open layout. The main hall, Sanqing Hall, has carved beams and painted pillars, with exquisite auspicious beasts carved on the eave top. Inside the hall are enshrined the clay sculptures of the highest revered deities of Daoism — the Three Pure Ones: Yuqing, Shangqing, and Taiqing — with exquisite painting craftsmanship and extraordinary bearing.

projects.name: 龙居寺
projects.address: 广汉市新丰镇龙居村
projects.content_zh: 龙居寺位于新丰镇龙居村，为禅宗八祖马祖道一的道场，寺内现存有一尊马祖塑像与一件石刻蒲团，相传为唐代遗物。龙居寺于2013年被国务院宣布为全国第七批重点文物保护单位。龙居寺为明洪武年间重建，历经历代增建方成今日规模。寺中的龙居寺中殿始建于明正统年间，是最为古老的建筑。原殿内前梁上题有惟大明正统十二年岁次丁卯十二月癸丑十二日已巳值口黄道吉日旦建立龙居禅寺字样，力证中殿建造年代。殿堂面阔三间，左右各有一道耳门。屋顶上覆青瓦，饰有宝顶，两端施鱼龙吻，甚是雄壮。中殿内保存着珍贵的明代壁画，相传为唐伯虎所作。近百平方米的壁画上描绘着佛教十二圆觉72僧众及供养人等内容，画工精妙，人物，造型庄严，形态各异，惟妙惟肖，加之线条敷以金粉，显得金碧辉煌，光彩夺目，张大千先生临摹时曾赞叹：大有敦煌遗风。这些壁画为明代绘画艺术珍品，价值斐然。
projects.content_en: Longju Temple is located in Longju Village, Xinfeng Town. It is the Daochang (spiritual site) of Mazu Daoyi, the Eighth Patriarch of Chan Buddhism. Inside the temple there currently survives a statue of Mazu and a stone-carved meditation cushion, said to be relics from Tang dynasty. Longju Temple was declared by the State Council as the 7th batch of National Key Cultural Relics Protection Units in 2013. Longju Temple was reconstructed during the Ming Hongwu era, and after successive additions through dynasties, it reached today's scale. The middle hall of Longju Temple in the temple was first built during the Ming Zhengtong era, and is the oldest building. On the front beam inside the original hall is inscribed the text: Established on the auspicious day of the 12th day of the 12th month of the Dingmao year, the 12th year of Zhengtong of the Great Ming — strongly testifying to the construction date of the middle hall. The hall is 3 bays wide, with a side door on each left and right side. The roof is covered with grey tiles, decorated with a precious top, with fish-dragon ornaments at both ends, very majestic. Inside the middle hall, precious Ming dynasty murals are preserved, said to be by Tang Bohu. The nearly 100-square-meter murals depict the Twelve Perfect Enlightenment Bodhisattvas, 72 monks, and donors of Buddhism, etc.; the painting craftsmanship is exquisite, with figures, solemn modeling, various forms, and lifelike depiction; in addition, the lines are applied with gold powder, appearing resplendent and dazzling. Mr. Zhang Daqian once sighed in admiration when copying: Greatly has the legacy style of Dunhuang. These murals are treasures of Ming dynasty painting art, with remarkable value.

projects.name: 广汉文庙
projects.address: 广汉市中心文庙建筑群
projects.content_zh: 广汉文庙始建于北宋年间，明代多次重修，明末荒废，清康熙元年(1662年)重建，清代又经多次修整。在2008年5月12日的特大地震中，文庙受到了较大损毁，后经修缮，恢复了文庙的大致面貌，并于2013年9月正式免费对外开放。文庙即孔庙，是中国古代祭祀供奉孔子的庙宇，地方文庙也是地方官学教授儒学的最高学府，是庙学合一的礼制性建筑。广汉文庙即为典型的左庙右学的格局，主要由棂星门、大成殿、戟门、名宦祠、东庑、乡贤祠、泮池、东西庑及学宫等古代礼制性建筑组成。棂星门是一座六柱五开间的石质牌楼建筑，明间有清中期书法家张怀泗所书的棂星门三字。门两面遍布雕刻，技艺精湛，造型优美，尤以赵孟頫的八骏图为最佳，堪称川西石刻艺术珍品。文庙内的泮池，寓意泮宫之池，呈半圆形，用拱桥相连。除了这个泮池，广汉文庙还有外泮池(现叫房湖荷花池)，是广汉文庙特别的地方。清代汉州志中记载的汉州八景之一的泮鲤呈祥即指外泮池。造访之时，池内荷花正盛，接天莲叶，映日荷花，美不胜收。传说每逢乡试之时，池内浮出几条红鲤，就预示着今年能考中几人。大成殿是整个建筑群的核心建筑，面阔三间17米，进深9.5米，穿斗抬梁式构架，单檐歇山式顶，6根透雕的云龙石柱精美无比，凸显了大成殿的气象庄严。戟门亦称大成门，取义于《孟子》中言：孔子之谓集大成。面阔五间21.8米，进深8.8米，为硬山式顶，抬梁式构架，前面有廊。戟门原用于存放祭祀礼和乐器，祭祀时也兼作官绅的更衣室。现作为文庙接待室和工艺品部。广汉文庙形制完整，规模宏大，每年的9月28日，也就是孔子的诞辰日举行祭孔仪式，对传承城市历史文脉、传播中华优势传统文化、宣导华夏礼仪、丰富民众精神文化生活发挥出积极作用。
projects.content_en: Guanghan Confucian Temple was first built during the Northern Song dynasty, repaired multiple times in Ming, abandoned at the end of Ming, and rebuilt in the 1st year of Kangxi (1662), Qing, then renovated multiple times in Qing. In the great earthquake of May 12, 2008, the temple suffered relatively severe damage; after later repairs, the general appearance of the temple was restored, and it was officially opened to the public free of charge in September 2013. Wenmiao is the Confucius Temple, the temple for sacrificing and enshrining Confucius in ancient China; local Confucian temples were also the highest institutions for local official schools to teach Confucianism, a ritual building combining temple and school. Guanghan Confucian Temple is a typical layout of temple on the left and school on the right, mainly composed of ancient ritual buildings such as Lingxing Gate, Dacheng Hall, Ji Gate, Minghuan Shrine, East Corridor, Xiangxian Shrine, Pan Pool, East and West Corridors, and the School Palace. Lingxing Gate is a stone paifang building with six columns and five bays; in the central bay are the three characters Lingxing Gate written by mid-Qing calligrapher Zhang Huaisi. Both sides of the gate are covered with carvings, with exquisite craftsmanship and beautiful forms; especially the Eight Steeds painting by Zhao Mengfu is the finest,堪称 a treasure of western Sichuan stone carving art. The Pan Pool inside the temple, meaning the pool of Pan Palace, is semicircular, connected by an arch bridge. Besides this Pan Pool, Guanghan Confucian Temple also has an outer Pan Pool (now called Fanghu Lotus Pond), a special feature of Guanghan Confucian Temple. One of the Eight Scenes of Hanzhou recorded in the Qing dynasty Hanzhou Prefecture Annals, Pan Li Cheng Xiang (Auspicious Carp in the Pan Pool), refers to the outer Pan Pool. When visiting, the lotus flowers in the pool were in full bloom; the lotus leaves reaching the sky and the lotus flowers reflecting the sun were a feast for the eyes. Legend says that whenever the provincial examination comes, if several red carp surface in the pool, it foretells how many people will pass the exam this year. Dacheng Hall is the core building of the entire complex, 3 bays wide (17m), 9.5m deep, with a chuan-dou and post-and-lintel frame, single-eave xieshan roof, and 6 exquisitely openwork-carved cloud-dragon stone columns, highlighting the solemn aura of Dacheng Hall. Ji Gate, also called Dacheng Gate, takes its meaning from the Mencius saying: Confucius is called the one who集大成 (gathers all achievements). It is 5 bays wide (21.8m), 8.8m deep, with a flush gable roof, post-and-lintel frame, and a corridor in front. Ji Gate was originally used to store sacrificial rituals and musical instruments, and also served as a changing room for officials and gentry during sacrifices. It now serves as the temple reception room and crafts department. Guanghan Confucian Temple has a complete form and large scale. Every year on September 28, the birthday of Confucius, a Confucius worship ceremony is held, playing a positive role in inheriting the city's historical context, spreading excellent traditional Chinese culture, promoting Chinese etiquette, and enriching the people's spiritual and cultural life.

projects.name: 平武报恩寺
projects.address: 绵阳市平武县龙安镇东风路26号
projects.highlights: 明代木构、转轮藏、千手观音
projects.content_zh: 平武报恩寺是目前我国保存最完整的明代古建筑群之一，主要建筑始建于明代，极为珍贵。寺庙始建于明正统五年(1440年)，完工于天顺四年(1460年)，为明代龙州(今天的平武)土官王玺奏请朝廷为报答皇恩而修建。它平面布局设计考究，单体建筑建造精美。值得一提的是全寺木构件均用楠木做成，具有较高的抗震性能。在平武报恩寺山门之前立有一对石经幢，为净化度人之意；紧邻山门则有两个面目沧桑的石雕大石狻猊，据传说是龙的第五子，因为龙即为天子，所以狻猊在此守门有报谢皇恩之意。跨过了山门大殿，里面有钟楼，上题天音醒世，据说声音非常洪亮；有趣的是对面却没有鼓楼，这个现象打破了寺庙的一般形制。另有一口范公古井，水质清甜。过了金水桥和天王殿，就是镇寺之宝转轮经藏的所在地——华严藏殿，这里的转轮藏是我国所存三座转轮经藏中最完整精美的，边上的雕龙也栩栩如生，大有飞腾之势。再后面的大悲殿内，则供有一座楠木的千手观音像，其雕刻之精细，亦是世间少有。再看报恩寺的正殿大雄宝殿，内供九龙牌位，佛坛上有泥塑佛像三尊，屏壁背面是三大士像。殿内墙壁上还绘有十二圆觉壁画。塑像与彩绘结合呈现，十分精彩。除了这些主要建筑，报恩寺内的步步高升斜廊也是研究抗震结构的极佳样本。据传，至今已有500多年历史的报恩寺全寺共有9999条龙，它们与传统的形象稍有出入，形态各异；再加大雄宝殿供奉的皇帝牌位(龙位)，恰好10000条龙，确是规模不凡。
projects.content_en: Bao'en Temple in Pingwu is one of the most completely preserved Ming dynasty ancient building complexes in China today; its main buildings were first built in Ming dynasty, extremely precious. The temple was first built in the 5th year of Zhengtong (1440), Ming, and completed in the 4th year of Tianshun (1460). It was built by Wang Xi, the local official of Longzhou (today's Pingwu) in Ming dynasty, who petitioned the imperial court to build it to repay the emperor's grace. Its planar layout design is exquisite, and individual buildings are beautifully constructed. It is worth mentioning that all timber components of the entire temple are made of nanmu (phoebe) wood, with high seismic performance. In front of the mountain gate of Pingwu Bao'en Temple stand a pair of stone sutra pillars, meaning purification and salvation of beings; adjacent to the mountain gate are two weathered stone-carved great suanni (mythical lions), said to be the fifth son of the dragon; because the dragon is the Son of Heaven, the suanni guarding the gate here has the meaning of repaying the emperor's grace. Crossing the mountain gate hall, inside there is a bell tower, inscribed with Tianyin Xingshi (Heavenly Sound Awakens the World), said to have a very resonant sound; interestingly, there is no drum tower opposite, a phenomenon that breaks the general form of temples. There is also an ancient well called Fan Gong Ancient Well, with sweet and clear water. Crossing the Golden Water Bridge and the Heavenly Kings Hall, one reaches the location of the temple's treasure, the revolving sutra cabinet — the Huayan Zang Hall. The revolving sutra cabinet here is the most complete and exquisite among the three surviving revolving sutra cabinets in China; the carved dragons beside are also lifelike, with a great tendency to soar. Further back, in the Great Compassion Hall, there is enshrined a thousand-armed Guanyin statue made of nanmu wood; its carving finesse is also rare in the world. Looking again at the main hall of Bao'en Temple, the Mahavira Hall, it enshrines a Nine-Dragon tablet; on the altar there are three clay Buddha statues, and on the back of the screen wall are the images of the Three Great Bodhisattvas. The walls inside the hall are also painted with murals of the Twelve Perfect Enlightenment Bodhisattvas. The combination of statues and polychrome paintings is presented, very splendid. Besides these main buildings, the step-by-step ascending sloping corridor inside Bao'en Temple is also an excellent sample for studying seismic-resistant structures. According to legend, Bao'en Temple, with over 500 years of history to date, has a total of 9,999 dragons throughout the temple; they differ slightly from traditional images, with various forms; plus the emperor's tablet (dragon throne) enshrined in the Mahavira Hall, there are exactly 10,000 dragons — truly extraordinary in scale.

projects.name: 昭忠祠、王玺公衙和镇羌门及城墙
projects.name_en: Zhaozhong Shrine, Official Residence of Wang Xi, Zhenqiang Gate and City Wall
projects.address: 绵阳市平武县龙安镇东风路
projects.content_zh: 昭忠祠又名北岳殿，是绵阳市平武县城隍庙最后一殿。该祠为龙州宣抚司使薛氏建于明代，大堂前的四株古柏苍翠遒劲。经过近年整修，焕然一新，现为清式风格。王玺公衙：看过作为深山宫殿的平武报恩寺，很多人会关注王玺平日里办公的所在。其实王玺的公堂就在紧邻报恩寺的王玺公衙内。王玺公衙始建年代不详，明嘉靖四十五年(1566年)龙州改龙安府后，这里就成为了土司衙门，于1986年迁人报恩寺内。这座土司官署原为三进院落，以大堂为中心，前面列有仪门、牌坊和石鼓，后面有二堂、三堂，侧有廊屋；布局紧凑，规模宏大，现在仅有大堂建筑得以保存。镇羌门及城墙：龙州城墙也为薛忠义所建，建于宣德五年(1430年)。原环城九里，有东西南北四座城门，有东西两栋门楼。现在仅剩长约626米的残墙，城门仅存西门镇羌门。城墙外侧以石块与片石砌筑，内部用卵石泥土夯筑，顶部墙垛部用砖砌成。镇羌门也经过整修，上面的二层城楼是新建建筑，面阔五间，歇山顶，与城墙保持协调。
projects.content_en: Zhaozhong Shrine, also known as Beiyue Hall, is the last hall of the City God Temple in Pingwu County town, Mianyang City. This shrine was built by the Xue family, the Xuanfu Commissioner of Longzhou, in Ming dynasty; the four ancient cypresses in front of the main hall are verdant and vigorous. After recent renovations, it has taken on a completely new look, now in Qing style. Official Residence of Wang Xi: Having seen Pingwu Bao'en Temple as a deep-mountain palace, many people will pay attention to where Wang Xi worked on weekdays. In fact, Wang Xi's official hall is within the Official Residence of Wang Xi, immediately adjacent to Bao'en Temple. The founding date of the Official Residence of Wang Xi is unknown; after Longzhou was changed to Long'an Prefecture in the 45th year of Jiajing (1566), Ming, this place became the chieftain's yamen, and was moved into Bao'en Temple in 1986. This chieftain's official residence was originally a three-courtyard complex, centered on the main hall; in front were listed the ceremonial gate, archway, and stone drums; behind were the second and third halls, with corridor rooms on the sides. The layout is compact and the scale is grand; now only the main hall building has been preserved. Zhenqiang Gate and City Wall: The Longzhou city wall was also built by Xue Zhongyi, in the 5th year of Xuande (1430). Originally it encircled the city for nine li, with four city gates in the east, west, south, and north, and two gate towers in the east and west. Now only a remnant wall about 626m long remains, and only the West Gate, Zhenqiang Gate, survives among the city gates. The outer side of the city wall is built of stone blocks and flagstones, the interior is rammed with cobbles and earth, and the top crenellations are built of bricks. Zhenqiang Gate has also been renovated; the two-story gate tower above is a newly built structure, 5 bays wide, with xieshan roof, coordinated with the city wall.

projects.name: 豆叩寺
projects.address: 绵阳市平武县豆叩镇中街
projects.content_zh: 如今，走进平武县豆叩镇的人远远就能看见一座坐落在清漪江旁的气势恢宏的古寺，它在重重基台顶端傲然耸立，气势不凡——这就是建于明代早期的全国重点文物保护单位，豆叩寺。豆叩寺已经经历了历史上多次大地震，汶川震后更是在受损严重的情况下顽强挺立。现在它已经成为绵阳平武县首个挂牌并免费对外开放的文物保护站，让当地人们可以进一步了解关于文物保护的知识。为了保护古迹，临河一侧还修建了坚固的河堤。豆叩寺原名为五显庙，为当地窦、寇二氏人家捐资修建，故又名窦寇寺。清代时该寺一度称为豆口寺，后谐名为豆叩寺。豆叩寺原建筑群规模较大，依山就势，由山门、罗汉殿、观音殿、正殿(大佛殿)组成四合院建筑。如今仅有正殿存留。关于豆叩寺始建于何年，其实并无文献或碑文记载，故无从考证。但从现今遗存的古迹格局做法来看，专家断定其为明代建筑，距今500多年。值得一提的是，豆叩寺前檐下斗拱采用斜下45度斜昂的做法，势如劈竹、斜刺向下，使建筑看上去刚劲有力。这种做法在四川地区古建筑中十分罕见。豆叩寺虽仅存大殿，却是集历史、宗教、建筑、艺术为一体，向今人展示了当时古建筑的工艺和杰出的抗震能力。
projects.content_en: Today, people walking into Doukou Town, Pingwu County, can see from afar a magnificent ancient temple situated beside the Qingyi River, standing proudly atop layered foundation platforms with extraordinary momentum — this is Doukou Temple, a National Key Cultural Relics Protection Unit built in the early Ming dynasty. Doukou Temple has experienced multiple major earthquakes in history; after the Wenchuan earthquake, it stood tenaciously despite severe damage. Now it has become the first listed and free-to-the-public cultural relic protection station in Pingwu County, Mianyang, allowing local people to further learn about cultural relic protection knowledge. To protect the ancient site, a sturdy river embankment has been built on the river-facing side. Doukou Temple was originally named Wuxian Temple, built with donations from the local Dou and Kou families, hence also called Doukou Temple (with different characters). In Qing dynasty the temple was once called Doukou Temple (with yet other characters), later homophonically named Doukou Temple. The original building complex of Doukou Temple was relatively large-scale, following the mountain terrain, consisting of a mountain gate, Arhat Hall, Guanyin Hall, and main hall (Great Buddha Hall) forming a siheyuan building. Today only the main hall survives. Regarding the year Doukou Temple was first built, there is actually no document or stele inscription record, so it cannot be verified. But judging from the surviving ancient site layout and practices, experts conclude it is a Ming dynasty building, over 500 years old to date. It is worth mentioning that the bracket sets under the front eave of Doukou Temple adopt the practice of ang (lever arm) slanting downward at 45 degrees, like splitting bamboo, thrusting diagonally downward, making the building look vigorous and powerful. This practice is very rare among ancient buildings in Sichuan region. Although only the main hall survives at Doukou Temple, it integrates history, religion, architecture, and art, showing people today the craftsmanship and outstanding seismic resistance of ancient buildings at that time.

projects.name: 永平堡古城
projects.address: 绵阳市北川县开坪乡永安村东800米
projects.content_zh: 永平堡古城是北川羌族自治县境内现存规模最大、保存较为完好的明代军事设施。据记载，古城建于明嘉靖二十六年(1547年)，原为松潘总兵所在地。这座明代的军事遗址分上、中、下三城，以及九墩和一个校场，分布面积约900万平方米。三城的城墙均为就地取石，用粗加工条石垒砌外墙，中心再以碎石、泥土夯实填筑，这正是羌族依山居止，垒石为室建筑艺术特色的体现。因此这座古城对研究羌人独特的建筑文化有重要价值。三城周围没有九墩，用于军人观察瞭望和传递信号，每墩高10米以上，顶上再竖起10米高的灯杆，关、堡、墩联结为一个巨大的防御体系。永平堡古城的修建根源于明朝政府与一些少数氐族暴民之间的冲突，为了平息暴乱、抵御羌民攻劫、维护连接内地与边疆的必经之路，明王朝才修建了这座坚固的永平堡古城。其中下城视野开阔，中城运筹帷幄，上城把守关口，三城依山而建，全面防守，遵循了作战需求。至清朝之后，统治者对边远地区民族实行以抚化为主的政策，故不再需要这座堡垒，那些砖石也慢慢被青苔覆盖；今日，尚有几户人家居住于内。
projects.content_en: Yongpingbao Ancient Fortress is the largest-scale and relatively well-preserved Ming dynasty military facility surviving within Beichuan Qiang Autonomous County. According to records, the ancient fortress was built in the 26th year of Jiajing (1547), Ming, originally the location of the Songpan General-in-Chief. This Ming dynasty military site is divided into upper, middle, and lower cities, as well as nine mounds and a parade ground, with a distribution area of about 9 million sq m. The city walls of all three cities use locally quarried stone, with roughly dressed stone blocks laid for the outer wall, and the center rammed and filled with crushed stone and earth — this precisely reflects the Qiang people's architectural art characteristic of living according to the mountain and piling stone as rooms. Therefore this ancient fortress has important value for studying the Qiang people's unique architectural culture. Around the three cities there are nine mounds, used by soldiers for observation, lookout, and signal transmission; each mound is over 10m high, with a 10m-high lamp pole erected on top; the passes, fortresses, and mounds are connected into a huge defense system. The construction of Yongpingbao Ancient Fortress originated from conflicts between the Ming dynasty government and some violent Di ethnic minority people; to quell the riots, resist Qiang raids, and maintain the necessary route connecting the interior and the frontier, the Ming dynasty built this sturdy Yongpingbao Ancient Fortress. Among them, the lower city has a broad view, the middle city is for strategic planning, and the upper city guards the pass; the three cities are built according to the mountain, with comprehensive defense, following combat requirements. After Qing dynasty, the rulers adopted a policy mainly of pacification for ethnic groups in remote areas, so this fortress was no longer needed, and those bricks and stones were slowly covered by moss; today, several households still live inside.

projects.name: 青林口古镇
projects.address: 二郎庙镇西南
projects.content_zh: 在二郎庙镇西南的小山沟里，潼江之源马阁水与另一条小河的交汇处，青林口静静依山傍水而立。历史上，青林口曾经是交通要道，自然而然地发展成为一座商业发达的古镇。如今的青林口虽然街道破旧，石板路也显得饱经风雨，但从两侧林立的老房子，以及雕刻着精美图案的高大木结构建筑，依然可见古镇曾经商贾云集、会馆林立、庙堂四布的繁华风貌。《西游记》续集剧组曾在此拍摄两集外景，青林口古镇因此声名鹊起。现在古街两侧有些小店铺，或是饭馆，或是卖些当地的特产。其中尤以豆腐干和皮蛋出名。新街的尽头是著名的红军桥，原名合益桥。是红四方面军强渡嘉陵江，建立了苏维埃政权的地方。一名刘姓女红军因伤被安置在镇上的杨姓银匠家里，后不幸被国民党清共队查出。在国民党的严刑拷打中，她宁死不屈，在合益桥头上英勇就义。人们为纪念这位红军，在桥上的风雨楼挂上了红军桥的匾牌。如今，红军桥上石刻的拥护红军坚决反帝抗日红军是穷人的救星等标语历经沧桑依然清晰可见，无声地向后人述说着那段血雨腥风的历史。红军桥连接着老街的另一头，老房子沿着无名小河一字排开，使小镇呈T字形结构。老街的最南端是火神庙，建于清光绪年间。由火神殿、文昌殿、玉皇殿组成，里面供着的有道教的玉皇大帝、火神、文昌君，也有佛主释迦牟尼。沿着青石板路朝北走，拐过一棵古老的菩提树，就是半边街。曾经是青林口最早的中心半边街如今只剩一溜稀稀拉拉的房子，难得见到一个人影，昔日辉煌已不在。在道路尽头，是横跨潼江的铁索桥，名永济桥。曾三次毁于洪灾，因而为了镇水护桥，还修建一座三楼一殿的云楼，名曰锁水寺。民国十六年(1927年)重建后，又更名为桂林桥。锁水寺山门右边有一道高4米的巨型石碑。石碑上书桂林桥三字，刚劲有力，小写有三丰神笔，传说为张三丰所书。青林口古镇共有五省会馆、五座大型宫殿和五座古戏台。古镇街道还有一幢别具一格的过街凉亭，每逢夜晚，古镇都会点亮七盏巨大的街灯，亮如白昼。
projects.content_en: In the small mountain valley southwest of Erlangmiao Town, at the confluence of the Mange River (source of the Tong River) and another small river, Qinglinkou stands quietly against the mountain and beside the water. Historically, Qinglinkou was once a transportation hub, naturally developing into a commercially prosperous ancient town. Today's Qinglinkou, although its streets are dilapidated and the stone slab roads appear weathered, from the old houses standing in rows on both sides and the tall timber structures carved with exquisite patterns, one can still see the prosperous appearance of the ancient town once gathering merchants, with numerous guild halls and temples spread around. The crew of the Journey to the West sequel once filmed two episodes of exterior scenes here, and Qinglinkou Ancient Town rose to fame as a result. Now on both sides of the ancient street there are some small shops, either restaurants or selling local specialties. Among them, dried tofu and preserved eggs are particularly famous. At the end of the new street is the famous Red Army Bridge, originally named Heyi Bridge. It was the place where the Fourth Front Army of the Red Army forcibly crossed the Jialing River and established the Soviet regime. A female Red Army soldier surnamed Liu was placed in the home of a silversmith surnamed Yang in the town due to injury, but was unfortunately discovered by the Kuomintang Communist-Clearance Squad. Under the Kuomintang's severe torture, she would rather die than surrender, and heroically died at the head of Heyi Bridge. To commemorate this Red Army soldier, people hung a Red Army Bridge plaque on the wind-and-rain tower on the bridge. Today, the stone-carved slogans on the Red Army Bridge such as Support the Red Army, Resolutely Oppose Imperialism and Resist Japan, and The Red Army is the Savior of the Poor are still clearly visible despite vicissitudes, silently recounting that bloody history to later generations. The Red Army Bridge connects to the other end of the old street; old houses line up along the nameless small river, making the small town呈 a T-shaped structure. At the southernmost end of the old street is the Fire God Temple, built during the Qing Guangxu era. It consists of the Fire God Hall, Wenchang Hall, and Jade Emperor Hall, enshrining the Daoist Jade Emperor, Fire God, and Wenchang Lord, as well as the Buddhist Lord Shakyamuni. Walking north along the bluestone slab road and turning past an ancient bodhi tree, one reaches Banbian Street (Half Street). Once the earliest center of Qinglinkou, Banbian Street now only has a sparse row of houses, with rarely a person in sight; its former glory is gone. At the end of the road is an iron chain bridge spanning the Tong River, named Yongji Bridge. It was destroyed by floods three times; therefore, to subdue the water and protect the bridge, a cloud tower with three stories and one hall was built, named Suoshui Temple (Water-Locking Temple). After reconstruction in the 16th year of the Republic (1927), it was renamed Guilin Bridge. To the right of the Suoshui Temple mountain gate is a giant stone stele 4m high. On the stele are written the three characters Guilin Bridge, vigorous and powerful, with small writing Sanfeng Divine Brush, legend says written by Zhang Sanfeng. Qinglinkou Ancient Town has a total of five provincial guild halls, five large palaces, and five ancient theater stages. The ancient town street also has a unique cross-street pavilion; every night, the ancient town lights up seven huge street lamps, bright as daylight.

projects.name: 文胜普照寺
projects.address: 绵阳市江油市文胜乡长坪村东500米
projects.content_zh: 据记载，文胜普照寺修建于明朝洪武年间，后经明清前后14年的维修加建，成为一座远近闻名的寺院。文胜普照寺坐东朝西，现存一进四合院。该寺内除大雄殿为明代建筑外，其余房屋均为清乃至现代所建。大雄殿为单檐悬山顶，屋顶陡峻，用材硕大，有明代后期风格，是市内遗存较早的木建筑。此外，文胜普照寺的一个与众不同之处就是它内部收藏的一系列石碑碑文记载了它在一代代人的努力下逐渐发展前进的感人历史。寺内存有古碑五块，分别是道光四年(1824年)万善同归碑记、道光十四年(1834年)广种福田碑记、道光十四年新修雨廊碑记、咸丰十年(1860年)功德碑记和光绪二十一年(1895年)中元会碑记。另有当代维修普照寺碑记一通。将石碑上的故事串联起来，就是普照寺的发展史：住持圆慧培补了大雄宝殿、文昌殿和两廊，后来再次化缘培补了寺庙、塑造了神像；住持法林化缘培补了寺庙，新修了东西两廊，几年后又化缘新塑三尊大佛，为罗汉穿金。住持超凡兴办了一次中元会。看过这些你会恍然惊叹，这样一座幽深的小院凝聚了那么多先辈的心血。
projects.content_en: According to records, Wensheng Puzhao Temple was built during the Ming Hongwu era, and after 14 years of maintenance and expansion before and after the Ming-Qing period, it became a well-known temple near and far. Wensheng Puzhao Temple faces west from east, with one existing siheyuan courtyard. Inside the temple, except for the Mahavira Hall which is a Ming dynasty building, the other houses were built in Qing or even modern times. The Mahavira Hall has a single-eave overhanging gable roof, with a steep roof and large timber materials, having a late Ming style; it is an earlier surviving timber building in the city. In addition, a distinctive feature of Wensheng Puzhao Temple is that a series of stone stele inscriptions collected inside record its touching history of gradual development and progress through the efforts of generations. There are five ancient steles preserved in the temple: respectively the Wan Shan Tong Gui (All Goodness United) Stele Record of the 4th year of Daoguang (1824), the Guang Zhong Fu Tian (Broadly Planting Blessing Fields) Stele Record of the 14th year of Daoguang (1834), the Newly Built Rain Corridor Stele Record of the 14th year of Daoguang, the Merit Stele Record of the 10th year of Xianfeng (1860), and the Zhongyuan Festival Stele Record of the 21st year of Guangxu (1895). There is also one contemporary Maintenance of Puzhao Temple Stele Record. Connecting the stories on the stone steles is the development history of Puzhao Temple: Abbot Yuanhui repaired and supplemented the Mahavira Hall, Wenchang Hall, and two corridors; later he again begged for alms to repair the temple and sculpt deity statues; Abbot Falin begged for alms to repair the temple and newly built the east and west corridors; a few years later he again begged for alms to newly sculpt three Great Buddhas and gild the Arhats. Abbot Chaofan organized a Zhongyuan Festival once. After reading these, you will suddenly marvel that such a deep and quiet small courtyard has condensed the efforts of so many predecessors.

projects.name: 河西普照寺
projects.address: 绵阳市江油市太平镇普照村南5米
projects.content_zh: 河西普照寺位于江油市太平镇平通河西岸，这一带汉代文化遗址众多，包括汉台、河西汉代崖墓群等。普照寺位于江油市城市与青莲镇之间，与云岩寺及太白故居等多个文物景点连成一线，具有重要文物价值。江油作为诗仙李白曾经居住的地方，自然少不了他四处云游留下的印记。天台国清寺，天下为四绝。今到普照游，到来复何别。楠木白云飞，高僧顶残雪。门外一条溪，几回流岁月正是他游览普照寺之后留下的诗篇。作为回应，普照寺山门楹联写道：寺古曾留唐寺迹，楼高恰映汉云台。另外这里还有李白夜读，神明为李白挂灯，莹莹朗朗，光照十里，故称天灯。李白别去，天灯即不复发光的神奇传说。从李白留诗的故事来看，普照寺可能初建于唐代，也可能更早。如今至少也有1300多年的历史。时至今日，寺内留存的古建筑仅存大雄宝殿，它建于明代，并留有一些明以前的遗风。屋面起坡平缓，原为九脊顶，现在九脊已经不复存在。室内有栩栩如生的彩雕云龙盘踞，精美华丽。在汶川地震之后，在对这座建筑的修复中专家们最大限度的使用了原有构件，保持了原汁原味。殿内遗存了不少有年头的古物塑像等，其中的一部分已是残损不全。比如高约2米、似整木雕刻的一座漆金造像，从其左袖上刀痕看，曾有人破坏性挑开辨真伪。这样的急功近利，浮躁浅薄不禁令人心痛。
projects.content_en: Hexi Puzhao Temple is located on the west bank of the Pingtong River, Taiping Town, Jiangyou City. This area has numerous Han dynasty cultural sites, including the Han Platform and the Hexi Han dynasty cliff tomb group. Puzhao Temple is located between Jiangyou City and Qinglian Town, forming a line with multiple cultural relic attractions such as Yunyan Temple and the Former Residence of Li Bai, with important cultural relic value. As the place where the Poet Immortal Li Bai once lived, Jiangyou naturally cannot lack the imprints he left during his travels everywhere. Tiantai Guoqing Temple, among the four finest under heaven. Today I visit Puzhao, what difference is there upon arrival. Nanmu trees and white clouds fly, eminent monks wear remnant snow on their heads. Outside the gate a stream flows, several times flowing through the years — this is precisely the poem he left after visiting Puzhao Temple. In response, the couplet on the Puzhao Temple mountain gate reads: The ancient temple once left traces of Tang temples; the tower height precisely reflects the Han Cloud Terrace. In addition, there is also a magical legend here: Li Bai studied at night, and the deity hung a lamp for Li Bai, bright and clear, illuminating for ten li, hence called Heavenly Lamp. After Li Bai left, the Heavenly Lamp no longer emitted light. Judging from the story of Li Bai leaving a poem, Puzhao Temple may have been first built in Tang dynasty, or even earlier. Today it has at least over 1,300 years of history. To this day, among the ancient buildings preserved in the temple, only the Mahavira Hall survives; it was built in Ming dynasty and retains some pre-Ming legacy.
