The scenery has passed, leaving only this building; if there is no people's attention and protection, all memories will, together with it, continue to sleep.

projects.name: 弹子石摩崖造像
projects.address: 南岸区弹子石街道德聚村1号
projects.content_zh: 元末明初，红巾军将领明玉珍统一全川，国号大夏，定都重庆。其时，传说长江岸边一座人头山有妖魔作怪，使得滩险浪急，船只时常触礁。为镇压妖魔，明玉珍命大将邹兴在长江南岸凿石刻像，保佑船只平安。这便是位于南岸区大佛鸿集村长江边上的临江大佛。明永乐十九年(1421年)这里又凿造了五尊佛。清代时，这里逐渐形成佛教寺院群落，气势恢宏。
projects.content_en: At the end of Yuan and beginning of Ming, Ming Yuzhen, a general of the Red Turban Army, unified all of Sichuan, with the state name Daxia, and made Chongqing the capital. At that time, legend has it that a demon was causing trouble at a Human-Head Mountain on the bank of the Yangtze River, making the shoals dangerous and waves rapid, with ships often hitting reefs. To suppress the demon, Ming Yuzhen ordered his great general Zou Xing to chisel stone statues on the south bank of the Yangtze River, to bless the safety of ships. This is the riverside Great Buddha located on the edge of the Yangtze River in Dafo Hongji Village, Nan'an District. In the 19th year of Yongle (1421), Ming, five more Buddha statues were chiseled here. During Qing dynasty, a Buddhist temple complex gradually formed here, with grand momentum.

projects.name: 塔子山文峰塔
projects.address: 江北区寸滩街道东北650米
projects.content_zh: 从前，取道水路坐船来的人，只要看见长江北岸塔子山上那个高耸挺拔的白塔，就知道重庆城到了。此白塔便是江北塔子山文峰塔，因为南山的黄桷垭文峰塔在先，所以它也被称为寸滩塔。它与黄桷垭文峰塔隔江遥相对峙，像一对兄弟镇守着重庆。据《重修文峰塔记》载，此塔建于清光绪十四年(1888年)，为六角七层空心楼阁式砖塔。塔身呈六角形，通高26.64米。塔壁厚1.2米。内阁七层，楼层已毁，逐层内收，各层开一窗，底层设门。除底层用条石砌成外，以上六层均为青砖所砌，每块砖上都有文峰塔三字，塔身存裂纹。门券刻大清光绪十四年戊子岁孟夏吉旦三里士民恭建等字样，门额匾刻繁体题名胜迹四字。塔子山文峰塔的左右各架起一座气势如虹的大桥——大佛寺大桥与朝天门大桥；长江、嘉陵江汇合处的重庆大剧院也可尽收眼底；远处，渝中半岛上拔地而起的高楼，用无法抗拒的现代化气息，改变着人们关于这座城市的记忆。幸好，这古塔仍在，静静地驻守着一段老城的回忆，使人们不致在城市的快速变化中迷失自己。
projects.content_en: In the past, people who came by boat via the water route, as soon as they saw the tall and upright White Pagoda on Tazi Mountain on the north bank of the Yangtze River, knew that Chongqing City had arrived. This White Pagoda is the Wenfeng Pagoda of Tazi Mountain in Jiangbei; because the Wenfeng Pagoda at Huangjueya on South Mountain came first, it is also called the Cuntan Pagoda. It faces the Wenfeng Pagoda at Huangjueya across the river from afar, like a pair of brothers guarding Chongqing. According to the Record of Rebuilding Wenfeng Pagoda, this pagoda was built in the 14th year of Guangxu (1888), Qing; it is a hexagonal seven-story hollow pavilion-style brick pagoda. The pagoda body is hexagonal, with a total height of 26.64m. The pagoda wall is 1.2m thick. The inner pavilion has seven stories; the floors have been destroyed, tapering inward layer by layer, each layer opens a window, and the bottom layer has a door. Except for the bottom layer built of dressed stones, the above six layers are all built of grey bricks; each brick has the three characters Wenfeng Pagoda on it, and the pagoda body has cracks. On the door arch are engraved characters such as Auspicious Day of Early Summer in the Wuzi Year, the 14th Year of Guangxu of the Great Qing, Respectfully Built by the Scholars and People of Three Li; on the door lintel plaque are engraved the four traditional characters of Title, Famous Scenic Spot. On the left and right of the Wenfeng Pagoda of Tazi Mountain, there are each spanned a bridge with imposing momentum like a rainbow — the Dafo Temple Bridge and the Chaotian Gate Bridge; the Chongqing Grand Theater at the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing Rivers can also be fully seen; in the distance, the high-rise buildings rising from the ground on the Yuzhong Peninsula, with an irresistible modern atmosphere, are changing people's memories about this city. Fortunately, this ancient pagoda is still here, quietly guarding a memory of the old city, so that people do not lose themselves in the rapid changes of the city.

projects.name: 觉林寺报恩塔
projects.address: 南岸区下浩觉林寺街95号
projects.content_zh: 报恩塔，又名下浩塔，位于南岸区下浩觉林寺街，是原觉林寺附属建筑。觉林寺建于南宋绍兴年间，明末毁于兵火，清康熙二年(1663年)僧雪痕复建，清乾隆二十二年(1757年)僧月江增建石塔、山门等。据《巴县志》记载，报恩塔是月江和尚为报母恩所建，但塔未成即圆寂，由其弟子善明续修，历16年完成。此塔为八角九层空心楼阁式砖石塔，坐南向北，通高45米。塔基每边长5.7米，前有垂带台阶2级。塔身逐层内收，各层挑檐，并开窗、开门，有佛龛，塔身内外有多处石刻题记。塔刹为攒尖葫芦宝顶，由金属铸成。围垣门是一座小牌坊，上书报恩塔三字，两旁柱刻因传心法分三教，为建浮屠报四恩对联。清代文人何彤云有一首《游览觉林寺》诗：一径入苍翠，寻幽来化城。小池鱼可唤，深树鸟无名。孤塔江中影，飞泉石上声。僧闲能导客，筇履尽情行。描写的便是100多年前的觉林寺。新中国成立后，此处先后兴办了新华皮鞋、新民塑料厂、合成纤维厂。为扩大厂址，佛祖菩萨塑像陆续被毁，所有亭阁殿堂面目全非，只剩下报恩塔一座旧迹。文革期间，原寺址全部改成厂房、职工宿舍和居民住宅，塔也遭到破坏。经1985年维修，目前保存状况较好，孤独地守望着这片曾经的神圣土地。
projects.content_en: Bao'en (Requiting Kindness) Pagoda, also called Xiahao Pagoda, is located on Juelin Temple Street, Xiahao, Nan'an District, and was an ancillary building of the original Juelin Temple. Juelin Temple was built during the Southern Song Shaoxing era, destroyed by war and fire at the end of Ming, rebuilt by Monk Xuehen in the 2nd year of Kangxi (1663), Qing, and with the stone pagoda and mountain gate added by Monk Yuejiang in the 22nd year of Qianlong (1757), Qing. According to the Ba County Annals, Bao'en Pagoda was built by Monk Yuejiang to requite his mother's kindness, but he passed away before the pagoda was completed; it was continued and finished by his disciple Shanming, taking 16 years to complete. This pagoda is an octagonal nine-story hollow pavilion-style brick-stone pagoda, facing south, with a total height of 45m. Each side of the pagoda base is 5.7m long, with 2垂带-style steps in front. The pagoda body tapers inward layer by layer, with each layer having overhanging eaves, and opening windows and doors, with Buddhist niches; there are many stone inscriptions inside and outside the pagoda body. The pagoda finial is a pyramidal gourd precious top, cast from metal. The enclosure gate is a small archway, with the three characters Bao'en Pagoda written on it; on the pillars on both sides are engraved the couplet Because transmitting the mind-dharma divides three teachings, to build a stupa requites four kindnesses. The Qing literatus He Tongyun has a poem Touring Juelin Temple: A path enters the verdant, seeking seclusion comes to the transformation city. Small pool fish can be called, deep trees birds have no name. Lonely pagoda shadow in the river, flying spring sound on stone. Monk idle can guide guests, staff and shoes walk to their heart's content. This describes Juelin Temple over 100 years ago. After the founding of New China, Xinhua Leather Shoes, Xinmin Plastic Factory, and Synthetic Fiber Factory were successively established here. To expand the factory site, the statues of Buddha and Bodhisattvas were successively destroyed, and all pavilions and halls were beyond recognition, leaving only the old trace of Bao'en Pagoda. During the Cultural Revolution, the original temple site was all converted into factory buildings, staff dormitories, and residential houses, and the pagoda was also damaged. After maintenance in 1985, it is currently in relatively good preservation condition, lonely watching over this once sacred land.

projects.name: 涂山寺
projects.address: 南岸区黄桷垭镇真武山15号
projects.content_zh: 涂山寺高踞涂山之侧，回龙桥之上，四周古树参天，苍翠欲滴。古往今来，涂山寺以名胜古刹闻名遐迩，朝山拜佛者和游客众多。唐代著名诗人白居易，在任忠州(今忠县)刺史时，来到此地，写下一首《涂山寺独游》：野径行无伴，僧房宿无期。涂山来路熟，唯是马蹄知。传说此地为远古时代涂山氏族所居之地。夏禹疏通九河时，到此娶涂山氏之女，四月后外出治水，三过家门而不入。古人为了纪念夏禹治水功绩，在涂山顶建禹王祠涂后祠，祠内壁有夏禹和涂后像。其后建为真武山，供奉真武祖师。明永乐十一年(1413年)贵州铁瓦寺道洪、正旭二僧来广化寺(今老君洞)任住持，随后将广化寺与真武山进行置换，真武山改为佛教寺庙。但因保持有道教的真武、祖师两殿，保留了真武寺的名称，山为真武山；又因与禹王祠旧址合并，又有涂山寺之称谓。整个庙分左右殿两部分，一为真武殿等属道教，一为大雄殿等属佛教，是佛道和睦共处的庙院。现存多为清代建筑，飞檐翘角，宏伟壮观。大雄殿又叫佛殿，供奉华严三圣。1954年后改为密宗布喇供奉宗喀巴，叫宗喀巴殿。殿前置有五尺长的大方形香炉一个、千斤重的大化钱炉一口，台阶上有石雕狮子一对，殿檐上悬国民革命陆军上将四川督军熊克武献立的大雄宝殿四个金字大匾一块。大殿为悬山顶，脊饰宝瓶，两端鱼吻，姿态活泼。1965年重庆市无线电一厂进驻庙内，把殿堂改为了车间或库房，1966年文革开始，庙内外碑记、石刻、佛像、雕塑、具有密宗布置特色的殿宇建筑、历史文物等悉被毁坏。1984年1月，地方政府贯彻落实宗教政策，将房产发还给涂山寺。1986年1月，经重庆市政府批准，修复开放涂山寺，经20余年修复，寺院面貌发生了很大变化，2000年列为重庆市文物保护单位，2014年列为国家级文物保护单位，继续吸引着善男信女与游人访客的到来。
projects.content_en: Tushan Temple perches high on the side of Tushan Mountain, above the Huilong Bridge, surrounded by ancient trees towering to the sky, verdant and dripping. Through the ages, Tushan Temple has been famous far and wide as a famous scenic ancient temple, with many mountain-worshipping Buddhists and tourists. The famous Tang poet Bai Juyi, when serving as the prefect of Zhongzhou (today's Zhongxian County), came to this place and wrote a poem Solo Tour of Tushan Temple: Wild path walks with no companion, monk room stays with no fixed date. Tushan Mountain coming road familiar, only the horse's hooves know. Legend has it that this place was the residence of the Tushan clan in ancient times. When Xia Yu dredged the nine rivers, he came here and married the daughter of the Tushan clan; after four months he went out to control floods, passing his home three times without entering. To commemorate Xia Yu's achievements in flood control, ancient people built the Yuwang Shrine and Tuhou Shrine on the top of Tushan Mountain, with statues of Xia Yu and Tuhou on the inner walls. Later it was built as Zhenwu Mountain, enshrining the Zhenwu Patriarch. In the 11th year of Yongle (1413), Ming, two monks Daohong and Zhengxu from the Iron Tile Temple in Guizhou came to Guanghua Temple (today's Laojun Cave) to serve as abbots, then exchanged Guanghua Temple with Zhenwu Mountain, and Zhenwu Mountain was converted to a Buddhist temple. But because it retained the two Daoist halls of Zhenwu and Patriarch, it retained the name Zhenwu Temple, and the mountain is Zhenwu Mountain; also because it merged with the old site of Yuwang Shrine, it also has the appellation Tushan Temple. The entire temple is divided into two parts, left and right halls: one is the Zhenwu Hall etc. belonging to Daoism, and one is the Daxiong (Mahavira) Hall etc. belonging to Buddhism — a temple where Buddhism and Daoism coexist harmoniously. Most of the existing buildings are Qing dynasty, with flying eaves and upturned corners, grand and spectacular. The Daxiong Hall is also called the Buddha Hall, enshrining the Three Sages of Huayan. After 1954 it was changed to the Tantric Bula enshrining Tsongkhapa, called the Tsongkhapa Hall. In front of the hall there is a five-chi-long square incense burner, a thousand-jin-large money-burning furnace, and a pair of stone-carved lions on the steps; on the hall eave hangs a large four-gold-character plaque of Daxiong Baodian (Mahavira Hall) presented and erected by Xiong Kewu, General of the National Revolutionary Army and Sichuan Military Governor. The main hall has an overhanging gable roof, with a precious vase on the ridge and fish-shaped ornaments at both ends, with lively postures. In 1965, Chongqing Radio Factory No. 1 moved into the temple, converting the halls into workshops or warehouses; in 1966, when the Cultural Revolution began, stele inscriptions, stone carvings, Buddha statues, sculptures, hall buildings with Tantric arrangement characteristics, and historical relics inside and outside the temple were all destroyed. In January 1984, the local government implemented the religious policy and returned the property to Tushan Temple. In January 1986, with the approval of the Chongqing Municipal Government, Tushan Temple was restored and opened; after over 20 years of restoration, the temple's appearance has undergone great changes. In 2000 it was listed as a Chongqing Municipal Cultural Relics Protection Unit, and in 2014 it was listed as a National Cultural Relics Protection Unit, continuing to attract devout men and women and tourists and visitors.

projects.name: 黄桷垭文峰塔
projects.address: 南岸区黄桷垭街道文峰峰山
projects.content_zh: 重庆主城区的人都听说过三塔不相见的说法。这三塔由北到南沿长江分布，分别是江北塔子山顶的文峰塔，下浩莲花山麓觉林寺中的报恩塔，以及南山上的黄桷垭文峰塔。前文已经介绍过另外两座古塔，下面，就让我们来认识这三塔的最后一塔。建成于清道光三十一年(1851年)的黄桷垭文峰塔是一座六角七层空心楼阁式砖塔，1986年、2008年有过两次维修。砖塔通高24米，素面条石塔基，每边长3.28米。塔身逐层内收，挑檐极富韵律，塔顶为六角攒尖葫芦顶。塔内一、二层楼道为石梯，三至七层为木梯，但目前文峰塔已经不对外开放，不能进入。真正使得黄桷垭文峰塔广为人知的是一部20世纪50年代的惊险小说《一双绣花鞋》。这个故事发生在解放初期的重庆，黄桷垭文峰塔在其中扮演了重要的角色。据其改编的电影、电视剧，都曾在文峰塔下取景拍摄。
projects.content_en: People in the main urban area of Chongqing have all heard of the saying that the three pagodas do not see each other. These three pagodas are distributed along the Yangtze River from north to south, respectively the Wenfeng Pagoda on the top of Tazi Mountain in Jiangbei, the Bao'en Pagoda in Juelin Temple at the foot of Lianhua Mountain in Xiahao, and the Wenfeng Pagoda of Huangjueya on South Mountain. The other two ancient pagodas have been introduced above; below, let us get to know the last of these three pagodas. The Wenfeng Pagoda of Huangjueya, built in the 31st year of Daoguang (1851), Qing, is a hexagonal seven-story hollow pavilion-style brick pagoda; it underwent two repairs in 1986 and 2008. The brick pagoda has a total height of 24m, with a plain dressed-stone pagoda base, each side 3.28m long. The pagoda body tapers inward layer by layer, with overhanging eaves full of rhythm; the pagoda top is a hexagonal pyramidal gourd top. Inside the pagoda, the corridors of the first and second layers are stone steps, and the third to seventh layers are wooden ladders; but currently the Wenfeng Pagoda is no longer open to the public and cannot be entered. What really made the Wenfeng Pagoda of Huangjueya widely known is a thriller novel of the 1950s, A Pair of Embroidered Shoes. This story took place in Chongqing in the early days of liberation, and the Wenfeng Pagoda of Huangjueya played an important role in it. The movies and TV series adapted from it have all shot scenes under the Wenfeng Pagoda.

projects.name: 宝轮寺正殿
projects.address: 沙坪坝区磁器口白岩山
projects.content_zh: 宝轮寺位于重庆沙坪坝区磁器口古镇，坐落于嘉陵江畔、白岩山(也叫白崖山)上。其始建年代有多种说法，有传说为唐朝时由尉迟恭主持修建，也有说是西魏年间(535—556年)所建，而官府所修的《巴县志》则称是宋真宗咸平年间(998—1003年)所建。宝轮寺因山而初名白岩寺(或白崖寺)，明朝时成帝朱允炆被朱棣篡位，避难于此，白岩寺遂易名为龙隐寺。清朝改为宝轮寺。寺院在鼎盛时期有殿宇16座，佛像372尊，可惜殿宇毁于明末战火，近代又经日寇轰炸，只留下大雄宝殿和紧邻其后的药师殿。重庆解放后办过校、住过居民，改革开放后政府拨款将其修缮，进行保护及重建工作，新建了川主殿、四面千手观音殿、天王殿、经楼和禅房等建筑。寺院于1988年对外开放，再续千年盛景。如今宝轮寺山门邻街，外面是热闹的磁器口古街，里边台阶之上是一块书有龙隐禅院的石牌坊，原物毁于明末战火，现在看到的是改革开放后仿制之物。寺庙正殿为大雄宝殿，为明宣德七年(1432年)所建，占地约400平方米。殿坐南向北，面阔三间、进深三间、高15米，重檐歇山琉璃瓦顶，屋顶脊饰轻盈起翘，檐下斗拱玲珑透漏，整体风格古朴精致。大殿为全木结构建筑，殿柱粗壮，两人也不能合抱。大雄宝殿牌匾上四个大字为著名书法家赵朴初所题。如今来此参拜的多为游览磁器口古镇的游客，虽然大殿前的香火台常年香火不断，但了解这里历史的人已经不多了。
projects.content_en: Baolun Temple is located in the ancient town of Ciqikou, Shapingba District, Chongqing, situated by the Jialing River and on Baiyan Mountain (also called Baiya Mountain). There are various sayings about its founding date; some legends say it was presided over and built by Yuchi Gong in Tang dynasty, some say it was built during the Western Wei period (535-556), while the officially compiled Ba County Annals say it was built during the Song Zhenzong Xianping era (998-1003). Baolun Temple was initially named Baiyan Temple (or Baiya Temple) after the mountain; in Ming dynasty, when Emperor Chengdi Zhu Yunwen was usurped by Zhu Di and took refuge here, Baiyan Temple was renamed Longyin (Dragon-Hidden) Temple. In Qing dynasty it was changed to Baolun Temple. In its heyday, the temple had 16 halls and 372 Buddha statues; unfortunately, the halls were destroyed in the war fires at the end of Ming, and in modern times it was bombed by the Japanese army, leaving only the Mahavira Hall and the Medicine Buddha Hall adjacent behind it. After Chongqing's liberation, schools were run and residents lived here; after the reform and opening up, the government allocated funds to repair it, carrying out protection and reconstruction work, newly building halls such as the Chuanzhu Hall, Four-Faced Thousand-Armed Guanyin Hall, Heavenly Kings Hall, scripture tower, and meditation rooms. The temple opened to the public in 1988, continuing its thousand-year prosperity. Today, the mountain gate of Baolun Temple is adjacent to the street; outside is the bustling Ciqikou ancient street, and inside above the steps is a stone archway inscribed with Longyin Chan Courtyard; the original was destroyed in the war fires at the end of Ming, and what is seen now is an imitation after the reform and opening up. The main hall of the temple is the Mahavira Hall, built in the 7th year of Xuande (1432), Ming, covering about 400 sq m. The hall faces south, 3 bays wide, 3 bays deep, 15m high, with double-eave xieshan glazed tile roof; the roof ridge ornaments are lightly upturned, and the bracket sets under the eaves are exquisite and openwork, with an overall style simple and refined. The main hall is an all-timber structure building; the hall columns are sturdy, and two people cannot wrap their arms around them. The four large characters on the plaque of the Mahavira Hall were inscribed by the famous calligrapher Zhao Puchu. Today, most of those who come to worship here are tourists visiting the ancient town of Ciqikou; although the incense burner in front of the main hall has constant incense year-round, not many people understand the history here.

projects.name: 盘溪无铭阙
projects.address: 江北区石马河盘溪香炉湾石门街道500米
projects.content_zh: 盘溪和嘉陵江交接的地方有一高丘，叫作香炉湾，这里有着重庆最为古老的石刻艺术品——无铭阙。因阙身无铭文，故名无铭阙，也称香炉石。建于东汉晚期，属墓阙。左阙早塌，残石存重庆中国三峡博物馆，现存右阙，坐东向西，通高4.15米。石阙分为阙基、阙身和仿木楼部三部分。阙基为单层实质，表面朴素。阙身为单一石块刻成，高2.26米，下宽1.15米，上宽0.80米，下部进深0.64米，上部进深0.54米。四角有隐柱形，左侧面刻有浮雕白虎衔璧，右侧面则是女娲捧月。上部仿木结构由四层构成，刻有护斗、枋子、角神鸳鸯交手拱等元素，形态丰富。文保机构于20世纪80年代已建亭保护阙，亭身较为封闭，慕名而来的人们只能从窗子外观看石阙。据附近居民介绍，这一带正大力开发房地产，可能会搬迁石阙进入新建好的小区内。
projects.content_en: At the place where Panxi meets the Jialing River there is a high hill called Xiangluwan (Incense Burner Bay), where there is Chongqing's oldest stone carving artwork — the Wuming (Uninscribed) Tower. Because the tower body has no inscription, it is named Wuming Tower, also called Incense Burner Stone. Built in the late Eastern Han, it belongs to a tomb tower. The left tower collapsed early, and the remnant stone is stored in the Chongqing China Three Gorges Museum; the existing right tower faces west, with a total height of 4.15m. The stone tower is divided into three parts: tower base, tower body, and imitation-timber section. The tower base is a single-layer solid mass, with a plain surface. The tower body is carved from a single stone block, 2.26m high, 1.15m wide at the bottom, 0.80m wide at the top, 0.64m deep at the lower part, and 0.54m deep at the upper part. At the four corners there are hidden column shapes; on the left side is carved a relief of a White Tiger holding a jade disk, and on the right side is Nüwa holding the moon. The upper imitation-timber structure consists of four layers, carved with elements such as bracket blocks, lintels, corner deities, and mandarin-duck hand-in-hand bracket sets, with rich forms. The cultural relic protection institution built a pavilion to protect the tower in the 1980s; the pavilion body is relatively enclosed, and people who come especially to see it can only view the stone tower from outside the window. According to nearby residents, this area is vigorously developing real estate, and the stone tower may be relocated into a newly built residential community.

projects.name: 华岩寺
projects.address: 九龙坡区华岩镇华岩村
projects.highlights: 华岩洞天、院落、寺内藏品、宗教文化
projects.content_zh: 华岩寺历史悠久，规模宏大，为西南十大丛林之一，有巴山灵境之称。始建于明万历二十七年(1599年)，后多次重修、扩修，现存建筑为清代遗构，由华岩洞、华岩寺、接引殿，以及北侧新建的七佛塔等独立院落组成，总建筑面积8280平方米，为重庆市内最大的佛教禅院。华岩洞庙又称小寺，为华岩寺之祖庙，位于南部。传说盛唐时期，有僧依岩结庵修行，名华严，久之讹称华岩。明万历及清同治两次重修，现存上、下两殿，依山崖而建，有着神秘的宗教氛围。清时圣可大师任住持，授徒传戒讲学，另于对面山地建设华岩寺，即今日的大寺。华岩寺坐北朝南，中轴线上分布有天王殿、大雄宝殿、圣祖可祖师堂、观音堂，两侧绕长廊。其中，大雄宝殿四根通天中柱每颗长达十几米，重数十吨，极为壮观。接引殿位于大寺东北侧，建于清道光五年(1825年)，坐西向东，四合院布局。中轴线上依次有放生池、牌坊、前殿(大门)、正殿(三圣殿)。牌坊上的石刻造像栩栩如生。
projects.content_en: Huayan Temple has a long history and large scale, being one of the Ten Great Monasteries in Southwest China, known as the Bashan Spiritual Realm. It was first built in the 27th year of Wanli (1599), Ming, and later rebuilt and expanded multiple times; the existing buildings are Qing dynasty surviving structures, composed of independent courtyards such as the Huayan Cave, Huayan Temple, Jieyin (Receiving and Guiding) Hall, and the newly built Seven-Buddha Pagoda on the north side, with a total building area of 8,280 sq m, making it the largest Buddhist monastery in Chongqing. The Huayan Cave Temple, also called the Small Temple, is the ancestral temple of Huayan Temple, located in the south. Legend has it that during the High Tang period, a monk built a thatched hut by the cliff for practice, named Huayan; over time it was mispronounced as Huayan. It was rebuilt twice in Ming Wanli and Qing Tongzhi; the existing upper and lower halls are built against the cliff, with a mysterious religious atmosphere. In Qing dynasty, Master Shengke served as abbot, teaching disciples, transmitting precepts, and giving lectures; he separately built Huayan Temple on the opposite mountain land, which is today's Great Temple. Huayan Temple faces south; on the central axis are distributed the Heavenly Kings Hall, Mahavira Hall, Shengzu Ke Patriarch Hall, and Guanyin Hall, with long corridors on both sides. Among them, the four sky-reaching central columns of the Mahavira Hall are each over ten meters long and weigh dozens of tons, extremely spectacular. The Jieyin Hall is located on the northeast side of the Great Temple, built in the 5th year of Daoguang (1825), Qing, facing east, with a siheyuan layout. On the central axis are sequentially the Free Life Pond, archway, front hall (main gate), and main hall (Three Sages Hall). The stone-carved statues on the archway are lifelike.

projects.name: 塔坪寺塔
projects.address: 北碚区静观镇塔坪村
projects.content_zh: 塔坪寺始建于南宋绍兴十六年(1146年)，原名小昆仑古藏寺。经明万历四十年(1612年)重修，改称塔坪寺。清嘉庆二十四年(1819年)后再次重修。布局沿袭中原唐以后已经失传的以塔为中心的格局，中轴线上依次排列山门、宋塔、大雄殿、藏经楼、后殿等建筑，结构古朴。寺中耸立的宋代石塔，享有朝天文笔插空稳，拔地楼阁依势牢的赞誉。石塔建于南宋乾道丁亥年(1167年)，为方形楼阁式砖结构空心塔，高14.4米，底边周长6.2米。塔身逐层内收，四角屋檐上挑。塔身四周有用各种彩色瓷片镶成而成的图案，内容为动物、花卉等，造型生动。塔内有17尊浮雕神像，以及历代游人留书，极为珍贵。塔中狭窄的斜式石梯上下连通，可助人登上塔顶远眺。寺内还存有明清石坊、清代铁塔、经幢、华表等文物。伴随其间的是遍布四处的参天古木与园林花草，它们给予寺院特有的清净氛围，亦成塔坪寺胜景之一。
projects.content_en: Taping Temple was first built in the 16th year of Shaoxing (1146), Southern Song, originally named Xiao Kunlun Ancient Cang Temple. After being rebuilt in the 40th year of Wanli (1612), Ming, it was renamed Taping Temple. It was rebuilt again after the 24th year of Jiaqing (1819), Qing. Its layout follows the pagoda-centered pattern that has been lost in the Central Plains after Tang; on the central axis are sequentially arranged the mountain gate, Song pagoda, Mahavira Hall, scripture tower, rear hall, and other buildings, with a simple and unsophisticated structure. The Song stone pagoda standing in the temple enjoys the praise of The heavenly writing brush pierces the sky steadily, the ground-pulled pavilion relies on the terrain firmly. The stone pagoda was built in the Dinghai year of Qiandao (1167), Southern Song; it is a square pavilion-style brick-structure hollow pagoda, 14.4m high, with a bottom perimeter of 6.2m. The pagoda body tapers inward layer by layer, with the four-corner eaves upturned. Around the pagoda body there are patterns inlaid with various colored porcelain pieces, with contents of animals, flowers and plants, etc., with vivid modeling. Inside the pagoda there are 17 relief deity statues, as well as inscriptions left by tourists of various dynasties, extremely precious. The narrow slanted stone steps inside the pagoda connect up and down, helping people climb to the top of the pagoda to look into the distance. The temple also preserves cultural relics such as Ming-Qing stone archways, Qing iron pagoda, stone pillars (jingchuang), and ornamental columns (huabiao). Accompanying them are towering ancient trees and garden flowers and plants spread everywhere; they give the temple its unique pure atmosphere, and also become one of the scenic spots of Taping Temple.

projects.name: 温泉寺
projects.address: 北碚区澄江镇北温泉内
projects.content_zh: 重庆以山城著称于世，也是俗称长江三大火炉之一。因夏季炎热，人们纷纷向郊外寻找清凉避暑之地，其中，北温泉便是人们的首选。北温泉人文景观众多，以温泉寺最负盛名。温泉寺创建于南朝刘宋景平元年(423年)，最初是缙云寺的下院，南齐中设东阳郡后，寺内香火兴旺，庙宇广大。后经北周武帝和唐武宗两次灭佛，遭受严重破坏。唐贞观时期重建庙宇，并在后山岩间刻摩崖佛像。北宋景德四年(1007年)，温泉寺受朝廷封赐为崇胜禅院。据说，南宋开庆元年(1259年)蒙哥大汗于钓鱼城被炮火击中，于此寺中病逝。此后，崇胜禅院因山岩崩塌而毁坏，明代迁现址重建。目前整个建筑群占地4200平方米，总建筑面积800余平方米。各殿宇依山而建，层层叠落，与自然环境和谐并存。寺内有四座殿堂为明代遗构，依次为关圣殿、接引殿、大佛殿、观音殿。关圣殿也是山门，面积137平方米，小青瓦单檐屋面，民居风格强烈。接引殿面积173平方米，抬梁式木构架，重檐歇山顶，琉璃瓦屋面。殿后有一山泉细流汇成的方池，池上石桥栏杆上刻有麒麟、芭蕉及花鸟等图案，皆为明代遗存。大佛殿面积200余平方米，重檐歇山顶，小青瓦屋面，装修华丽，脊饰精致。压轴的是观音殿，因其屋面为金属瓦盖，也称铁瓦殿，整体造型简洁古朴。四大殿周围有古香园、石刻园、观鱼池、乳花洞、五潭印月等景点。其中古香园为崇胜禅院旧址，园中植物繁茂，古木参天，存有宋、明、清三代僧人墓塔。石刻园内有宋、明、清等三代多处石碑，部分宋石刻极为珍贵。
projects.content_en: Chongqing is known to the world as a Mountain City, and is also commonly called one of the Three Great Furnaces along the Yangtze. Because of the hot summer, people go to the suburbs one after another to find cool summer retreats; among them, the North Hot Spring is people's first choice. The North Hot Spring has many cultural landscapes, with Wenquan (Hot Spring) Temple being the most famous. Wenquan Temple was founded in the 1st year of Jingping (423) of Liu Song, Southern Dynasties; originally it was the lower courtyard of Jinyun Temple. After Dongyang Commandery was established in the middle of Southern Qi, the temple's incense flourished and the temple buildings were vast. Later, after two Buddhist persecutions by Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou and Emperor Wuzong of Tang, it suffered severe damage. During the Tang Zhenguan era, the temple buildings were rebuilt, and cliffside Buddha statues were carved in the rocks of the back mountain. In the 4th year of Jingde (1007), Northern Song, Wenquan Temple was bestowed by the court as the Chongsheng Chan Courtyard. It is said that in the 1st year of Kaiqing (1259), Southern Song, the Great Khan Möngke was hit by cannon fire at Diaoyu City and died of illness in this temple. Thereafter, the Chongsheng Chan Courtyard was destroyed due to mountain rock collapse, and was rebuilt at the current site in Ming. At present, the entire building complex covers 4,200 sq m, with a total building area of over 800 sq m. Each hall is built according to the mountain, cascading layer by layer, coexisting harmoniously with the natural environment. There are four halls in the temple that are Ming dynasty surviving structures, sequentially the Guansheng (Holy Lord Guan) Hall, Jieyin (Receiving and Guiding) Hall, Dafo (Great Buddha) Hall, and Guanyin Hall. The Guansheng Hall is also the mountain gate, with an area of 137 sq m, small grey tile single-eave roof, with a strong folk-house style. The Jieyin Hall has an area of 173 sq m, with a抬梁式 (beam-lifting) timber frame, double-eave xieshan roof, and glazed tile roof. Behind the hall there is a square pool formed by a mountain spring trickle; on the stone bridge railings over the pool are carved patterns of qilin, banana, flowers and birds, etc., all Ming dynasty remains. The Dafo Hall has an area of over 200 sq m, with double-eave xieshan roof, small grey tile roof, ornate decoration, and exquisite ridge ornaments. The finale is the Guanyin Hall; because its roof is covered with metal tiles, it is also called the Iron Tile Hall, with an overall shape simple and unsophisticated. Around the four halls there are scenic spots such as the Ancient Fragrance Garden, Stone Carving Garden, Fish-Viewing Pond, Ruhua Cave, and Five Pools Reflecting the Moon. Among them, the Ancient Fragrance Garden is the old site of the Chongsheng Chan Courtyard; in the garden plants are luxuriant and ancient trees tower to the sky, preserving monk tomb pagodas of Song, Ming, and Qing dynasties. In the Stone Carving Garden there are many stone steles of Song, Ming, Qing and other dynasties, and some Song stone carvings are extremely precious.

projects.name: 缙云寺
projects.address: 北碚区缙云山
projects.highlights: 木结构、照壁、石牌坊、迦叶古佛
projects.content_zh: 缙云古名巴山，因山间常常白云缭绕，早晚间在阳光照射下呈现缤纷色彩，古人称赤多白少为缙，由此得名缙云山。位于山间的缙云寺始建于刘宋景平元年(423年)，后曾受到历代帝王封赐。唐名禅宫相思寺，宋改崇胜寺，明为崇教寺，明万历三十年(1602年)神宗皇帝改名为缙云寺，沿用至今。明末寺庙破败，清康熙二十二年(1683年)由破空大师重建。缙云寺占地面积2000平方米，坐西北向东南，现存山门、大雄殿、后殿、厢房等建筑。由于缙云寺为国内唯一的迦叶古佛道场，所以大雄殿里供奉的佛像不是释迦牟尼佛，而是迦叶古佛。该古佛立于康熙22年，高约两米，左右是大梵天、帝释天等清代塑像。缙云寺前有青石雕石照壁，高4.0米，宽4.0米，有专家认为是晚唐文物。石照壁正中为芭蕉麒麟图，图案古朴雅致。石照壁之上有一座石牌坊，高6米，宽5米，由青石砌成。坊正面刻有明神宗朱翊钧御笔迦叶道场，背面为明成祖朱棣所题缙云胜境。坊前有石雕青狮一对，高1.70米，形态勇猛威武。缙云云寺自古办学，名为缙云书院。1930年秋，中国佛教协会会长太虚法师在此创建世界佛学苑汉藏教理院，曾培养出如赵朴初等大批佛教人才，被誉为川东佛教圣地。缙云寺与温泉寺、绍隆寺、白云寺、石华寺、复兴寺、大隐寺、转龙寺并称缙云山八大寺庙。古寺名山，千年道场，至今仍然吸引大量游客观赏。
projects.content_en: Jinyun Mountain was anciently called Bashan Mountain; because white clouds often wind around the mountain, presenting colorful hues under sunlight in the morning and evening, ancient people called much red and little white as jin (red silk), hence the name Jinyun Mountain. Jinyun Temple, located in the mountains, was first built in the 1st year of Jingping (423) of Liu Song, and later received bestowals from emperors of various dynasties. In Tang it was named the Chan Palace Xiangsi (Lovesickness) Temple; in Song it was changed to Chongsheng Temple; in Ming it was Chongjiao Temple; in the 30th year of Wanli (1602), Ming, Emperor Shenzong renamed it Jinyun Temple, which is still used today. At the end of Ming the temple fell into disrepair; in the 22nd year of Kangxi (1683), Qing, it was rebuilt by Master Pokong. Jinyun Temple covers an area of 2,000 sq m, facing southeast from the northwest; the existing buildings include the mountain gate, Mahavira Hall, rear hall, and wing rooms. Because Jinyun Temple is the only ashram of the ancient Buddha Kasyapa in China, the Buddha statue enshrined in the Mahavira Hall is not Sakyamuni Buddha, but the ancient Buddha Kasyapa. This ancient Buddha was erected in the 22nd year of Kangxi, about 2m high, with Qing dynasty statues of Great Brahma, Indra, etc. on the left and right. In front of Jinyun Temple there is a bluestone-carved stone screen wall, 4.0m high and 4.0m wide; some experts believe it is a late Tang cultural relic. In the center of the stone screen wall is a Banana-Qilin pattern, with a simple and elegant design. Above the stone screen wall there is a stone archway, 6m high and 5m wide, built of bluestone. On the front of the archway is engraved the imperial brush of Emperor Shenzong Zhu Yijun of Ming: Kasyapa Ashram; on the back is inscribed Jinyun Scenic Realm by Emperor Chengzu Zhu Di of Ming. In front of the archway there is a pair of stone-carved blue lions, 1.70m high, with brave and mighty forms. Jinyun Temple has run schools since ancient times, named Jinyun Academy. In the autumn of 1930, the president of the Chinese Buddhist Association, Master Taixu, founded the Han-Tibetan Buddhist Institute of the World Buddhist Academy here, which trained a large number of Buddhist talents such as Zhao Puchu, and is known as the Buddhist Holy Land of Eastern Sichuan. Jinyun Temple, together with Wenquan Temple, Shaolong Temple, Baiyun Temple, Shihua Temple, Fuxing Temple, Dayin Temple, and Zhuanlong Temple, are called the Eight Great Temples of Jinyun Mountain. Ancient temple and famous mountain, a thousand-year ashram, still attracts a large number of tourists to visit today.

projects.name: 多功城
projects.address: 渝北区鸳鸯镇翠云街道花朝村西1公里
projects.content_zh: 提到重庆的古城堡，大家第一个想到的或许是钓鱼城。事实上，除了合川钓鱼城外，南宋末年，川渝地区还修建了江北多功城、泸州神臂岩、金堂云顶山、苍溪大获城、南充青居城、万县天生城等多座城池，形成一道三江八柱防御体系，共同抵御蒙古军的入侵。其中，重庆江北的翠云山作为战略要地，是南宋末年重庆军民坚持抗元斗争的重要据点，因为屡立战功，山上的城寨由朝廷赐名多功。据民国《江北厅志》载，该城建于南宋淳祐年间(1127—1278年)，清咸丰三年(1853年)曾补修。平面形状呈椭圆形，东西长70—100米、南北宽200米，占地面积约1.3万平方米。现存石砌城墙、石券东城门和西城门。城墙残长700米，厚3.7米，存高6米。西城门高2.8米，宽1.9米，进深3.7米。门洞呈双券拱状，券拱顶部条石上刻有南宋题记端明殿学士大中大夫四川安抚制置大使朱禩孙建。从西城门进城，即可看到翠云寺遗址。史料记载，翠云寺建于1021年，比多功城的历史还要早。不过，寺庙早已破败，铁门紧锁。抗战期间，不少的大学纷纷迁往重庆。多功城也被用作学校校址，即江北县女中部。曾有七八百学生在此就读，建有礼堂等建筑若干。今天大多建筑已然无存，仅留下古树若干，碧水一池，低声讲述古城数百年的故事。
projects.content_en: Mentioning Chongqing's ancient castles, the first thing everyone thinks of may be Diaoyu City. In fact, besides Diaoyu City in Hechuan, at the end of Southern Song, the Sichuan-Chongqing region also built many cities such as Duogong Town in Jiangbei, Shenbi Rock in Luzhou, Yunding Mountain in Jintang, Dahuocheng in Cangxi, Qingjucheng in Nanchong, and Tianshengcheng in Wanxian, forming a Three Rivers Eight Pillars defense system to jointly resist the invasion of the Mongol army. Among them, Cuiyun Mountain in Jiangbei, Chongqing, as a strategic location, was an important stronghold for Chongqing's military and civilians to persist in the struggle against the Yuan at the end of Southern Song; because of repeated meritorious service, the mountain fortress was bestowed the name Duogong (Many Merits) by the court. According to the Republic-era Jiangbei District Annals, this city was built during the Southern Song Chunyou era (1127-1278), and was repaired in the 3rd year of Xianfeng (1853), Qing. Its planar shape is elliptical, 70-100m long east-west, 200m wide north-south, covering an area of about 13,000 sq m. The existing stone city wall, stone-vaulted east city gate, and west city gate remain. The city wall has a remnant length of 700m, is 3.7m thick, and has a surviving height of 6m. The west city gate is 2.8m high, 1.9m wide, and 3.7m deep. The gate opening is in a double-vaulted arch shape; on the dressed stones at the top of the vault arch are engraved the Southern Song inscription: Built by Zhu Sisun, Duanming Hall Scholar, Grand Master of the Palace, Sichuan Pacification and Military Governor. Entering the city from the west gate, one can see the ruins of Cuiyun Temple. Historical records show that Cuiyun Temple was built in 1021, earlier than the history of Duogong Town. However, the temple has long been dilapidated, with its iron door locked. During the War of Resistance, many universities moved to Chongqing one after another. Duogong Town was also used as a school site, namely the Girls' Middle School Department of Jiangbei County. Once seven or eight hundred students studied here, with several buildings such as an auditorium built. Today most buildings no longer exist, leaving only several ancient trees and a pool of clear water, quietly telling the story of the ancient city for hundreds of years.

projects.name: 白帝城
projects.address: 奉节县白帝镇白帝村1社
projects.highlights: 诗词、三国文化、夔门景色、碑刻
projects.content_zh: 白帝城位于瞿塘峡西口的长江北岸，雄奇壮丽的自然景色和著名的历史典故让白帝城素来为诗家青睐。李白、杜甫、白居易、苏东坡等都曾登临白帝城，留下大量脍炙人口的诗篇。朝辞白帝彩云间，千里江陵一日还。两岸猿声啼不住，轻舟已过万重山。李白的这首诗奠定了许多孩子对于白帝城的第一印象。白帝城的历史可追溯到西汉末年。公孙述占据蜀地，自封为白帝，修筑白帝城，时为军政要塞。述死后，当地人建白帝庙祭奠他。三国时期，刘备兵败退守白帝城，在此建永安宫，于宫内托孤诸葛亮，这便是三国史上有名的白帝托孤。后因三国的故事广为流传，自明代之后逐渐形成了白帝庙内只祭祀蜀汉人物而不见白帝踪影的局面。如今白帝城的主要建筑就是白帝庙。占地面积约2600平方米，坐北朝南。传统合院式布局，由东、中、西三品院落组成。中轴线上依次排列着山门、托孤堂、明良殿等。明良殿始建于明代，采用抬梁式梁架，硬山顶，殿内供奉着刘、关、张和诸葛亮的彩色塑像。明良殿西侧为武侯祠，祠内供奉的是诸葛亮及其子孙的塑像，以感念诸葛家族对蜀所做的巨大贡献。武侯祠前有六角形观星亭，攒尖式屋顶。亭内的石桌、石墩上镌刻着唐代诗人杜甫在夔州写下的脍炙人口的诗篇《秋兴八首》，诗意浓厚。东西院建于清代，现内存有从隋至清的70多通碑刻，统称为碑林。其中不乏《龙山公墓志铭》《金轮寺舍利塔铭》等具有重要历史价值的隋代碑刻。无论是想雄霸天下的公孙述，还是怀着遗憾死去的刘备，又或是曾在此遇赦而心情大好的李白，都已化为了历史的尘埃。但如今站在这里，面对着眼前滔滔的江水和险峻的峭壁，仿佛能真切地感受到前人的无奈、痛苦或欢愉。
projects.content_en: Baidi (White Emperor) Town is located on the north bank of the Yangtze River at the west mouth of Qutang Gorge; its magnificent natural scenery and famous historical allusions have long made Baidi Town favored by poets. Li Bai, Du Fu, Bai Juyi, Su Dongpo, etc. all once climbed Baidi Town, leaving a large number of well-loved poems. Leaving at dawn from Baidi among colored clouds, a thousand li to Jiangling is returned in one day. The apes on both banks keep crying without stopping, the light boat has already passed ten thousand mountains. This poem by Li Bai established many children's first impression of Baidi Town. The history of Baidi Town can be traced back to the late Western Han. Gongsun Shu occupied the Shu region, proclaimed himself White Emperor, and built Baidi Town, which was then a military and political fortress. After Shu's death, locals built the White Emperor Temple to worship him. During the Three Kingdoms period, Liu Bei, after defeat, retreated to Baidi Town, built the Yong'an Palace here, and entrusted his orphan to Zhuge Liang inside the palace — this is the famous Baidi Orphan Entrustment in Three Kingdoms history. Later, because the Three Kingdoms story spread widely, after Ming dynasty a situation gradually formed where only Shu-Han figures were worshipped in the White Emperor Temple, with no trace of the White Emperor. Today the main building of Baidi Town is the White Emperor Temple. It covers an area of about 2,600 sq m, facing south. It has a traditional courtyard layout, composed of east, central, and west three courtyards. On the central axis are sequentially arranged the mountain gate, Orphan-Entrustment Hall, Mingliang Hall, etc. Mingliang Hall was first built in Ming, using a beam-lifting frame, with a flush gable roof; inside the hall are enshrined colored statues of Liu, Guan, Zhang, and Zhuge Liang. To the west of Mingliang Hall is the Wuhou (Marquis of Wu) Shrine, inside which are enshrined statues of Zhuge Liang and his descendants, to感念 the great contributions of the Zhuge family to Shu. In front of the Wuhou Shrine there is a hexagonal Star-Observing Pavilion, with a pyramidal roof. On the stone table and stone stools inside the pavilion are engraved the well-loved poem Eight Autumn Meditations written by the Tang poet Du Fu in Kuizhou, with strong poetic flavor. The east and west courtyards were built in Qing; currently they preserve over 70 stele carvings from Sui to Qing, collectively called the Stele Forest. Among them there are Sui dynasty steles with important historical value such as the Epitaph of Lord Longshan and the Relic Pagoda Inscription of Jinlun Temple. Whether it was Gongsun Shu who wanted to dominate the world, Liu Bei who died with regret, or Li Bai who was in a great mood after being pardoned here, they have all turned into the dust of history. But standing here today, facing the surging river water and the steep cliffs in front of us, as if one can truly feel the helplessness, pain, or joy of predecessors.

projects.name: 瞿塘峡摩崖题刻
projects.address: 奉节县瞿塘峡南岸白盐山西侧
projects.content_zh: 瞿塘峡全长八公里，是三峡中最短却最为雄伟的一个。尤其是西端入口处的夔门，两岸峭壁耸峙，中间宽不及百米，形同门户。杜甫曾有诗云：众水会涪万，瞿塘争一门。道出了夔门天下雄的气势。瞿塘峡北岸为赤甲山，南岸为白盐山，由于碳酸盐岩质附于岩壁表面，岩壁呈灰白色而得名。在白盐山西侧180余米长的岩壁上，排列着从南宋至民国时期的十三幅碑刻，皆为阴刻。这些碑刻同八百多年风云变幻的历史一样，内容十分丰富，字体也涉及楷、隶、草、篆等多种风格。其中最著名的是刻于南宋乾道七年(1171年)的《皇宋中兴圣德颂》，这是最早的一幅题刻。全文980字，记载了南宋高宗禅位于孝宗一事，赞颂了高宗的美德。楷书略带行草风味，是南宋著名书法家赵公硕的手迹。除了颂德之作，题刻中也不乏对夔门自然景观的赞美，如明代诗人沈庆的《赋瞿塘上峡》；有面对胜景生发的思古之幽情，如《白帝城怀古》；有从侧面反映近代军阀混乱争战史实的，如马林所书七律诗；还有表达抗日救国豪情的，如爱国将领冯玉祥将军的踏出夔巫，打走倭寇打出夔门去等。清代著名书法家刘心源所书夔门二字，古朴苍劲，别具一格；张伯翔所书瞿塘二字则秀润沉着，也是难得的书法精品。想着能得一叶扁舟，泛于江上，一边感受这自然峡谷的壮美，一边如欣赏这历代题刻，倘不尽意，靠岸登临，一探究竟，罢了再乘小舟同夕阳携手归去，任那一笔一捺的余味伴着云霞缭绕，必是人间一大美事啊！
projects.content_en: Qutang Gorge has a total length of 8 km, being the shortest but most magnificent of the Three Gorges. Especially at the west entrance, the Kuimen (Kuimen Gate), with steep cliffs towering on both banks, the middle is less than 100m wide, shaped like a gate. Du Fu once wrote a poem: All waters meet at Fu and Wan, Qutang contends for one gate. This expresses the momentum of Kuimen being the most majestic gate under heaven. The north bank of Qutang Gorge is Chijia Mountain, and the south bank is Baiyan (White Salt) Mountain; because carbonate rock material adheres to the cliff surface, the cliff is grayish-white, hence the name. On the over-180m-long cliff on the west side of Baiyan Mountain, thirteen stele carvings from Southern Song to Republic period are arranged, all in intaglio. These stele carvings, like the over 800 years of changing history, have very rich content, and the calligraphy styles also involve regular, clerical, cursive, seal, and other styles. Among them, the most famous is the Ode to the Holy Virtue of the Restoration of the Great Song, carved in the 7th year of Qiandao (1171), Southern Song, which is the earliest inscription. The full text has 980 characters, recording the abdication of Emperor Gaozong of Southern Song to Emperor Xiaozong, praising the virtues of Gaozong. The regular script has a slight running-cursive flavor, being the handwriting of the famous Southern Song calligrapher Zhao Gongshuo. Besides works praising virtue, the inscriptions also include praises of the natural landscape of Kuimen, such as the Ming poet Shen Qing's Ode to the Upper Gorge of Qutang; there are nostalgic feelings for the past aroused by facing the scenic beauty, such as Meditating on the Past at Baidi Town; there are those reflecting from the side the chaotic warfare history of modern warlords, such as the seven-character regulated poem written by Ma Lin; and there are those expressing the lofty sentiments of resisting Japan and saving the nation, such as the patriotic General Feng Yuxiang's Step out of Kui-Wu, Beat Away the Japanese Pirates and Go out through Kuimen, etc. The two characters Kuimen written by the famous Qing calligrapher Liu Xinyuan are simple, vigorous, and unique; the two characters Qutang written by Zhang Boxiang are elegant, moist, and composed, also being rare fine calligraphy works. Imagine getting a small boat, floating on the river, while feeling the magnificence of this natural gorge, while appreciating these inscriptions of various dynasties; if not fully satisfied, dock and climb to explore, then take the small boat back hand in hand with the setting sun, letting the lingering flavor of each stroke accompany the clouds and mist — it must be a great joy in the world!

projects.name: 磐石城
projects.address: 重庆市云阳县双江镇爱国村
projects.content_zh: 早在唐代，磐石城已是屯兵之处。唐代宗永泰元年(765年)，杜甫从成都举家东迁，途经云阳时曾作《将晓二首》，其中石城除击柝，铁锁欲开关。鼓角悲荒塞，星河落九天等诗句，描写的就是磐石城军营黎明时的景象。南宋淳祐年间，四川安抚处置使余阶率四川中路军民抵抗蒙古军入侵，他依照因山为垒，棋布星分的守备战略，在长江、嘉陵江沿线及一些交通要冲建造完善了15处寨堡，成为抗击蒙古大军的战略防御要点。磐石城是万州天生城防御体系的重要支点，由余阶部将吕师夔在此驻守，成功抗击蒙古军侵犯，使得磐石城名声大振。磐石城又名大石城，因为形如巨大磨盘，也称作磨盘寨。城外四面均为绝壁，唯独山顶地面平坦，总面积约3.5万平方米。磐石城有前后两寨门，前寨门在偏东方向，门前左方绝壁上镌有磐石城三个颜体大字，右方石壁上镌有清许缵曾的《磐石城记》，已斑驳不能辨认。寨门由巨石砌筑，厚重坚固，其上设有警楼、炮位等军事防御设施。后门形制与前门相同，寨门上锈迹斑驳的虎头铁环，造型相当凶猛威武。元代，寨中曾建有昙华寺。清雍正、乾隆年间，此地为私人所占，分属谭、柳二姓。乾隆五十四年(1789年)，涂怀安购得，在城中扩修寨墙，整修寨门，增设枪眼、炮洞。同时修建房屋数百间，将涂姓人家全部迁至寨上居住，使之成为涂氏一族聚居要塞。清末民初，名儒涂凤书于此修建祠堂，并作家谱，留有张作霖、阎锡山等民国名人的题序。今天磐石城中已无人居住，而是辟为景点，因其险要山势与雄奇建筑而成为云阳重要的旅游景点。
projects.content_en: As early as Tang dynasty, Panshi Fortress was already a place for stationing troops. In the 1st year of Yongtai (765) of Emperor Daizong of Tang, Du Fu moved his family east from Chengdu; when passing Yunyang he wrote Two Poems at the Approach of Dawn, among which verses such as The stone city removes the night watchman's clapper, the iron lock is about to open the gate. Drums and horns mourn the desolate frontier, the stars and river fall from the ninth heaven describe the scene at dawn of the Panshi Fortress military camp. During the Southern Song Chunyou era, Yu Jie, the Sichuan Pacification and Administration Commissioner, led the Sichuan Middle Route military and civilians to resist the Mongol army invasion; he followed the defense strategy of using mountains as fortresses, distributed like chess pieces and stars, and built and improved 15 fortresses along the Yangtze and Jialing Rivers and at some traffic hubs, becoming strategic defense points against the Mongol army. Panshi Fortress was an important fulcrum of the Tianshengcheng defense system in Wanzhou; it was garrisoned here by Yu Jie's subordinate general Lü Shikui, who successfully resisted the Mongol army's invasion, making Panshi Fortress's reputation soar. Panshi Fortress is also called Dashi (Great Stone) City; because it is shaped like a huge millstone, it is also called Mopan (Millstone) Fortress. Outside the fortress all four sides are sheer cliffs, only the mountaintop ground is flat, with a total area of about 35,000 sq m. Panshi Fortress has front and rear two fortress gates; the front fortress gate is in the偏 east direction; on the sheer cliff to the left in front of the gate are engraved the three large Yan-style characters Panshi City; on the stone wall to the right is engraved the Record of Panshi City by Xu Zanzeng of Qing, already mottled and unrecognizable. The fortress gate is built of huge stones, heavy and solid, on which are set military defense facilities such as watchtowers and artillery positions. The rear gate has the same shape as the front gate; the rusty tiger-head iron rings on the fortress gate have a quite fierce and mighty shape. In Yuan dynasty, the Tanhua Temple was once built in the fortress. During Qing Yongzheng and Qianlong eras, this place was privately occupied, belonging to the Tan and Liu surnames. In the 54th year of Qianlong (1789), Tu Huai'an purchased it, expanded and repaired the fortress wall in the city, renovated the fortress gate, and added gun holes and cannon holes. At the same time, hundreds of houses were built, and all the Tu surname people were moved to live on the fortress, making it a gathering fortress for the Tu clan. At the end of Qing and beginning of Republic, the famous scholar Tu Fengshu built an ancestral hall here and wrote a family genealogy, preserving prefaces by Republic-era celebrities such as Zhang Zuolin and Yan Xishan. Today no one lives in Panshi Fortress; it has been opened as a scenic spot, becoming an important tourist attraction in Yunyang due to its dangerous mountain terrain and magnificent architecture.

projects.name: 张桓侯庙
projects.address: 重庆市云阳县盘石镇龙宝村狮子岩下
projects.content_zh: 张飞，字益德，三国时期蜀汉名将。驻守阆中时闻关羽死讯，急令部将范疆、张达为兄报仇，不料反被暗害。二人取其首级投奔东吴，行至云阳，闻吴蜀讲和，便将其首级抛弃江中，为一渔翁捕鱼时打捞上岸，埋葬于飞凤山麓，世人在此立庙纪念。这便是最早的张飞庙，因为后主刘禅追谥其为桓侯，故也称张桓侯庙，但最广为人知的名称仍然是张飞庙。经宋、元、明、清历代扩建，张飞庙迄今已有1700多年历史，庙宇多为1870年水患后重建。因三峡工程建设，作为库区唯一一个远距离整体搬迁的文物单位，张飞庙闭馆拆迁，溯江而上30公里，由飞凤山搬迁至盘石镇龙安村。2003年7月19日搬旧如旧的新张飞庙正式开馆，与云阳新县城隔江相望，相映增辉。张飞庙充分利用地形地貌，依山而建，临江迎风。庙前石壁上刻江上风清四个大字，气势磅礴，天下闻名。庙内建筑主要有七座，其中正殿、旁殿、结义楼、望云轩、助风阁、得月亭和杜鹃亭为主要建筑。
projects.content_en: Zhang Fei, courtesy name Yide, was a famous general of Shu-Han during the Three Kingdoms period. When garrisoning Langzhong, upon hearing the news of Guan Yu's death, he urgently ordered his subordinates Fan Jiang and Zhang Da to avenge his brother; unexpectedly he was assassinated instead. The two took his head and defected to Eastern Wu; when reaching Yunyang, hearing that Wu and Shu had made peace, they threw his head into the river; it was salvaged ashore by a fisherman while fishing, and buried at the foot of Feifeng Mountain; people built a shrine here to commemorate him. This is the earliest Zhang Fei Temple; because the later lord Liu Shan posthumously honored him as Huanhou, it is also called Zhang Huanhou's Shrine, but the most widely known name remains Zhang Fei Temple. Through expansions in Song, Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties, Zhang Fei Temple has a history of over 1,700 years to date; most of the temple buildings were rebuilt after the flood disaster of 1870. Due to the construction of the Three Gorges Project, as the only cultural relic unit in the reservoir area to be relocated as a whole over a long distance, Zhang Fei Temple closed for demolition and relocation, going 30 km upstream, relocated from Feifeng Mountain to Long'an Village, Panshi Town. On July 19, 2003, the new Zhang Fei Temple, relocated as old as old, officially opened, facing the new Yunyang county town across the river, enhancing each other's splendor. Zhang Fei Temple fully utilizes the terrain and landforms, built against the mountain, facing the river and wind. On the stone wall in front of the temple are engraved the four large characters Clear Wind Above the River, with majestic momentum, famous under heaven. The temple mainly has seven buildings, among which the main hall, side hall, Sworn-Brotherhood Tower, Wangyun (Cloud-Gazing) Pavilion, Zhufeng (Wind-Assisting) Pavilion, Deyue (Moon-Gaining) Pavilion, and Dujuan (Cuckoo) Pavilion are the main buildings.

projects.name: 彭氏宗祠
projects.address: 重庆市云阳县里市乡黎明村
projects.content_zh: 彭氏宗祠又名彭家楼子，是渝东地区仅有的一座保存完整的晚清封建地主庄园。清乾隆中叶，湖北省武昌府大冶县水灾连连，当地人彭光奎听闻渝东一带十分富庶，便孤身入川，定居云阳，开设一家酿酒作坊，购得当地刘姓老屋。而后，其子彭宗义持家有道，在当地富甲一方。清道光二十五年(1845年)，家道中兴的彭氏家族大兴土木，开始修建彭氏宗祠，历时20年，于同治三年(1864年)建成。该祠坐西向东，占地3500平方米，建筑面积2561平方米，为封闭型城堡复式四合院布局，由前门厅、正门厅、享殿、戏楼、天井、城墙、围墙、厢房、箭楼及四角炮楼组成。院中心石木结构的九级楼阁通高37米，下部六层为石砌体，厚重朴实，上部为三重檐四角盔顶木构，轻巧灵动。整个建筑高耸宏大，兼具古朴与精巧，是极为少见的砖石木构混合建筑，是云阳县一心两翼的重点人文景观之一。彭氏宗祠是祠堂与坞堡结合的群体建筑，集祭祀、防护、住宿为一体，体现了移民氏族聚居建筑的独特性。祠内现存近代书画石刻13通。是研究晚清川东民居建筑风格和造型艺术的重要文物史料。
projects.content_en: Peng's Ancestral Hall, also called Peng Family Tower, is the only well-preserved late-Qing feudal landlord manor in the eastern Chongqing region. In the mid-Qianlong era of Qing, Daye County, Wuchang Prefecture, Hubei Province, suffered successive floods; local Peng Guangkui heard that the eastern Chongqing area was very prosperous, so he entered Sichuan alone, settled in Yunyang, opened a wine-making workshop, and purchased the old house of the local Liu surname. Later, his son Peng Zongyi managed the family well, becoming the richest in the area. In the 25th year of Daoguang (1845), Qing, the Peng family, with its family fortunes revived, undertook large-scale construction and began building Peng's Ancestral Hall, taking 20 years and completed in the 3rd year of Tongzhi (1864). This ancestral hall faces east, covering 3,500 sq m, with a building area of 2,561 sq m; it has a closed castle-type compound siheyuan layout, composed of the front gate hall, main gate hall, offering hall, theater tower, courtyard, city wall, enclosure wall, wing rooms, arrow tower, and four-corner gun towers. The nine-story pavilion of stone-timber structure in the center of the courtyard has a total height of 37m; the lower six stories are of stone masonry, heavy and plain, and the upper part is a triple-eave four-corner helmet-top timber structure, light and agile. The entire building is towering and grand, combining simplicity and exquisiteness; it is an extremely rare mixed brick-stone-timber building, and is one of the key cultural landscapes of the One Center Two Wings of Yunyang County. Peng's Ancestral Hall is a group building combining an ancestral hall and a fortress (wubao), integrating sacrifice, protection, and accommodation, reflecting the uniqueness of immigrant clan settlement architecture. Inside the hall there are 13 modern painting-calligraphy stone carvings preserved. It is important cultural relic material for studying the residential architectural style and plastic arts of eastern Sichuan in the late Qing.

projects.name: 天生城
projects.address: 万州区天城镇流水村
projects.type: 古战场遗址、城墙、石结构
projects.content_zh: 万州天生城又名天子城，与合川钓鱼城一样，同为南宋抗金遗址。但天生城这一名字却起源于三国，相传刘备伐吴时曾屯兵于此，故名天子城。南宋淳祐二年，余玠任四川安抚制置使时，迁万州州治于此，并借助山势修建堡垒，成为抵抗蒙古大军的坚固据点。后蒙军将其占领后并没有毁城，而是继续沿用。清朝初年，川东抗清三谭之一的谭宏也曾据守其上，足见天生城所具备的极高军事价值。天生城城垣位于海拔450米的山顶上，平面呈月牙形，由巨石砌筑，极为坚固。此山南北走向，长约1.5公里，山势险峻，东西均为绝壁，仅一条小路可从中通行。现存有石砌城墙三层，石阶梯数百级。第一道城门前，立有一牌，上书全民健身登山步道几个大字。往上攀登，一路上碰见许多老老少少、男男女女，一副不到山顶非好汉的架势，才知此言不虚。沿着石阶走到中段，城墙早已不见踪影，而是竹影森森，农田叠叠，屋舍交错，典型的山间农家景象。这是此山最宽、最平坦的一段。再往后走，道路渐窄，两旁峭壁渐露，又有了城墙遗迹。站在山顶俯瞰城区，江水，高楼，群山，和谐地交织在一起，这是长江旁的山城重庆特有的景色。往山下走，在后城门处偶遇一个拄拐的少女，沿着山路艰难地向上攀登。据文献记载，天生城内尚存宋代题刻多则和至元十三年(1276年)宣相杨公攻取万州之记碑一则。不知隐藏在何处，寻访未得见，估计有缘人才有幸一睹吧。
projects.content_en: Tiansheng (Heaven-Born) Fortress in Wanzhou is also called Tianzi (Son-of-Heaven) City; like Diaoyu City in Hechuan, it is likewise a Southern Song anti-Jin (anti-Mongol) site. But the name Tiansheng City originated from the Three Kingdoms; legend has it that when Liu Bei invaded Wu, he stationed troops here, hence the name Tianzi City. In the 2nd year of Chunyou, Southern Song, when Yu Jie served as Sichuan Pacification and Military Governor, he moved the Wanzhou prefectural seat here and built a fortress using the mountain terrain, becoming a strong point resisting the Mongol army. Later, after the Mongol army occupied it, they did not destroy the city but continued to use it. At the beginning of Qing, Tan Hong, one of the Three Tans resisting Qing in eastern Sichuan, also garrisoned and defended it, sufficient to show the extremely high military value of Tiansheng City. The city wall of Tiansheng City is located on the mountaintop at an altitude of 450m; its plane is crescent-shaped, built of huge stones, extremely solid. This mountain runs north-south, about 1.5 km long, with steep mountain terrain; both east and west are sheer cliffs, with only a small path passing through the middle. The existing remains include three layers of stone city wall and hundreds of stone steps. In front of the first city gate, there stands a sign with the large characters National Fitness Mountain-Climbing Trail. Climbing upward, along the way one meets many old and young, men and women, with an attitude of not being a true man until reaching the mountaintop, only then knowing this saying is not false. Walking along the stone steps to the middle section, the city wall has long disappeared; instead there are dense bamboo shadows, layered farmland, and interleaved houses — a typical mountain farmhouse scene. This is the widest and flattest section of this mountain. Walking further back, the road gradually narrows, and steep cliffs gradually appear on both sides, with city wall remains again. Standing on the mountaintop overlooking the city, the river water, high-rise buildings, and mountains are harmoniously intertwined — this is the unique scenery of the mountain city Chongqing beside the Yangtze River. Walking down the mountain, at the rear city gate one encounters a young girl on crutches,艰难地 climbing upward along the mountain road. According to literature records, inside Tiansheng City there remain many Song dynasty inscriptions and a stele of the Record of Lord Yang, Xuanxiang, Capturing Wanzhou in the 13th year of Zhiyuan (1276). It is unknown where they are hidden; a search did not find them, presumably only those with good fortune have the chance to catch a glimpse.

projects.name: 梁平文峰塔
projects.address: 梁平县双桂街道青竹村
projects.content_zh: 文峰塔位于梁平县双桂街道，共11层，高35.68米，是仅次于福建泉州石塔的全国第二高石塔。石塔始建于清道光七年(1827年)，初名文风塔，光绪年间进行过一次历时10年之久的维修，竣工后更名为文峰塔。清代徐名湘在《重建考棚并建塔记》一文中记载了文峰塔的来源。时有当地乡绅捐资修建考棚，剩余银两4700余两。后来大家商议后决定用这些银两在县城北门外修建高塔，搭配风水，并用于鼓励后学科甲蝉联，文章报国，当有理学名儒，继瞿唐先生而起，为梓里光者，文峰塔由此而来。文峰塔为楼阁式塔，用质地坚硬的青砂石精细叠砌而成，塔身逐层收分明显，整体呈锥状。塔基呈八边形，每边长4.71米。底层门两侧镌刻灵秀文明草书大字。各层错落开有拱形窗洞。最令人印象深刻的当属那起翘的檐角。每层八个角都高高向上翘起，为坚固沉稳的石塔增加了轻盈灵动之感。顶层檐角本来各挂有一个铜铃，今已不复存在。第十层正面刻有文峰二字，笔迹遒劲有力。塔顶攒尖，有宝珠刹。塔内原有的梯道被毁，后来修建了一到十层的木楼道供人攀登。关于文峰塔，后世百姓在不清楚其修建缘由的情况下，凭借着超凡的想象力流传过一些风水之说。原来梁平境内西山与四川大竹交界，西山山岭交错，似一狐狸。狐狸头朝东，尾朝西，嘴巴正好对着产粮的梁平大坝，不免有吃梁平面肥大竹的嫌疑。因此梁平人在此修建了高大的文峰塔，望它能撑住那贪吃的狐狸的嘴巴。这一民间笑谈生动地体现了文峰塔的雄伟形象，有几分意思。
projects.content_en: Wenfeng Pagoda is located in Shuanggui Subdistrict, Liangping County, with 11 stories and a height of 35.68m; it is the second tallest stone pagoda in the country, second only to the stone pagoda in Quanzhou, Fujian. The stone pagoda was first built in the 7th year of Daoguang (1827), Qing, initially named Wenfeng (Literary Style) Pagoda; during the Guangxu era it underwent a repair lasting 10 years, and after completion it was renamed Wenfeng (Literary Peak) Pagoda. The Qing scholar Xu Mingxiang recorded the origin of Wenfeng Pagoda in his article Record of Rebuilding the Examination Shed and Building the Pagoda. At that time, local gentry donated to build an examination shed, with over 4,700 taels of silver remaining. Later, after discussion, everyone decided to use this silver to build a high tower outside the north gate of the county seat, to complement fengshui, and to encourage later scholars to have consecutive examination successes, serve the country with their writings, and that there should be famous Neo-Confucian scholars rising after Mr. Qutang, bringing glory to their hometown — hence Wenfeng Pagoda. Wenfeng Pagoda is a pavilion-style pagoda, finely stacked and built of hard bluestone; the pagoda body has obvious tapering layer by layer, overall in a conical shape. The pagoda base is octagonal, each side 4.71m long. On both sides of the bottom-layer gate are engraved the large cursive characters Lingxiu (Spiritually Beautiful) and Wenming (Civilized). Each layer has arched window openings staggered. The most impressive are the upturned eave corners. Each layer's eight corners are all highly upturned, adding a light and agile feeling to the solid and steady stone pagoda. The top-layer eave corners originally each had a copper bell hanging, which no longer exist today. On the front of the 10th layer are engraved the two characters Wenfeng, with vigorous and powerful handwriting. The pagoda top is pyramidal, with a precious pearl finial. The original ladder inside the pagoda was destroyed; later, a wooden staircase from the 1st to 10th layer was built for people to climb. Regarding Wenfeng Pagoda, later generations of common people, without knowing the reason for its construction, spread some fengshui tales with extraordinary imagination. Originally, in Liangping, the West Mountain borders Dazhu, Sichuan; the West Mountain ridges are intertwined, resembling a fox. The fox head faces east, tail faces west, and its mouth is exactly facing the grain-producing Liangping Great Plain, inevitably suspected of eating Liangping and fattening Dazhu. Therefore, the people of Liangping built the tall Wenfeng Pagoda here, hoping it could prop open the mouth of that gluttonous fox. This folk joke vividly reflects the majestic image of Wenfeng Pagoda, somewhat interesting.

projects.name: 双桂堂
projects.address: 梁平县金带镇双桂村
projects.highlights: 禅宗文化、雕刻、彩绘、佛寺组图
projects.content_zh: 双桂堂由著名僧人破山创立于清顺治十年(1653年)，其名字起源于其内所植两株桂树。相传这两株桂树为嫦娥亲手栽培，在一个中秋之夜被送往人间，落在宁波天童寺院内。密云法师命弟子破山将这两株桂树带回蜀中，在桂树生根之处建寺传法。破山遵命入蜀，一日行至万竹山，半夜正打坐之时，忽见桂树已落地生根，霎时霞光万丈，异象丛生。于是破山便在这里建立禅院，取名双桂。想象力丰富的传说自然不可全信，但它体现的双桂堂在民间百姓心中的神圣地位却颇符合实际。破山禅师一生培育弟子一百余人，后来这些弟子分赴四川、云南、贵州、陕西乃至东南亚等地建寺传法，为西南地区汉传佛教的发展做出了重大贡献，双桂堂也因此有西南禅宗祖庭之称。它不是简单的寺庙，而是培养了一大批佛法传播者的大学堂。双桂堂规模颇大，建筑面积达1.1万平方米。合院式布局。沿着中轴线依次排列着关圣殿、放生池、弥勒殿、大雄宝殿、戒堂、破山塔、大悲殿、藏经楼等。放生池上两座石拱桥，雕刻精美。大雄宝殿建于清顺治十年(1653年)，气势恢宏，面阔五间、进深四间、三重檐歇山顶。石柱间挂满吊着穗儿的红色祈愿符，里面有虔诚的信客们最美好的愿望，散发出浓厚暖意，为庄严的大雄宝殿平添了几分人情味。离开轴线从侧门走出重重院落，在一片开阔地中这四方重檐、体量巨大的罗汉堂显得格外有震慑力。我正在犹豫是否进去时天空突然洒下一阵大雨，逼得我慌忙往里躲。刚进去便被惊了一跳——大大小小许多个彩绘罗汉列满了整个大厅，其中不乏瞠目怒视者，着实生动得吓人，我只得心惊肉跳地默求宽恕惊扰之罪了。双桂堂内长廊厢房与殿堂相连，花圃水池与天井相辅，于威严肃穆中透露出人世情怀，兼有重要的历史渊源，也难怪其香火不断、游人不绝了。
projects.content_en: Shuangguitang (Double-Osmanthus) Temple was founded by the famous monk Poshan in the 10th year of Shunzhi (1653), Qing; its name originates from the two osmanthus trees planted inside. Legend has it that these two osmanthus trees were personally cultivated by Chang'e (the Moon Goddess), and on one Mid-Autumn night were sent to the human world, landing in the courtyard of Tiantong Temple in Ningbo. Master Miyun ordered his disciple Poshan to bring these two osmanthus trees back to Shu (Sichuan), and to build a temple and transmit the Dharma where the osmanthus trees took root. Poshan obeyed the order and entered Shu; one day when he reached Wanzhu Mountain, in the middle of the night while sitting in meditation, he suddenly saw the osmanthus trees had landed and taken root, instantly with rays of auspicious light soaring to the sky and strange phenomena sprouting everywhere. So Poshan built a Chan monastery here, named Shuanggui (Double Osmanthus). The imaginative legend naturally cannot be fully believed, but the sacred status of Shuangguitang in the hearts of ordinary people that it reflects is quite in line with reality. Chan Master Poshan cultivated over a hundred disciples in his lifetime; later these disciples went separately to Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou, Shaanxi and even Southeast Asia to build temples and transmit the Dharma, making major contributions to the development of Han Chinese Buddhism in the Southwest region; hence Shuangguitang also has the title of Ancestral Hall of Chan Buddhism in the Southwest. It is not a simple temple, but a great academy that cultivated a large number of Dharma disseminators. Shuangguitang is quite large in scale, with a building area of 11,000 sq m. It has a courtyard layout. Along the central axis are sequentially arranged the Guansheng (Holy Lord Guan) Hall, Free Life Pond, Maitreya Hall, Mahavira Hall, Precept Hall, Poshan Pagoda, Great Compassion Hall, and Scripture Library. On the Free Life Pond there are two stone arch bridges, exquisitely carved. The Mahavira Hall was built in the 10th year of Shunzhi (1653), Qing, with imposing momentum, 5 bays wide, 4 bays deep, and triple-eave xieshan roof. Between the stone columns hang red prayer charms with tassels, containing the best wishes of devout believers, exuding a strong warmth, adding a touch of human warmth to the solemn Mahavira Hall. Leaving the central axis and walking out of the layers of courtyards through a side door, in an open area this four-sided double-eave, huge-volume Arhat Hall appears particularly imposing. I was hesitating whether to go in when the sky suddenly poured down a heavy rain, forcing me to hurriedly take shelter inside. Just as I entered I was startled — large and small many painted arhats filled the entire hall, among them there were no lack of those glaring with wide eyes, truly vivid and frightening; I had to, with a pounding heart, silently beg forgiveness for the sin of disturbing them. In Shuangguitang, long corridors and wing rooms are connected with the halls; flower beds, ponds, and courtyards complement each other; amidst majesty and solemnity it reveals human feelings, and it also has important historical origins — no wonder its incense is constant and tourists are endless.

projects.name: 石宝寨
projects.address: 忠县石宝镇西60米玉印山
projects.highlights: 倚山楼阁、穿斗式结构、山水景致
projects.content_zh: 传说女娲补天时遗留下一块五彩石，落到了忠县境内。不过这石头并未幻化成公子哥，而是在距县城45公里处的长江北岸生了根，成为一座孤零零的山崖，人称石宝。明朝末年谭宏在此地结寨起义，自称武陵王，石宝因而成寨。石宝寨最初的建筑天子殿始建于明万历年间。自此以后，石宝寨几经改造扩建。清嘉庆二十四年(1819年)依傍崖壁建造了9层飞檐楼阁与山崖同高。咸丰四年(1854年)对最初的天子殿进行了扩建。20世纪50年代初，在清代9层楼阁的基础上于山巅加建3层，共合为12层，始成今日的模样。加建部分名为魁星阁，四角攒尖顶。寨中现存的建筑多为清代所建。12层楼阁是石宝寨最重要的建筑。它坐北朝南，靠山面水，通高56米，全木结构，形如楼阁式塔，是我国现存体积最大、层数最多的穿斗式木结构建筑。下九层楼阁高33.46米，有九重天的象征意义。阁内每层石壁上均有题刻，并有木楼梯盘旋而上。楼窗前有高6米多高的砖石结构山门，正面用陶瓷镶嵌有小蓬莱梯云直上等字样，辅以五龙捧圣哪吒闹海等浮雕故事，生动有趣。石宝山顶有一块平地，是天子殿(又名绀宇宫)的所在，为石宝寨的制高点。在此凭栏远眺，滔滔江流，孤帆远影，尽收眼底。受三峡工程蓄水影响，长江水面上升到寨门口，石宝寨从半岛变成了江中的一个孤岛，仅通过一架悬索桥与岸相接。寨下修建有一圈白色软堤。如今的石宝寨仿佛一个放大的盆景置于江中，十分奇特。
projects.content_en: Legend has it that when Nüwa mended the sky, she left behind a five-colored stone, which fell into the territory of Zhongxian County. However, this stone did not transform into a playboy; instead, it took root on the north bank of the Yangtze River 45 km from the county seat, becoming a lonely cliff, called Shibao (Stone Treasure). At the end of Ming, Tan Hong built a fortress and rose in rebellion here, proclaiming himself King of Wuling; hence Shibao became a fortress (zhai). The earliest building of Shibaozhai, the Tianzi (Son-of-Heaven) Hall, was first built during the Ming Wanli era. Since then, Shibaozhai has undergone several renovations and expansions. In the 24th year of Jiaqing (1819), Qing, a 9-story flying-eave pavilion was built against the cliff, equal in height to the cliff. In the 4th year of Xianfeng (1854), the original Tianzi Hall was expanded. In the early 1950s, on the basis of the Qing 9-story pavilion, 3 more stories were added on the mountain top, totaling 12 stories, becoming today's appearance. The added part is named Kuixing (Star of Literature) Pavilion, with a four-corner pyramidal roof. Most of the existing buildings in the fortress were built in Qing. The 12-story pavilion is the most important building of Shibaozhai. It faces south, backed by the mountain and facing the water, with a total height of 56m, all-timber structure, shaped like a pavilion-style pagoda; it is the largest-volume and most-story穿斗式 (column-and-tie) timber structure building existing in China. The lower nine stories of the pavilion are 33.46m high, with the symbolic meaning of Nine Heavens. On the stone wall of each story inside the pavilion there are inscriptions, and a wooden staircase spirals upward. In front of the pavilion window there is an over-6m-high brick-stone structure mountain gate; on the front are inlaid with ceramics the characters Small Penglai, Ladder Clouds Straight Up, etc., supplemented by relief stories such as Five Dragons Holding the Sage and Nezha Stirs the Sea, vivid and interesting. On the top of Shibao Mountain there is a flat ground, where the Tianzi Hall (also called Ganyu Palace) is located, being the highest point of Shibaozhai. Leaning on the railing and looking into the distance here, the surging river flow and lonely sail shadows are all in sight. Affected by the water storage of the Three Gorges Project, the Yangtze River water level rose to the fortress gate; Shibaozhai changed from a peninsula to an isolated island in the river, only connected to the shore through a suspension bridge. A circle of white soft embankment was built under the fortress. Today's Shibaozhai is like an enlarged bonsai placed in the river, very peculiar.

projects.name: 丁房阙和无铭阙
projects.address: 忠县忠州镇白公路24号白公祠内
projects.content_zh: 汉阙是汉代的一种表示威仪等级的纪念性建筑，有石质汉书之称。巴蜀一带的汉阙数量超过我国现存汉阙总数的二分之一，仅忠县一个县城就有乌杨阙、丁房阙、无铭阙等共五座汉阙。随着三峡水库的兴建，忠县老县城有将近三分之二被淹没，因此这些国宝也被迫迁移原址，其中丁房阙和无铭阙都迁进了白公祠内，并安置在同一处。丁房阙原本位于忠州镇人民路二巷，为双阙，高约7米。建于东汉，宋、明两代都曾有过修葺。关于其身份有不同的猜测，一说是墓阙，一说是巴王庙阙。东阙为母子阙(即紧邻的一大一小两阙)。每阙从下至上可划分为11层不同的结构，依次是阙基、阙身、刻画层、枋子层、介石层、斗拱层、腰檐、上枋子层、上介石层、上斗拱层、阙顶。阙身收分明显，显得瘦长而挺拔。阙正面刻有《巴国忠贞祠铭》，内侧刻《重修巴国忠贞祠铭》，背面刻清乾隆三十六年(1771年)题铭，内容均已难以辨认。刻画层正面有二只小兽口衔缠带的图案，其中一只已严重风化，形状已磨灭了；右侧浮雕有一乘鹿、一抱物的两个人。枋子层刻锯齿状枋头、角神、饕餮等。介石层与斗拱层由一块石头刻成，形制朴素。上斗拱层的正、背面刻有浮雕斗拱各二朵，一斗二升，两斗拱间刻着一个半开的小门，一个妇人探身而出，极富生活气息；侧面刻鸳鸯交手拱。阙顶盖是庑殿顶的形式，出檐较远。
projects.content_en: Han Que (Han dynasty gate towers) are a type of commemorative building of the Han dynasty indicating majesty and rank, known as the Stone Han Book. The number of Han Que in the Bashu (Sichuan) region exceeds half of the total existing Han Que in China; in Zhongxian County alone there are five Han Que including Wuyang Que, Dingfang Que, and Wuming Que. With the construction of the Three Gorges Reservoir, nearly two-thirds of the old county town of Zhongxian was submerged, so these national treasures were also forced to relocate from their original sites; among them, Dingfang Que and Wuming Que were both moved into the Bai Gong Shrine and placed at the same location. Dingfang Que was originally located in Lane 2, Renmin Road, Zhongzhou Town, as a pair of que, about 7m high. Built in Eastern Han, it was renovated in both Song and Ming dynasties. There are different speculations about its identity; one says it is a tomb que, another says it is the que of the Ba King Temple. The east que is a mother-son que (i.e., a large and a small que adjacent to each other). Each que can be divided from bottom to top into 11 different structural layers, sequentially: que base, que body, carving layer, lintel layer, stone-interlayer layer, bracket-set layer, waist eave, upper lintel layer, upper stone-interlayer layer, upper bracket-set layer, and que top. The que body has obvious tapering, appearing slender and upright. On the front of the que is engraved the Inscription of the Loyal and Chaste Shrine of the Ba State; on the inner side is engraved the Inscription of Rebuilding the Loyal and Chaste Shrine of the Ba State; on the back is engraved an inscription of the 36th year of Qianlong (1771), Qing, all contents already difficult to辨认. On the front of the carving layer there is a pattern of two small beasts with wrapped bands in their mouths; one of them has been severely weathered, its shape already worn away; on the right side are reliefs of two people, one riding a deer and one holding an object. The lintel layer is carved with serrated lintel heads, corner deities, taotie (gluttonous beast), etc. The stone-interlayer layer and bracket-set layer are carved from a single stone, with a simple shape. On the front and back of the upper bracket-set layer are carved two relief bracket sets each, one bucket with two capitals; between the two bracket sets is carved a half-open small door, with a woman leaning out, extremely rich in life atmosphere; on the side is carved a mandarin-duck hand-in-hand bracket set. The que top cover is in the form of a hip-and-gable (wudian) roof, with far-reaching eaves.

projects.name: 潼南大佛寺摩崖造像
projects.name_en: Cliffside Statues of Dafo Temple in Tongnan
projects.address: 潼南县梓潼镇石碾村
projects.highlights: 历代造像、龛窟、题刻、大佛阁
projects.content_zh: 大佛寺位于潼南县梓潼镇石碾村定明山下。始建于唐，称为南禅寺，宋代叫作定明院。后因在寺内依山凿成一座大佛，又改名为大佛寺。寺内有大佛阁、观音殿、玉皇殿、鉴亭等木构建筑，大多为清代所建。寺内的摩崖造像是隋唐至清代雕刻遗留下来的文物，内容与佛道两教有关，具有极高的历史研究价值。现存的128个龛窟和932尊造像分布在以大佛阁两旁长达一里左右的山崖峭壁上。其中最重要的是位于大佛阁内的金身坐佛像。寺内的山崖上刻有一则《皇宋创造石佛记》，从中我们得知该像是由佛道两教前后历时近300年共同凿刻而成的。唐咸通年间(843—860年)开凿了佛头，而后宋代道家按照佛首的比例续刻佛身，用了26年。大佛形体凿好后又浑身贴金，直到公元1152年才全部完成。佛像高18.43米，体型匀称，双目有神，为我国第一大金佛。后来在大佛外部倚靠山势修建了高七重的大佛阁，各层顶上均满铺琉璃瓦，檐角起翘，巍峨壮观。大佛阁是我国迄今为止保留不多的佛阁例证之一。大佛寺的东岩有隋代凿刻的道教造像，是重庆现存年代最久远的纪年造像。除了造像，岩壁上一个高8.85米的佛字也十分壮观。这个佛字书于清同治年间(1870年)，用笔刚劲有力。岩石经年累月因风雨冲刷形成的自然纹理，为其平添了几分沧桑之感。在大佛寺左侧的山崖上还有一处十分有趣的印记——从明代到民国七个不同年代的洪水标记线，由此可以清楚地看出历次涪江洪水的大小，也算是一份别样的史料贡献。
projects.content_en: Dafo (Great Buddha) Temple is located at the foot of Dingming Mountain, Shinian Village, Zitong Town, Tongnan County. It was first built in Tang, called Nanchan (Southern Chan) Temple, and in Song it was called Dingming Courtyard. Later, because a great Buddha was chiseled against the mountain inside the temple, it was renamed Dafo Temple. Inside the temple there are timber buildings such as the Great Buddha Pavilion, Guanyin Hall, Jade Emperor Hall, and Jian Pavilion, most of which were built in Qing. The cliffside statues inside the temple are cultural relics left by carving from Sui-Tang to Qing, with content related to both Buddhism and Daoism, having extremely high historical research value. The existing 128 niches and 932 statues are distributed on the cliff walls about one li long on both sides of the Great Buddha Pavilion. Among them, the most important is the gilded seated Buddha statue inside the Great Buddha Pavilion. On the mountain cliff inside the temple there is engraved a Record of the Great Song Creating the Stone Buddha, from which we learn that this statue was jointly chiseled by Buddhism and Daoism over a period of nearly 300 years. During the Tang Xiantong era (843-860), the Buddha head was chiseled; then Song Daoists continued to carve the Buddha body according to the proportion of the Buddha head, taking 26 years. After the Buddha form was chiseled, it was gilded all over, and it was not fully completed until 1152 AD. The Buddha statue is 18.43m high, with a well-proportioned body and spirited eyes, being the No.1 Great Gold Buddha in China. Later, outside the Great Buddha, a seven-story-high Great Buddha Pavilion was built against the mountain terrain; the tops of each layer are fully covered with glazed tiles, with upturned eave corners, towering and spectacular. The Great Buddha Pavilion is one of the few preserved examples of Buddha pavilions in China to date. On the east rock of Dafo Temple there are Daoist statues chiseled in Sui, being the oldest dated statues existing in Chongqing. Besides the statues, an 8.85m-high character Fo (Buddha) on the rock wall is also very spectacular. This Buddha character was written during the Qing Tongzhi era (1870), with vigorous and powerful brushwork. The natural texture formed by the rock over years of wind and rain erosion adds a touch of vicissitudes to it. On the cliff on the left side of Dafo Temple there is also a very interesting mark — flood marker lines from seven different eras from Ming to Republic, from which one can clearly see the magnitude of each Fujiang River flood, which can be regarded as a unique historical contribution.

projects.name: 独柏寺正殿
projects.address: 潼南县上和镇后沟村四社独柏小学内
projects.content_zh: 在潼南县东20公里的上和镇后沟村四社独柏小学内，保留着两座古老的木构建筑，它们就是独柏寺正殿和后殿。关于独柏寺的史料记载极少，仅在《潼南县志》上有一句话独柏寺始建于唐咸通三年(862年)，而民间的老百姓自有流传的说法。当地人认为这座寺庙与一尊叫作柏树菩萨的雕像有密切的关系。这尊雕像用一整根柏木雕刻而成，后人为了供奉它而修建了这座寺庙，也就顺理成章地给它取名独柏寺。独柏寺经唐、宋、元等各代维修改建，现在只剩下元代正殿与清代后殿(观音殿)。独柏寺正殿坐东北向西南，建在高0.55米的素面台基上，单檐歇山顶，抬梁式木结构。面阔三间，进深三间。正殿四周的檐面铺有二重椽，这一举措保证了屋面的出檐宽度。屋檐自中心向两边缓慢起翘，举折之比(比例：7.1:12.4)较小，坡度平缓。建筑用材较大，最大柱径为0.38米，高5米，给人坚实之感。斗拱的设置是整个建筑最值得称道之处。前檐下斗拱数量达10朵之多，朵朵构造精巧，造型美观，具有元代建筑的典型特征。据专家考证，独柏寺正殿是重庆境内年代最为久远的木构建筑。整座建筑古朴大方，初见觉得其貌不扬，但细观其阑额、普柏枋、圆形蜀柱、覆盖式柱础、殿内横梁彩绘等，便知这座看似普通的建筑其实具有很高的科学研究价值。独柏寺后殿建成于清代，面阔五间，硬山顶，同为抬梁式构架。梁上题有清康熙五十四年(1715年)修造记，昭示着它历经的悠久岁月。
projects.content_en: Inside Dubai Primary School, Group 4, Hougou Village, Shanghe Town, 20 km east of Tongnan County, there are preserved two ancient timber buildings — they are the main hall and rear hall of Dubai Temple. There are very few historical records about Dubai Temple; only one sentence in the Tongnan County Annals says Dubai Temple was first built in the 3rd year of Xiantong (862), Tang, while the common people have their own circulating sayings. Locals believe that this temple is closely related to a statue called the Cypress Tree Bodhisattva. This statue was carved from an entire cypress log; later generations built this temple to enshrine it, and naturally named it Dubai (Single Cypress) Temple. Dubai Temple underwent maintenance and reconstruction in Tang, Song, Yuan and other dynasties; now only the Yuan main hall and the Qing rear hall (Guanyin Hall) remain. The main hall of Dubai Temple faces southwest from the northeast, built on a 0.55m-high plain platform base, with single-eave xieshan roof and beam-lifting timber structure. It is 3 bays wide and 3 bays deep. Around the main hall, the eave surface is laid with double rafters; this measure ensures the eave projection width of the roof. The eaves slowly rise from the center to both sides, with a small举折 ratio (proportion: 7.1:12.4) and a gentle slope. The building materials are large; the maximum column diameter is 0.38m, 5m high, giving a solid feeling. The setting of bracket sets (dougong) is the most praiseworthy part of the entire building. There are as many as 10 bracket sets under the front eave, each exquisitely constructed and beautifully shaped, with typical features of Yuan architecture. According to expert research, the main hall of Dubai Temple is the oldest timber building within Chongqing. The entire building is simple and generous; at first glance it seems unremarkable, but a close look at its lan'e (architrave), pubai fang (plate), round shu zhu (short columns), covered-style column bases, and painted beams inside the hall reveals that this seemingly ordinary building actually has high scientific research value. The rear hall of Dubai Temple was built in Qing, 5 bays wide, with flush gable roof, also of beam-lifting frame. On the beam there is an inscription of repair and construction in the 54th year of Kangxi (1715), Qing, indicating its long history.

projects.name: 龙兴寺正殿
projects.address: 潼南县小渡镇代场村六社
projects.content_zh: 若不是特地前来寻访，大概第一眼看见这个被荒山荒草包围的小房子的人，都会觉得它不过是个因被弃而荒废多年的乡间草庐。但对稍有点儿中国古建筑常识的人来说，那比普通民居高出一个等级的歇山顶却也露出一些端倪。这是明代的遗物。虽经历代改造修缮，但总体依然保留了明代特征。龙兴寺正殿始建于明天顺四年(1460年)，脊檩上题有大明天顺四年寅辰字样。坐北朝南，面阔三间19.1米，进深三间12.09米，高8.2米。1米高的台基将正殿从杂草中抬起。柱子和梁直接结合，没有斗拱。柱顶也没有卷杀和侧脚等做法。梁架中的联系构件以横向为主，纵向较少。檩、垫板和枋子为一个整体。檐下的飞椽保证了可观的出檐宽度。殿身周围有四根擎檐柱，用于支撑大角梁，形成了0.85米宽的副阶周匝。殿内壁原有明代壁画4幅，可惜惨遭灰浆涂抹，已不可见。关于正殿的屋顶，据考察有被改造的痕迹。现有歇山顶的构件颜色、材质等与殿内梁架不同，并且在殿内屋架还可看到庑殿顶的构件由戗，由此判断原来的屋顶形式为单檐庑殿顶，不知为何被改为了歇山顶。而如今灰瓦歇山顶的正脊也被损毁，瓦间尽是枯黄的野草。龙兴寺正殿曾作为隆兴村小学的教室，内墙上仍保留着好好学习天天向上的标语。而在山墙的外面，愚公移山改造中国等豪言壮语也还清晰可见，这大概是最简单明了的历史印记了吧。
projects.content_en: If not specifically coming to visit, probably people who at first glance see this small house surrounded by barren mountains and weeds would all think it is nothing more than a countryside thatched hut abandoned and wasted for many years. But for those with a little knowledge of Chinese ancient architecture, the xieshan (overhanging gable) roof, one grade higher than ordinary folk houses, also reveals some clues. This is a relic of Ming. Although it has undergone reconstruction and repair through dynasties, overall it still retains Ming features. The main hall of Longxing Temple was first built in the 4th year of Tianshun (1460), Ming; on the ridge purlin is inscribed the characters Yinshen, 4th Year of Tianshun of the Great Ming. It faces south, 3 bays wide (19.1m), 3 bays deep (12.09m), 8.2m high. The 1m-high platform base lifts the main hall from the weeds. Columns and beams are directly combined, without bracket sets. There is also no entasis (juansha) or incline (cejiao) at the column tops. The connecting members in the beam frame are mainly horizontal, with fewer vertical ones. The purlin, backing board, and lintel are one whole. The flying rafters under the eave ensure a considerable eave projection width. Around the hall body there are four eave-supporting columns, used to support the large corner beams, forming a 0.85m-wide surrounding auxiliary eave (fujie zhouza). The inner walls of the hall originally had 4 Ming murals; unfortunately they were cruelly smeared with mortar and are no longer visible. Regarding the roof of the main hall, according to investigation there are traces of modification. The color and material of the existing xieshan roof components differ from the beam frame inside the hall, and in the interior roof frame one can still see the youqiang (diagonal beam) component of a wudian (hip) roof; from this it is judged that the original roof form was a single-eave wudian roof, which for unknown reason was changed to a xieshan roof. And now the main ridge of the grey-tile xieshan roof has also been damaged, with withered yellow weeds between the tiles. The main hall of Longxing Temple once served as the classroom of Longxing Village Primary School; on the inner walls there still remain the slogans Study Hard and Make Progress Every Day. And on the outside of the gable walls, heroic words such as The Foolish Old Man Removes the Mountains, Transforming China are still clearly visible — this is probably the simplest and clearest historical imprint.

projects.name: 涞滩二佛寺摩崖造像
projects.name_en: Cliffside Statues of Erfo Temple in Laitan
projects.address: 合川区涞滩镇二佛寺下殿
projects.content_zh: 涞滩古镇位于合川区东北部，宋代时已初具规模，现保留着清代瓮城等大量明清时代遗迹。古镇傍着流经合川的三江之一渠江，曾是个繁忙的码头。高低错落的小青瓦房，古朴典雅的青石小巷，别具风韵。涞滩二佛寺原名鹫峰禅寺，分为上下两寺，上寺居于鹫峰山顶，规模庞大，气势雄伟；下寺在山间，依山而建一重檐歇山式三层殿堂，名曰二佛殿。该寺在晚唐时期香火极盛。但自从南宋淳熙、嘉泰年间在下寺开凿了大批摩崖造像后，造像的名声渐渐盛于寺庙本身。据说后因寺内石佛曾居四川省第二，连名字都改为了二佛寺。摩崖造像分布在二佛殿内北、西、南三面崖壁上。有浮雕造像218龛，共计1676尊，规模可观。整个造像的核心部分——大型群雕释迦牟尼说法图位于北崖，体现的是禅宗不立文字，教外别传，直指人心，见性成佛的宗旨。主像是正中央的圆雕弥勒佛金身坐像。坐像高12.5米，头饰螺髻，双耳垂肩，双眼半睁，面部丰腴；着褒衣博带式袈裟，左手抚膝，作说法状。这就是当年仅次于乐山大佛的二佛。大佛旁侧侍阿难、迦叶、十菩萨等。后壁还有千佛、飞天等像。西崖禅宗六祖像壁刻有造像记一则，落款为皇宋淳熙丙午(1186年)季春。南崖也有两则淳熙年间的造像记。此外还有目连尊者、十六尊者、泗州大圣、达摩、须菩提和弥勒大士等像，各有特色。其中的达摩像最是与别处不同。达摩一贯以浓眉大眼、威猛异常的形象出现，而这里的达摩像却表情娴静，慈祥非凡，让人觉得可亲可近。无论是否有佛教的信仰，看完这些前人虔心雕刻的作品，心中多少怀有一丝敬畏和感念。若能因此种下些善的种子，那便是前人的大功德一件了。
projects.content_en: Laitan Ancient Town is located in the northeast of Hechuan District; it had already begun to take shape in Song, and now preserves a large number of Ming-Qing era relics such as the Qing barbican. The ancient town borders the Qujiang River, one of the three rivers flowing through Hechuan, and was once a busy wharf. The高低错落 small grey-tile houses and the simple and elegant bluestone alleys have a unique charm. Erfo (Second Buddha) Temple in Laitan was originally named Jiufeng Chan Temple, divided into upper and lower temples; the upper temple sits on the top of Jiufeng Mountain, with a large scale and imposing momentum; the lower temple is in the mountains, built against the mountain as a double-eave xieshan-style three-story hall, named the Second Buddha Hall. This temple had extremely flourishing incense in the late Tang period. But since large numbers of cliffside statues were chiseled in the lower temple during the Southern Song Chunxi and Jiatai eras, the reputation of the statues gradually surpassed that of the temple itself. It is said that later because the stone Buddha inside the temple once ranked second in Sichuan Province, even the name was changed to Erfo (Second Buddha) Temple. The cliffside statues are distributed on the north, west, and south cliff walls inside the Second Buddha Hall. There are 218 niches of relief statues, totaling 1,676 statues, with considerable scale. The core part of the entire statues — the large group carving of Sakyamuni Preaching the Dharma — is located on the north cliff, reflecting the Chan (Zen) sect's宗旨 of Not establishing written words, transmitting outside the teachings, pointing directly to the human heart, and seeing one's nature and becoming Buddha. The main statue is the round-carved Maitreya Buddha gilded seated statue in the exact center. The seated statue is 12.5m high, with spiral hair ornaments, long earlobes reaching the shoulders, half-open eyes, and a plump face; wearing a loose-robe and broad-sash style kasaya, with the left hand stroking the knee, in a preaching pose.
