This was the Second Buddha, second only to the Leshan Giant Buddha in those days. Beside the Great Buddha stand Ananda, Kasyapa, Ten Bodhisattvas, etc. On the back wall there are also images of Thousand Buddhas, flying apsaras, etc. On the west cliff, the wall carving of the Six Patriarchs of Chan has one statue inscription, dated to the late spring of the Bingwu year of Chunxi of the Great Song (1186). On the south cliff there are also two statue inscriptions from the Chunxi era. In addition there are images of Venerable Mulian, Sixteen Arhats, the Great Sage of Sizhou, Bodhidharma, Subhuti, and Maitreya, etc., each with its own characteristics. Among them, the Bodhidharma statue is most different from elsewhere. Bodhidharma has consistently appeared with thick eyebrows, big eyes, and an extraordinarily fierce image, but the Bodhidharma statue here has a serene expression, extraordinarily kind, making people feel approachable. Whether or not one has Buddhist faith, after seeing these works devoutly carved by predecessors, one's heart more or less harbors a trace of reverence and gratitude. If some seeds of goodness can thereby be planted, that would be a great merit of the predecessors.

projects.name: 净果寺
projects.address: 合川区古楼镇净果村
projects.content_zh: 古楼镇位于合川区西北部，嘉陵江穿境而过。以盛产枇杷而闻名。每年除了摘枇杷的时节会吸引大批嘴馋的游客外，其余时候并无太多喧嚣。而镇上最为安静的地方，应属古刹净果寺了。净果寺始建于北宋雍熙二年(985年)，明代时重修，清代维修，现存建筑均为明清时期所建。不知在这些建筑中间是否还能找到一些宋代的遗物。寺庙遵循传统的坐北朝南的四合院布局，占地3400平方米。中轴线上依次排列着天王殿、大雄宝殿和后殿，两侧有转轮经藏殿和观音殿。转轮经藏殿为歇山顶，脊檩上墨书大明正统捌年(1443年)……重立敬题。殿内原本有木质转轮藏一具，不幸毁于文革时期，只剩下铁轴座，座上铸大宋已丑乾道五年(1169年)十月二日甲申建立等字，现保存在区文管所内。大雄宝殿面阔三间、进深14.5米。重檐歇山顶，抬梁式梁架。檐下斗拱极多，足有21朵。正檩上有明永乐二年(1404年)年重修时追题的维宋朝雍熙贰年等字样。与明代重修时写下的小字相比，墙上歪歪扭扭的毛主席语录要抢镜得多。不过说不定正是这些语录让古老的寺庙在当时有了先进的标志而免于被摧毁呢。还有熟悉的团结、紧张、严肃、活泼几个大字，表明这地方曾经被征用做过学校。佛像背后的《纪念白求恩》文章还清晰可见。这些20世纪的纪念物早已与寺庙融为一体，不可分割了。净果寺因香火不盛而异常清静安宁，多亏寺里挂了不少鲜红的大灯笼，不然就该过于冷清了。
projects.content_en: Gulou Town is located in the northwest of Hechuan District, with the Jialing River passing through its territory. It is famous for producing loquats. Every year, except for the loquat-picking season which attracts large numbers of greedy tourists, there is not much noise at other times. And the quietest place in the town should be the ancient temple Jingguo Temple. Jingguo Temple was first built in the 2nd year of Yongxi (985), Northern Song; it was rebuilt in Ming and repaired in Qing; the existing buildings were all built in the Ming-Qing period. It is unknown whether some Song relics can still be found among these buildings. The temple follows the traditional north-facing-south siheyuan layout, covering 3,400 sq m. On the central axis are sequentially arranged the Heavenly Kings Hall, Mahavira Hall, and rear hall; on both sides are the Revolving Scripture Repository Hall and Guanyin Hall. The Revolving Scripture Repository Hall has a xieshan roof; on the ridge purlin is written in ink: The 8th Year of Zhengtong of the Great Ming (1443)... Re-erected and respectfully inscribed. Inside the hall there was originally one wooden revolving scripture repository, unfortunately destroyed during the Cultural Revolution, leaving only the iron axle base; on the base are cast characters such as Established on the甲申 day, the 2nd day of the 10th month, the 5th year of Qiandao of the Great Song (1169), now preserved in the district cultural relics management office. The Mahavira Hall is 3 bays wide and 14.5m deep. It has a double-eave xieshan roof and beam-lifting frame. There are extremely many bracket sets under the eave, as many as 21. On the main purlin there are characters such as In the 2nd year of Yongle (1404), Ming, when rebuilt, retrospectively inscribed: The 2nd year of Yongxi of the Great Song, etc. Compared with the small characters written during the Ming reconstruction, the crooked Chairman Mao quotations on the walls are much more eye-catching. But perhaps it was precisely these quotations that gave the ancient temple an advanced mark at that time and saved it from destruction. There are also the familiar large characters Unity, Tension, Seriousness, Liveliness, indicating that this place was once requisitioned as a school. The article In Memory of Norman Bethune behind the Buddha statue is still clearly visible. These 20th-century memorials have long since merged with the temple into one, inseparable. Jingguo Temple is exceptionally quiet and peaceful because its incense is not flourishing; thanks to the many bright red large lanterns hung in the temple, otherwise it would be too desolate.

projects.name: 钓鱼城
projects.address: 合川区合阳镇嘉陵江南岸钓鱼山上
projects.highlights: 战场遗址、摩崖造像、题刻
projects.content_zh: 在合川区合阳镇有一座钓鱼山，雄踞着嘉陵江、涪江、渠江三江交汇处，三面环水，乃兵家易守难攻之地。800年前的南宋朝廷显然也看到了这一点，于是才有了今天的钓鱼城。南宋淳祐二年(1242年)，为抵抗不断南侵的蒙古军队，时任四川制置使兼重庆府事余玠开始依山势建筑钓鱼城。此后直到祥兴二年(1279年)，在将近40年的时间里，钓鱼城历经大小战役200多次，是宋军的坚实堡垒，就连蒙古军队所向披靡的蒙哥大汗也丧命于此。钓鱼城因此有了上帝折鞭处的美誉。钓鱼城有内外城之分，均依山势地形而建。外城用条石垒砌，绵延近万米。内城约2500米，现存城墙的墙基都是宋代遗迹。在南北两侧各有一道一字墙，长度分别为1200米和2500米。城外嘉陵江边有水师码头遗址。从山下往上走，一处处遗迹依次出现在眼前，仿佛一幅巨大的抗战生活画卷在眼前缓缓展开。首先是城门，原本有九个，现尚存八个，均为石券门。始关门是进城经过的第一道关卡。规模最大的城门是位于城南第二道防线上的护国门，门洞上镌刻全蜀关键四字。城台上筑有重檐歇山顶城楼。当年钓鱼城军民在此出入都要借助栈道，今天还能看出遗留的栈道石穴。站在护国门上往下望，可见原一字墙遗址。不远处还有安置巨炮的炮台遗迹。继续往上，来到一处较为平坦的高地，只见地上有许多规则的圆形坑洞，这里便是九口锅遗迹。这是中国最早的兵工厂遗址。那些锅状的坑是当年守军碾磨硝、磺、木炭等配制火药的原料的碾盘。九口锅旁边是传说中神仙济世的远古遗迹钓鱼台和粮食加工场遗址。登上山顶，就是当年守军操练的校场和军营遗址了。校场为直径36米的圆形，七幢营房排列在正南边。这里的道路四通八达，便于军队在紧急时刻迅速出击。800年前的硝烟早已散去，钓鱼城也绝不仅仅是战场遗迹那么简单。而后的元、明、清及至民国，各个时期都在此留下了自己的印记。山崖上有历代摩崖造像和题刻数十处，其中包括晚唐时期的悬空卧佛；还有遍及整座山的宋代水井、清代建筑护国寺、忠义祠等。如今的钓鱼城更像是一个宋以来的文物宝库，只不过它本身肩负着更深的历史意义。痛苦的呻吟和胜利的欢呼都隐藏进大山里，也许化为一道辙痕、一个炮坑，等待着后人去发现。
projects.content_en: In Heyang Town, Hechuan District, there is a Diaoyu (Fishing) Mountain, towering at the confluence of the Jialing, Fu, and Qu three rivers, surrounded by water on three sides — a place easy to defend and difficult to attack for military strategists. The Southern Song court 800 years ago obviously also saw this point, hence today's Diaoyu Fortress. In the 2nd year of Chunyou (1242), Southern Song, to resist the constantly south-invading Mongol army, Yu Jie, then Sichuan Military Governor and concurrently Chongqing Prefect, began building Diaoyu Fortress according to the mountain terrain. Thereafter until the 2nd year of Xiangxing (1279), in nearly 40 years, Diaoyu Fortress experienced over 200 battles large and small, being a solid stronghold of the Song army; even the Great Khan Möngke, whom the Mongol army was invincible, lost his life here. Hence Diaoyu Fortress has the reputation of the Place Where God's Whip Was Broken. Diaoyu Fortress is divided into inner and outer cities, both built according to the mountain terrain. The outer city is built of dressed stones, stretching nearly 10,000m. The inner city is about 2,500m; the existing wall bases of the city wall are all Song relics. On the north and south sides there is each a one-character wall, with lengths of 1,200m and 2,500m respectively. Outside the city by the Jialing River there is a navy wharf ruin. Walking up from the foot of the mountain, ruins appear one after another before the eyes, as if a huge picture scroll of anti-war life slowly unfolds before the eyes. First are the city gates; originally there were nine, now eight still survive, all stone-vaulted gates. The Shiguan (Beginning-to-Close) Gate is the first checkpoint passed when entering the city. The largest city gate is the Huguo (Protecting the Nation) Gate located on the second defense line south of the city; on the gate opening are engraved the four characters Key to All of Shu. On the city gate platform is built a double-eave xieshan-roof gate tower. In those days, the military and civilians of Diaoyu Fortress had to use plank roads to enter and exit here; today one can still see the remaining plank-road stone holes. Standing on the Huguo Gate and looking down, one can see the original one-character wall ruin. Not far away there is also the artillery platform ruin for placing giant cannons. Continuing upward, one comes to a relatively flat highland, only to see many regular circular pits on the ground — this is the Nine Pots ruin. This is the earliest arsenal ruin in China. Those pot-shaped pits were the grinding discs for the garrison to grind raw materials for making gunpowder such as saltpeter, sulfur, and charcoal in those days. Beside the Nine Pots is the ancient ruin Diaoyu (Fishing) Terrace of legendary immortal salvation and the grain processing site ruin. Climbing to the mountaintop is the drill ground and military camp ruin where the garrison practiced in those days. The drill ground is circular with a diameter of 36m, with seven barracks arranged on the due south side. The roads here extend in all directions, facilitating the army to attack quickly in emergencies. The smoke of gunpowder 800 years ago has long dispersed, and Diaoyu Fortress is by no means simply a battlefield ruin. Later, Yuan, Ming, Qing and even Republic, each period left its own mark here. On the mountain cliffs there are dozens of cliffside statues and inscriptions of various dynasties, including the suspended reclining Buddha of the late Tang; there are also Song dynasty wells throughout the mountain, the Qing building Huguo Temple, Zhongyi (Loyalty and Righteousness) Shrine, etc. Today's Diaoyu Fortress is more like a treasure house of cultural relics since Song, except that it itself bears a deeper historical significance. Painful groans and victory cheers have all hidden into the great mountain, perhaps turning into a rut mark or a cannon pit, waiting for later generations to discover.

projects.name: 岩溪桥
projects.address: 合川区北郊嘉陵江西岸岩沟·地中海广场内
projects.content_zh: 岩溪桥位于合川区北郊嘉陵江西岸的岩溪河口上，原桥东3米外有一个摩崖《张氏建岩溪桥记》碑记。据碑记记载，该桥捐兴于庆元乙卯孟春。由此可知这座石桥建造于南宋庆元元年(1195年)，距今已有800多年历史。这座长21.5米、宽2.18米的单孔石拱桥连接着南北两岸。中央拱券形似半圆，矢高(拱顶到拱脚的高差)4.66米，净跨度5.6米，看上去比较丰满。拱石采用干式叠砌法。桥面上平铺石板，桥两侧无栏杆。桥身两端与河床上自然的石壁连成一个整体。西侧拱券中部有一个圆雕的鳞甲吸水兽。清道光年间(1827年)，曾经在老桥近旁修过一座新桥，因两桥高度一致，看起来似一个整体，所以一度有古今桥的说法。2011年，合川草街航电枢纽蓄水工程将要投入使用，岩溪桥所在的位置将被完全淹没，因此，不得不把这座在原地待了8个多世纪的古桥整体往上游方向移动了40米。同时，加固了桥基，桥身增加了石栏杆。但遗憾的是，原摩崖碑记已不见踪影，桥两端与自然石壁相连的结构也不复存在了。今天岩溪桥所在的地方已变成了一个地中海风格的婚纱拍摄基地和高档住宅区。包围在西餐厅、咖啡馆、现代雕塑和极具异国风情的植物之间，被拔了根的岩溪桥显得格外的落寞和虚弱。
projects.content_en: Yanxi Bridge is located at the mouth of Yanxi River on the west bank of the Jialing River in the northern suburb of Hechuan District; 3m east of the original bridge there was a cliffside stele inscription Record of the Zhang Family Building Yanxi Bridge. According to the stele inscription, this bridge was donated and initiated in the early spring of the Yimao year of Qingyuan. From this we know that this stone bridge was built in the 1st year of Qingyuan (1195), Southern Song, with a history of over 800 years to date. This single-arch stone bridge, 21.5m long and 2.18m wide, connects the north and south banks. The central arch券 resembles a semicircle, with a rise (height difference from arch top to arch springing) of 4.66m and a clear span of 5.6m, looking relatively plump. The arch stones use the dry stacking method. The bridge deck is paved with stone slabs, with no railings on both sides. Both ends of the bridge body are connected with the natural stone walls on the riverbed into one whole. In the middle of the west arch券 there is a round-carved scale-armored water-absorbing beast. During the Qing Daoguang era (1827), a new bridge was once built near the old bridge; because the two bridges had the same height and looked like one whole, there was for a time the saying of the Ancient-and-Modern Bridge. In 2011, the water storage project of the Caojie Navigation and Power Hub in Hechuan was about to be put into use, and the location of Yanxi Bridge would be completely submerged; therefore, this ancient bridge, which had stayed in place for over 8 centuries, had to be moved 40m upstream as a whole. At the same time, the bridge foundation was reinforced, and stone railings were added to the bridge body. But regrettably, the original cliffside stele inscription has disappeared, and the structure connecting both ends of the bridge with the natural stone walls no longer exists. Today, the place where Yanxi Bridge is located has become a Mediterranean-style wedding photography base and high-end residential area. Surrounded by Western restaurants, cafes, modern sculptures, and extremely exotic plants, the uprooted Yanxi Bridge appears particularly lonely and weak.

projects.name: 合川文峰塔
projects.address: 合川区合阳镇文峰古街
projects.content_zh: 城市发展与历史旧建筑保护之间似乎总是存在矛盾的，我们不止一次遗憾地看到许多珍贵的历史文物遗址在急功近利的城市建设中变成了建设用地，令人痛心。但是，合川应该算一个例外。作为重庆六大卫星城之一，合川近年来在新城建设的同时，对境内一大批历史文物也进行了建设性修缮，使文物在得以保存的基础上具有了更大的价值。文峰古街的建设就是一个比较成功的例子。文峰塔位于嘉陵江和涪江交汇处的河口，利用这良好的景观区位，围绕文峰塔顺势建起一条古色古香的文峰街，不仅使文峰塔免于陷在逼仄的高楼间的窘境，也为市民休闲观景打造了一个好去处，还吸引了大量游客，简直是一举三得，值得借鉴。文峰塔始建于清嘉庆十五年(1810年)，时为9层。道光十六年(1836年)，合州知州李宗沆又在原基础上加建4层，共13层，通高58米。因为塔身呈灰白色，当地人俗称其为白塔。石塔平面为八角形，密檐式，坐西南朝东北。底层塔门门额上浮雕有形态各异的八仙人物，上方悬挂书有文峰塔的石匾，下方为一石拱券。塔身逐级收分，呈锥状。各层门洞上均有门额，额上挂有更上一层欲罢不能俯瞰嘉涪等匾，这些字均是用青花碎瓷拼合而成的。黑色的塔檐采取叠涩出挑，塔刹为宝瓶顶。底层至11层的塔心是一个锥形实体，有石梯盘旋可至11层。每层塔心正面原来均有圆雕佛像，今已俱毁。登塔远眺，山光水色尽收眼底。文峰街的夜色极美。灯光将文峰塔通体照得晶莹剔透一般，周围仿古建筑的翘角飞檐也被灯光勾勒出漂亮的弧线。走到街边平台上，江风习习，可见江水荡漾，远山依稀，江上偶有一两星灯火摇晃，唤起人绵绵的情思，疑心是否闯进了谁的梦乡。
projects.content_en: There always seems to be a contradiction between urban development and the protection of historical old buildings; we have more than once regretfully seen many precious historical relic sites turned into construction land in quick-profit urban construction, heartbreaking. But Hechuan should be considered an exception. As one of the six satellite cities of Chongqing, in recent years Hechuan, while building new cities, has also carried out constructive repairs on a large number of historical relics within its territory, giving the relics greater value on the basis of being preserved. The construction of Wenfeng Ancient Street is a relatively successful example. Wenfeng Pagoda is located at the estuary where the Jialing and Fu rivers meet; utilizing this good landscape location, an antique Wenfeng Street was built顺势 around Wenfeng Pagoda, not only saving Wenfeng Pagoda from the dilemma of being trapped among cramped high-rise buildings, but also creating a good place for citizens to relax and view scenery, and attracting a large number of tourists — simply achieving three things at one stroke, worth learning from. Wenfeng Pagoda was first built in the 15th year of Jiaqing (1810), Qing, then with 9 stories. In the 16th year of Daoguang (1836), Li Zonghuang, the prefect of Hezhou, added 4 more stories on the original basis, totaling 13 stories, with a total height of 58m. Because the pagoda body is grayish-white, locals commonly call it the White Pagoda. The stone pagoda has an octagonal plane, of dense-eave style, facing northeast from the southwest. On the lintel of the bottom-layer pagoda gate are reliefs of the Eight Immortals with different forms; above hangs a stone plaque inscribed with Wenfeng Pagoda, and below is a stone arch券. The pagoda body tapers layer by layer, in a conical shape. Above the door openings of each layer there are door lintels, on which hang plaques such as One More Layer, Unable to Stop, Overlooking Jia and Fu, etc.; these characters are all assembled from broken blue-and-white porcelain pieces. The black pagoda eaves use corbelled projection, and the pagoda finial is a precious-vase top. The pagoda core from the bottom to the 11th layer is a conical solid mass, with stone steps spiraling up to the 11th layer. On the front of the pagoda core of each layer there were originally round-carved Buddha statues, now all destroyed. Climbing the pagoda and looking into the distance, mountain scenery and water views are all in sight. The night view of Wenfeng Street is extremely beautiful. Lights illuminate the entire Wenfeng Pagoda so that it appears crystal clear; the upturned corners and flying eaves of the surrounding antique buildings are also outlined by lights into beautiful arcs. Walking to the platform by the street, with the river breeze blowing gently, one can see the river water rippling, distant mountains faintly visible, and occasionally one or two star-like lights swaying on the river, evoking continuous tender feelings, and one suspects whether one has broken into someone's dreamland.

projects.name: 铜梁武庙
projects.address: 铜梁县巴川街道民主路2号·少云公园内
projects.content_zh: 来到铜梁，意外发现这里有很多邱少云的痕迹，才知道原来他是铜梁人。这让人多少有些欣喜，仿佛在一个陌生的地方找到了熟悉的东西。而我们要寻访的铜梁武庙正位于少云公园内的凤山上，山顶是邱少云烈士纪念馆。我们在当地人的指引下沿着石阶一路上山。没走多远，便在绿树掩映中发现一个显眼的金色琉璃顶，是它无疑了。武庙始建于明代，清同治六年(1867年)及20世纪80年代都有过修葺，庙内存同治年间重修碑记一则。传统合院式布局。现有天王殿、大雄宝殿、观音殿、厢房等。大门进去第一个是天王殿。天王殿位于0.8米高的台基上，东西垂带台阶各9级。面阔三间、进深五间，高7米。悬山顶，上铺灰瓦。穿斗式梁架结构。天王殿后面是大雄宝殿。面阔三间，进深四间，高13.5米。抬梁式梁架，共有七架梁。上为歇山琉璃顶，下有2米高的台基。80年代修缮时在台基正面加刻浮雕，分别以九龙壁姑苏城渔樵耕读天仙配等为主题，倒是令其生动不少。厢房面阔七间，进深三间，与天王殿一样为穿斗式梁架和悬山顶。最后面是观音阁，重檐歇山顶，虽也覆琉璃瓦，但明显要比大雄宝殿的琉璃顶粗劣得多，疑是后来加建的一座建筑。大雄宝殿右侧有一覆坡屋顶的二层小楼，走廊上悬挂着洗过的衣服，很明显有人在此居住。楼前有一块石照壁，刻二龙戏珠图案。上有几道明显的裂痕，似乎是碎后重新拼接上的，但总体十分完整。绕过石照壁，从侧门出了武庙，沿另一条路下山。回头望了一眼，发现那金色的琉璃顶在夕阳下熠熠生辉。
projects.content_en: Coming to Tongliang, we unexpectedly discovered many traces of Qiu Shaoyun here, only then learning that he was originally from Tongliang. This makes people somewhat delighted, as if finding something familiar in a strange place. And the Tongliang Wumiao (Emperor Guan's Temple) we want to visit is located on Fengshan Mountain inside Shaoyun Park; on the mountaintop is the Qiu Shaoyun Martyr Memorial Hall. Under the guidance of locals, we climbed up the mountain along the stone steps. Not far after walking, we spotted a conspicuous golden glazed roof among the green trees — it was undoubtedly it. Wumiao was first built in Ming; it was repaired in the 6th year of Tongzhi (1867), Qing, and in the 1980s; inside the temple there is one stele inscription of reconstruction during the Tongzhi era. It has a traditional courtyard layout. The existing buildings include the Heavenly Kings Hall, Mahavira Hall, Guanyin Hall, and wing rooms. The first one after entering the main gate is the Heavenly Kings Hall. The Heavenly Kings Hall is located on a 0.8m-high platform base, with 9垂带-style steps on the east and west each. It is 3 bays wide, 5 bays deep, 7m high. It has an overhanging gable roof, covered with grey tiles. It has a穿斗式 (column-and-tie) beam frame structure. Behind the Heavenly Kings Hall is the Mahavira Hall. It is 3 bays wide, 4 bays deep, 13.5m high. It has a beam-lifting frame, with a total of seven rafter beams. Above is a xieshan glazed roof, below is a 2m-high platform base. During the 1980s repair, reliefs were added on the front of the platform base, with themes such as Nine-Dragon Wall, Gusu City, Fisherman-Woodcutter-Farmer-Scholar, and Heavenly Match, which indeed make it much more vivid. The wing rooms are 7 bays wide and 3 bays deep, like the Heavenly Kings Hall with column-and-tie beam frame and overhanging gable roof. At the very back is the Guanyin Pavilion, with double-eave xieshan roof; although also covered with glazed tiles, it is obviously much cruder than the glazed roof of the Mahavira Hall, suspected to be a later-added building. On the right side of the Mahavira Hall there is a two-story small building with a sloped roof; washed clothes are hung on the corridor, obviously someone lives here. In front of the building there is a stone screen wall, carved with a Two Dragons Playing with a Pearl pattern. There are several obvious cracks on it, seemingly reassembled after being broken, but overall very complete. Bypassing the stone screen wall, we exited Wumiao through the side gate and went down the mountain along another road. Looking back, we found that golden glazed roof shining brilliantly in the setting sun.

projects.name: 铁佛寺
projects.address: 铜梁县巴川镇铁佛村
projects.content_zh: 在一条人车稀少的宽阔的大马路旁，是一个巨大的石砌高台，高台之上不是别的，正是铁佛寺的遗迹。铁佛寺始建于元至正年间(1341—1368年)，从明至清均有过不同程度的维修。四合院布局，坐北朝南，原建筑有山门、古塔、主殿、正殿、玉皇殿和东西厢房等。抗日战争时期，铜梁正谊中学曾迁来寺内多年。新中国成立后，这里又被改造成村小学，两侧的厢房分给百姓居住。这时寺内的佛像显得碍眼而多余，因此大部分被毁。文革时期，铁佛寺遭到更大破坏。玉皇殿连同殿内玉皇像、铁佛像遭火灾烧毁，主殿和古塔被毁，山门被改建成住房。经历多场浩劫后，现寺内仅存正殿和部分厢房，系典型的明代风格。正殿保存较为完整，高8.5米，面阔三间、进深三间，抬梁式梁架，歇山顶石件搭到厢房屋顶上。檐下共有斗拱28朵。前梁和次梁上分别题有皇清乾隆五年岁次庚申仲冬月和大清同治八年岁次己巳仲冬月维修记。殿内原先供奉西方三圣、文殊、普贤、十八罗汉等佛像，盘龙柱，顶上绘有西游记图集，均已被毁，令人惋惜。左厢房保存较好，右厢房仅剩下北山墙面的抬梁式构架和屋顶，其余部分为后来改建砖砌。正殿后面也有砖砌平房一座，可能是曾经的教室。就这么几座建筑，孤寂、冷清，却又高调地立在高台上。它们似乎想要说些什么，却欲言又止。语言和现实一样苍白。
projects.content_en: Beside a wide main road with few people and vehicles, there is a huge stone-built high platform; on top of the platform is none other than the ruins of Tiefo (Iron Buddha) Temple. Tiefo Temple was first built during the Yuan Zhizheng era (1341-1368), and underwent repairs of varying degrees from Ming to Qing. It has a siheyuan layout, facing south; the original buildings included the mountain gate, ancient pagoda, main hall, principal hall, Jade Emperor Hall, and east and west wing rooms, etc. During the War of Resistance against Japan, Tongliang Zhengyi Middle School once moved into the temple for many years. After the founding of New China, this place was converted into a village primary school, and the wing rooms on both sides were distributed to common people to live in. At this time, the Buddha statues inside the temple appeared obtrusive and redundant, so most were destroyed. During the Cultural Revolution, Tiefo Temple suffered even greater damage. The Jade Emperor Hall, together with the Jade Emperor statue and iron Buddha statue inside the hall, was destroyed by fire; the main hall and ancient pagoda were destroyed; the mountain gate was converted into housing. After multiple catastrophes, now only the principal hall and part of the wing rooms remain in the temple, of typical Ming style. The principal hall is relatively well preserved, 8.5m high, 3 bays wide, 3 bays deep, with beam-lifting frame; the xieshan-roof stone components rest on the wing room roofs. Under the eave there are a total of 28 bracket sets. On the front beam and secondary beam are respectively inscribed repair records of The Gengshen Year, the 5th Year of Qianlong of the Great Qing, Mid-Winter Month and The Jisi Year, the 8th Year of Tongzhi of the Great Qing, Mid-Winter Month. Inside the hall were originally enshrined Buddha statues such as the Three Sages of the West, Manjushri, Samantabhadra, and Eighteen Arhats, with coiled-dragon columns, and Journey to the West picture collections painted on the top, all have been destroyed, regrettable. The left wing room is relatively well preserved; the right wing room only has the beam-lifting frame and roof of the north mountain wall remaining, the rest was later rebuilt with bricks. Behind the principal hall there is also a brick one-story house, possibly a former classroom. Just these few buildings, lonely and desolate, yet standing high-profile on the high platform. They seem to want to say something, but hesitate to speak. Language is as pale as reality.

projects.name: 碑记桥
projects.address: 涪陵区马武镇蒲江办事处碑记村
projects.content_zh: 碑记桥为单孔石拱桥，始建于南宋绍熙五年(1194年)，清道光十年(1835年)补修，迄今已有约800年历史，过去是人们过往涪陵和南川的必经之地，是重庆现存最古老的、最大的一座石拱桥。原本无名，后因石碑记述修桥相关事宜而得名，但题有绍熙甲寅(1194)的碑记现已不存，只存有1996年乡民修桥身时立下的石碑。桥身南北走向，横跨东流溪河。桥长31.5米，宽5.32米，高7.7米。其石料普遍采用青石，表面呈人字形凿痕，利用原溪床基岩作桥基护底石，拱券条石为纵联砌置，箍以外圈。矢高6.6米，净跨9.9米，具有典型的宋代民间建桥工艺和风格。桥面以不规则的石板铺成，桥栏高0.35米，宽0.3米。碑记桥表现了古代劳动人民的智慧和才干，为探讨宋代桥梁建筑提供了极为珍贵的实物资料。曾经浩浩荡荡的蒲江只剩涓涓细流，800年的古桥被藤蔓缠绕若隐若现，但坚固牢实的桥墩、桥面、桥拱、桥栏，久经风吹雨打浪卷水冲，依然坚定地横卧在历史的长河上。
projects.content_en: Beiji (Stele-Inscription) Bridge is a single-arch stone bridge, first built in the 5th year of Shaoxi (1194), Southern Song, and repaired in the 10th year of Daoguang (1835), Qing; it has a history of about 800 years to date. In the past it was the only way for people to travel between Fuling and Nanchuan, and is the oldest and largest existing stone arch bridge in Chongqing. Originally nameless, it later got its name because a stone stele recorded matters related to building the bridge; but the stele inscription inscribed with Shaoxi Jiayin (1194) no longer exists now, only a stone stele erected by villagers when repairing the bridge body in 1996 remains. The bridge body runs north-south, spanning the Dongliuxi River. The bridge is 31.5m long, 5.32m wide, and 7.7m high. Its stone materials generally use bluestone, with herringbone chisel marks on the surface; the original stream bed bedrock is used as the bridge foundation bottom-protection stone; the arch券 dressed stones are laid in longitudinal connection, hooped with an outer ring. The rise is 6.6m, and the clear span is 9.9m, with typical Song folk bridge-building craftsmanship and style. The bridge deck is paved with irregular stone slabs; the bridge railing is 0.35m high and 0.3m wide. Beiji Bridge demonstrates the wisdom and talent of ancient working people, providing extremely precious physical material for discussing Song dynasty bridge architecture. The once mighty Pujiang River now only has a trickle; the 800-year-old ancient bridge is faintly visible wrapped in vines, but its solid and firm bridge piers, deck, arch, and railings, after long exposure to wind, rain, waves, and water, still firmly lie across the long river of history.

projects.name: 宝顶山摩崖造像
projects.address: 大足县宝顶镇
projects.content_zh: 与北山摩崖造像齐名的另一处大足石刻是位于大足县宝顶镇的宝顶山摩崖造像。不同于北山造像历经多个时代的凿刻，宝顶山的造像集中反映的是南宋时期的雕刻特点。宝顶山造像开凿于南宋淳熙六年(1179年)至淳祐九年(1249年)，由高僧赵智凤主持统一规划凿刻，是著名的密宗佛教道场。各造像之间衔接紧凑，排布合理，数以万计却毫不零乱，相反，组成一个有序的整体。在这整体之中，又有突出和侧重，其中大佛湾的造像最具价值。大佛湾山崖形似马蹄，长500多米，其上密集排布着30余幅巨型浮雕，雕刻工艺精湛，图文并茂，宛如一本有趣的连环画。而其中内容竟毫无雷同之处，让人不得不佩服前人的智慧和想象力。既是佛教道场，造像的题材必然要宣扬这一时期的佛教理念，各种反映佛经故事、教义精髓的群雕自然少不了。华严三圣像、千手观音像、释迦涅槃圣迹图、孔雀明王经变、六道轮回图等，不一而足。但与之前其他时期的佛教造像所不同的是，这里面还有不少反映民间生活、倡导忠孝仁义的雕塑，如父母恩重经变、养鸡女图等，造型生动，贴近生活，仿佛为我们展开了一幅丰富多彩的南宋社会生活画卷；又如大佛湾南岩的宝顶圆觉洞，佛像周围十分细致地雕刻了楼阁亭台、人物鸟兽、花草树木，将佛像放入十分写实的场景之中，给人亲切真实之感。宝顶山造像中有不少大型造像，均利用天然岩石镂空雕刻，因造型的需求会产生一些力学问题。工匠们以子之矛攻子之盾，巧用造型中的法器、飘带、配饰等对佛像整体进行平衡；又利用祥云、飞天华盖等对山顶排水问题进行了妥善处理。排水方面构思和设计最为周密的还属宝顶圆觉洞。山间的泉水经洞顶被引入洞中，顺着壁间的小沟流入雕塑的龙口，作喷水状吐出，再注入暗沟，流出洞外。此设计简直浑然天成，以致观者察觉不出雕琢痕迹。在大佛湾一旁，还有同样为名僧赵智凤南宋年间主持修建的密宗禅院圣寿寺，几经损毁，现有建筑为明清重建。寺庙规模宏大，沿山势布局，主要建筑有天王殿、玉皇殿、大雄宝殿、经殿、燃灯殿、维摩殿等。此外，始建于明的万岁楼重檐八角，屋角高跷，极为灵动。1999年，宝顶山摩崖造像与北山摩崖造像一起被联合国教科文组织列入《世界文化遗产名录》，其价值得到了更大范围的认可。近年来，国家组织对大佛湾千手观音像进行了全面修复，也得到社会各界广泛关注。
projects.content_en: Another Dazu Rock Carving as famous as the North Mountain cliffside statues is the Baoding Mountain cliffside statues located in Baoding Town, Dazu County. Unlike the North Mountain statues which were chiseled through multiple eras, the Baoding Mountain statues centrally reflect the carving characteristics of the Southern Song period. The Baoding Mountain statues were chiseled from the 6th year of Chunxi (1179) to the 9th year of Chunyou (1249), Southern Song, under the unified planning and chiseling presided over by the eminent monk Zhao Zhifeng; it is a famous Tantric Buddhist ashram. The statues connect compactly and are reasonably arranged; numbering in the tens of thousands yet not at all messy, on the contrary, they form an orderly whole. Within this whole, there are also highlights and emphases; among them, the statues of Dafo (Great Buddha) Bay are the most valuable. The cliff of Dafo Bay is shaped like a horseshoe, over 500m long, on which over 30 giant reliefs are densely arranged, with exquisite carving craftsmanship, combining pictures and texts, just like an interesting comic strip. And the contents among them are surprisingly without any duplication, making one have to admire the wisdom and imagination of predecessors. Since it is a Buddhist ashram, the themes of the statues must propagate the Buddhist concepts of this period; various group carvings reflecting Buddhist scripture stories and the essence of doctrines are naturally indispensable. The Three Sages of Huayan statue, Thousand-Armed Guanyin statue, Sakyamuni Nirvana Holy Trace picture, Peacock Ming King Sutra Illustration, Six Paths of Reincarnation picture, etc., are too numerous to list. But different from Buddhist statues of other previous periods, there are also many sculptures reflecting folk life and advocating loyalty, filial piety, benevolence, and righteousness, such as the Parents' Kindness Sutra Illustration and Chicken-Raising Woman picture, with vivid modeling, close to life, as if unfolding for us a rich and colorful picture scroll of Southern Song social life; another example is the Baoding Yuanjue (Perfect Enlightenment) Cave on the south rock of Dafo Bay, around the Buddha statues are very meticulously carved pavilions, towers, terraces, figures, birds, beasts, flowers, and trees, placing the Buddha statues in a very realistic scene, giving a亲切 and真实 feeling. Among the Baoding Mountain statues there are many large statues, all using natural rock for openwork carving; due to modeling needs, some mechanical problems arise. The craftsmen, using the spear to attack the shield, cleverly use the ritual implements, ribbons, and accessories in the modeling to balance the whole Buddha statue; they also use auspicious clouds, flying apsaras, and canopies to properly handle the mountaintop drainage problem. The most thoughtful in drainage conception and design is still the Baoding Yuanjue Cave. The mountain spring water is introduced into the cave through the cave top, flows along the small grooves on the wall into the dragon mouth of the sculpture, spurts out in a water-spraying shape, then is injected into a hidden ditch and flows out of the cave. This design is simply浑然天成, so that viewers cannot detect carving traces. Beside Dafo Bay, there is also the Tantric Chan monastery Shengshou (Holy Longevity) Temple, likewise presided over and built by the famous monk Zhao Zhifeng during the Southern Song era; after several destructions, the existing buildings were rebuilt in Ming-Qing. The temple is large in scale, laid out along the mountain terrain; the main buildings include the Heavenly Kings Hall, Jade Emperor Hall, Mahavira Hall, Scripture Hall, Burning-Lamp Hall, and Vimalakirti Hall, etc. In addition, the Wansui (Long-Live) Tower, first built in Ming, has double eaves and eight corners, with high-raised eave corners, extremely agile. In 1999, the Baoding Mountain cliffside statues, together with the North Mountain cliffside statues, were inscribed on the World Cultural Heritage List by UNESCO, and their value has been recognized on a larger scale. In recent years, the state organized a comprehensive restoration of the Thousand-Armed Guanyin statue in Dafo Bay, which has also received widespread attention from all sectors of society.

projects.name: 北山摩崖造像
projects.address: 大足县龙岗镇龙岗山
projects.highlights: 历代造像风格、雕刻技艺、转世塔
projects.content_zh: 提到北山摩崖造像大家可能感到十分陌生，但若说出大足石刻的名字，恐怕是无人不知，无人不晓。其实，北山摩崖造像就是大名鼎鼎的重庆大足石刻的重要部分，位于大足县城西北2公里的龙岗镇龙岗山上。造像始创于唐景福元年(892年)，创凿者为昌、普、渝、合四州都指挥使韦君靖，历经五代、北宋，直到南宋绍兴年间，共计250年才全部完成。各朝代雕刻风格明显，保存完好，完美地展现了这一时期我国石窟艺术风格的发展变化。造像分布在佛湾、营盘坡、观音坡、佛耳岩等处，其中以佛湾规模最为宏大。佛湾形似一牙新月，长达300米的崖面分为南北两段，龛窟密集，通编290号，共计4360余躯造像。南段多为晚唐、五代作品，北段多为两宋时期的作品。晚唐造像以观音、地藏、观音地藏合龛等居多，颇具盛唐风格——人物体态丰满端庄，气质浑厚，衣纹细腻，线条流畅；五代的造像则更小巧活泼一些，体态富于变化，呈现出由唐代向宋代过渡的特征。两宋时期的作品题材更为丰富多样，人物形象鲜明，比例匀称，体态优美，衣着华丽，极具生活气息。这一时期的佛教造像已具有明显的民族特征。最具代表性的是凿于公元1142年至1146年的第136号转轮经藏窟，被誉为中国石窟艺术皇冠上的一颗明珠。该窟中央是一个镂空的八角形转轮经藏，三面壁上对称分布着二十余尊造像。各造像神情体态生动无比，反映出鲜明的性格，如普贤菩萨的典雅，玉印观音的庄重，数珠手观音的文静……尊尊雕像神性掺杂着人性，令人感受到神佛的可爱之处，又心生敬意，真是奇妙无比。此外，佛湾的韦君靖碑蔡京碑古文孝经碑等碑文在给人以书法之美感的同时兼具重要的史料参考价值，十分珍贵。在宋代释迦多宝龛之上不远处有一座砖砌的多宝塔，为空心密檐式塔，平面呈八角形，建于南宋绍兴年间。塔的内外壁上镶嵌有一百多幅宋代雕刻。从塔心的通道拾级而上，登临塔顶，向下俯瞰，周围景色尽收眼底，这是与在各个窟间仰视佛像时的应接不暇完全不同的感受。
projects.content_en: Mentioning the North Mountain cliffside statues, everyone may feel quite unfamiliar; but if the name Dazu Rock Carvings is spoken, I am afraid no one does not know it. In fact, the North Mountain cliffside statues are an important part of the famous Dazu Rock Carvings in Chongqing, located on Longgang Mountain, Longgang Town, 2 km northwest of Dazu county town. The statues were first created in the 1st year of Jingfu (892), Tang; the founder was Wei Junjing, the Commander-in-Chief of the four prefectures of Chang, Pu, Yu, and He; through Five Dynasties and Northern Song, until the Southern Song Shaoxing era, it took a total of 250 years to fully complete. The carving styles of each dynasty are distinct and well preserved, perfectly showing the development and changes of Chinese grotto art style during this period. The statues are distributed in Fo Bay, Yingpan Slope, Guanyin Slope, Fo'er Rock, etc., among which Fo Bay is the largest in scale. Fo Bay is shaped like a crescent moon; the 300m-long cliff face is divided into north and south sections, with dense niches and caves, consecutively numbered 290, totaling over 4,360 statues. The south section is mostly works of late Tang and Five Dynasties, and the north section is mostly works of the Two Song periods. Late Tang statues are mostly Guanyin, Ksitigarbha, and combined Guanyin-Ksitigarbha niches, quite with the High Tang style — figures with plump and dignified postures, solid temperament, delicate garment patterns, and fluent lines; Five Dynasties statues are smaller and more lively, with postures full of variation, showing the transitional features from Tang to Song. Works of the Two Song period have richer and more diverse themes, with vivid figure images, well-proportioned ratios, graceful postures, and gorgeous clothing, extremely full of life atmosphere. Buddhist statues of this period already have obvious ethnic characteristics. The most representative is Cave No. 136, the Revolving Scripture Repository Cave, chiseled from 1142 to 1146 AD, known as a pearl on the crown of Chinese grotto art. In the center of this cave is an openwork octagonal revolving scripture repository; on the three walls are symmetrically distributed over twenty statues. Each statue has vivid expressions and postures, reflecting distinct personalities, such as the elegance of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, the dignity of the Jade-Seal Guanyin, the quietness of the Prayer-Beads-Hand Guanyin... each statue has divinity mixed with humanity, making people feel the loveliness of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and also心生 respect — truly奇妙无比. In addition, the inscriptions such as the Wei Junjing Stele, Cai Jing Stele, and Ancient Text Classic of Filial Piety Stele in Fo Bay, while giving people the beauty of calligraphy, also have important historical reference value, very precious. Not far above the Song Sakyamuni-Prabhutaratna niche there is a brick Duobao (Many Treasures) Pagoda, a hollow dense-eave style pagoda with an octagonal plane, built during the Southern Song Shaoxing era. On the inner and outer walls of the pagoda are inlaid over a hundred Song carvings. Climbing up step by step from the passage in the pagoda center, reaching the top of the pagoda and looking down, the surrounding scenery is all in sight — this is a completely different feeling from the overwhelming experience of looking up at Buddha statues between the various caves.

projects.name: 璧山文庙大成殿
projects.name_en: Dacheng Hall of Temple of Confucius in Bishan
projects.address: 璧山县璧城街道中山北路
projects.content_zh: 璧山文庙又名孔庙，南宋绍熙年间始建。据乾隆《璧山县志》记载，文庙曾经几易其址。最初文庙建在县城南门；明万历年间改建西门内，坐西朝东，毁于明朝末年；清康熙二十五年(1686年)在城南旧址重建，毁于雍正七年(1729年)；雍正十一年(1733年)又于西门内复建，也就是今天所在的地方。清咸丰四年(1854年)重建，经同治、光绪补修。如此反复之重建，倒是证明了儒家学派在历朝历代难以撼动的较高地位。大成殿是文庙的主体建筑，明代时为祭奠孔子所建，现存建筑为清代遗构。正殿高14米，位于双层素面石台基(高分别为1.2米和1.4米)之上，两侧分设台阶4级、7级。面阔五间16米，进深三间11米。明间设置6道六合门，次间3道，稍间有障水板，门窗上皆有雕花窗棂。大殿为抬梁式梁架，中檩上墨书咸丰四年甲寅四月二十九日谷旦。檐下斗拱密集，造型独特。屋顶为重檐歇山琉璃顶，顶上装饰用的戗脊、正脊、翼角及鸱吻等均用镂空的黄、绿色琉璃件砌筑，整体造型庄严大方。20世纪50年代起，璧山文庙一度作为璧山区公安局的办公场所使用，因此建筑得以躲过一些灾难，较完整地保存了形制。如今，大成殿内每周日下午都有川剧演出，殿前设几张竹木桌椅，常有人在此品茶论道，读书看报，文化气息十分浓厚，也算是不负历史上因庙设学之庙学传统了。
projects.content_en: Bishan Temple of Confucius, also called the Confucian Temple, was first built during the Southern Song Shaoxi era. According to the Qianlong-era Bishan County Annals, the Temple of Confucius changed its location several times. Originally the Temple of Confucius was built at the south gate of the county town; during the Ming Wanli era it was rebuilt inside the west gate, facing east, and was destroyed at the end of Ming; in the 25th year of Kangxi (1686), Qing, it was rebuilt at the old site south of the city, and was destroyed in the 7th year of Yongzheng (1729); in the 11th year of Yongzheng (1733) it was rebuilt again inside the west gate, which is where it is today. It was rebuilt in the 4th year of Xianfeng (1854), Qing, and repaired in Tongzhi and Guangxu. Such repeated reconstructions actually prove the high and unshakable status of the Confucian school in all dynasties. The Dacheng (Great Achievement) Hall is the main building of the Temple of Confucius; in Ming it was built to sacrifice to Confucius, and the existing building is a Qing surviving structure. The main hall is 14m high, located on a double-layer plain stone platform base (1.2m and 1.4m high respectively), with 4 and 7 steps on both sides respectively. It is 5 bays wide (16m) and 3 bays deep (11m). The central bay has 6 six-panel doors, the secondary bays have 3 each, and the side bays have water-blocking boards; the doors and windows all have carved window lattice. The main hall has a beam-lifting frame; on the middle purlin is written in ink: Auspicious Day, the 29th Day of the 4th Month, the Jiayin Year, the 4th Year of Xianfeng. The bracket sets under the eave are dense and uniquely shaped. The roof is a double-eave xieshan glazed roof; the decorative qiang ridges, main ridge, wing corners, and chiwen (owl-tail ornaments) on the roof are all built with openwork yellow and green glazed components, with an overall shape solemn and generous. From the 1950s, Bishan Temple of Confucius once served as the office space of the Bishan District Public Security Bureau, so the building managed to avoid some disasters and preserved its form relatively completely. Today, every Sunday afternoon there are Sichuan opera performances inside the Dacheng Hall; in front of the hall there are several bamboo-wood tables and chairs, and people often come here to taste tea and discuss the Way, read books and newspapers — the cultural atmosphere is very strong, which can be regarded as living up to the temple-school tradition of establishing schools because of temples in history.

projects.name: 朝元寺牌坊
projects.address: 璧山县梅江大兴镇朝元村
projects.highlights: 石仿木结构、石刻装饰、故事表现
projects.content_zh: 在大兴镇山间曾隐藏着一座建于明万历癸巳年(1593年)的古刹——朝元寺。据村里耄耋之年的老人回忆，他们小时候常在寺里玩耍流连，度过了许多快乐的时光。令人痛心惋惜的是，朝元寺的殿宇均毁于文革时期，如今只剩下两道牌坊承载着所有的过去。头道牌坊位于山门处，坐西北向东南，与朝元寺同年建成，为明代遗迹。牌坊共有四柱三间，高宽均为6米，重檐歇山顶，明间檐下刻有交错菱形纹饰。此牌坊最大的特点是它的斗拱，虽为石质，却是仿木结构。其中明间一共有6攒斗拱，左右次间各2攒，均为一斗三升形式。牌坊上还有莲花瓣、鱼肠绣球、二龙戏珠、双狮、云凤等精美雕刻。牌坊当中立一匾额，上书欣国太平四个大字，落款为万历癸巳年孟冬吉旦立。经过头道牌坊往里走十余米，矗立着另一座清代牌坊。同为四柱三间，歇山顶，但比明代牌坊略大些，通高7米，宽6.8米。柱子两侧有抱鼓夹杆石。牌坊上依稀可见嘉庆四年(1799年)等字样，风化较为严重。坊面上的雕刻涉及多种题材，有戏曲人物、神话传说，民间生活，也有花卉鸟兽，诸如二龙戏珠、双狮戏球等，大大小小共计50余幅，丰富有趣。朝元寺虽毁，但周围的田间地头尚散落着许多破损的构件、雕像等。希望今后它们和这两座牌坊都能得到尊重，免于被再次伤害，甚至成为文献上的传说。
projects.content_en: In the mountains of Daxing Town there once hid an ancient temple built in the Ming Wanli Guisi year (1593) — Chaoyuan Temple. According to recollections of octogenarian elders in the village, when they were children they often played and lingered in the temple, spending many happy times. It is heartbreaking and regrettable that the halls of Chaoyuan Temple were all destroyed during the Cultural Revolution; today only two memorial archways carry all of the past. The first archway is located at the mountain gate, facing southeast from the northwest, built in the same year as Chaoyuan Temple, and is a Ming relic. The archway has a total of four columns and three bays, both height and width are 6m, with double-eave xieshan roof; under the eave of the central bay are carved interlaced diamond patterns. The biggest feature of this archway is its bracket sets; although of stone, they imitate timber structure. Among them, the central bay has a total of 6 clusters of bracket sets, and the left and right secondary bays have 2 clusters each, all in the one-bucket-three-capital form. On the archway there are also exquisite carvings such as lotus petals, fish-intestine silk balls, two dragons playing with a pearl, double lions, and cloud-phoenix. In the middle of the archway stands a horizontal plaque, inscribed with the four large characters Happy Country and Peaceful World, with the signature: Erected on an Auspicious Day in the Early Winter of the Wanli Guisi Year. Walking more than ten meters inward past the first archway, another Qing archway stands. Also with four columns and three bays and xieshan roof, but slightly larger than the Ming archway, with a total height of 7m and width of 6.8m. On both sides of the columns there are drum-shaped clamping stones. On the archway one can faintly see characters such as the 4th year of Jiaqing (1799), with relatively severe weathering. The carvings on the arch surface involve various themes, including opera figures, myths and legends, folk life, as well as flowers, birds, and beasts, such as two dragons playing with a pearl and double lions playing with a ball, totaling over 50 large and small, rich and interesting. Although Chaoyuan Temple was destroyed, many damaged components, statues, etc. are still scattered in the surrounding fields. It is hoped that in the future they and these two archways can all be respected,免于 being harmed again, or even becoming legends in literature.

projects.name: 何氏百岁坊
projects.address: 璧山县青杠街道石安村1组
projects.highlights: 石仿木结构、石刻装饰、故事表现
projects.content_zh: 清道光年间，璧山来凤有个周继盛，素爱行善。他的祖母何氏，即奉直大夫周绍熙之妻，在周家一生严守妇道，也常行善积德，备受人们尊重。于是周继盛在何氏年满百岁之时，即道光二十五年(1845年)，奏明朝廷，得圣旨恩准为祖母修建这座石牌坊，故称何氏百岁坊。何氏百岁坊本是来凤古驿道上三座牌坊中的第二座，因此当地人也称其为二道牌坊。可惜第一座和第三座牌坊均毁于文革时期，百岁坊能这么完整地保存下来实为幸事。何氏百岁坊为仿木结构的石牌坊，重檐庑殿式顶，四柱三间五楼。通高11米，宽7.88米。最上方有寿字火焰宝珠顶，檐脊上饰有鱼龙飞吻。牌坊上刻有狮子、白象、麒麟、蝙蝠等众多动物形象，明间正、背面的小额坊上题有旌表例赠奉直大夫周绍熙之妻何氏百岁坊，表明了此坊得圣上恩准的荣耀。小额坊上的匾额刻有周绍熙的历任官职和何氏百岁坊序。大额坊上浮雕有神话故事，故事里的人物姿态各异，栩栩如生。其两端立柱上本来凿有八尊戏装人物造像，如今只剩六尊。最上方的匾额正面刻升平人瑞，背面刻贞寿之门。整个石坊雕饰丰富多彩，又不失庄严的气质。石坊在此经历百余年月，周边光景早已改换，但它体现的孝义思想等作为传统美德的一部分却流传至今，仍然滋养着这一方土地。
projects.content_en: During the Qing Daoguang era, there was a Zhou Jisheng in Laifeng, Bishan, who always loved doing good deeds. His grandmother, née He, the wife of Fengzhi Dafu (a rank) Zhou Shaoxi, strictly observed wifely duties throughout her life in the Zhou family, and also often did good deeds to accumulate virtue, highly respected by people. So when He reached the age of 100, i.e., the 25th year of Daoguang (1845), Zhou Jisheng petitioned the court and obtained the imperial decree's approval to build this stone archway for his grandmother, hence called He's Centenarian Archway. He's Centenarian Archway was originally the second of three archways on the ancient post road of Laifeng, so locals also called it the Second Archway. Unfortunately, the first and third archways were both destroyed during the Cultural Revolution; it is truly fortunate that the Centenarian Archway has been preserved so completely. He's Centenarian Archway is a timber-imitating stone archway, with double-eave hip-and-gable (wudian) style roof, four columns, three bays, and five stories. It has a total height of 11m and width of 7.88m. At the very top there is a寿-character flame precious-pearl top, and on the eaves and ridges are decorated fish-dragon kissing ornaments. On the archway are carved many animal images such as lions, white elephants, qilin, and bats. On the small lintel of the front and back of the central bay is inscribed: This archway marks the centenarian He, wife of the posthumously granted Fengzhi Dafu Zhou Shaoxi, in recognition of her virtues — indicating the glory of this archway being approved by the emperor. On the plaque above the small lintel are carved Zhou Shaoxi's successive official positions and the preface to He's Centenarian Archway. On the large lintel are reliefs of mythological stories, with figures in various postures, lifelike. On the columns at both ends there were originally eight opera-costumed figure statues chiseled, now only six remain. On the front of the topmost plaque is carved Peaceful Times and Human Sage, and on the back is carved Gate of Chastity and Longevity. The entire stone archway has rich and colorful carvings and decorations, yet without losing its solemn temperament. The stone archway has experienced over a hundred years here; the surrounding scenery has long changed, but the concepts of filial piety and righteousness it embodies, as part of traditional virtues, have been passed down to this day, still nourishing this land.

projects.name: 河包报恩寺塔
projects.name_en: Pagoda of Bao'en Temple in Hebao
projects.address: 荣昌县河包镇白塔社区
projects.highlights: 盘龙柱、石斗拱、龙凤雀替
projects.content_zh: 报恩寺塔位于荣昌县河包镇白塔社区内一个小山坡上，当地人称之为白塔。行车至山坡下，离了公路，沿着一条石阶小路蜿蜒而上，来到坡顶一片石砌的平地上，便是塔的所在了。报恩寺塔建于南宋绍兴二年(1132年)，其所在地原为报恩寺。明末清初，报恩寺毁于大火，仅这一石塔幸免于难。塔为八层方形空心楼阁式，正面朝北，通高16米。塔基为素面双层正方形，边长5.2米，高1米，已被茂密的杂草湮没。塔身由下往上逐层内收，每层四面或开窗，或设有椭圆形佛龛，少数龛内残存佛像，但面容早已风化不清。底层四角有盘龙柱浮雕，鳞甲须鬣尚可辨认。各层檐下均施一斗三升斗拱若干，并浮雕龙凤雀替，造型别致，虽有局部风化，但神韵犹存。柱枋间依稀可见榫卯结构。塔身各层刻有经文。据记载，塔内有方形空心柱直贯顶层，石阶绕之盘旋，人可沿着石阶登至七层。然而如今一层正面的门已被石板砌封上，无法一尽登临之兴了。虽然整个塔身檐部缺损较多(越往上损毁越重，塔刹已全毁)，但它用石质构造向后世呈现了一斗三升、龙凤雀替等南宋独特的木构营造法式，堪称南宋石塔的建筑标本。报恩寺塔历经800余年沧桑，如今只与群山草木为伴，与白云飞鸟为友，纵使经文漫漶，佛像损毁，自另有一番禅意，难以言说，只可近它身旁细细体味，方得一二罢了。
projects.content_en: Bao'en (Requiting Kindness) Temple Pagoda is located on a small hillside in Baita Community, Hebao Town, Rongchang County; locals call it the White Pagoda. Driving to the foot of the hill, leaving the highway, and winding up along a stone-step path, one comes to a stone-paved flat ground on the hilltop, where the pagoda is located. Bao'en Temple Pagoda was built in the 2nd year of Shaoxing (1132), Southern Song; its location was originally Bao'en Temple. At the end of Ming and beginning of Qing, Bao'en Temple was destroyed by fire, and only this stone pagoda survived. The pagoda is an eight-story square hollow pavilion style, facing north, with a total height of 16m. The pagoda base is a plain double-layer square, 5.2m per side and 1m high, already湮没 by dense weeds. The pagoda body tapers inward from bottom to top layer by layer; each layer either opens windows on four sides or has oval Buddhist niches; a few niches have remnant Buddha statues, but their faces have long been weathered beyond recognition. At the four corners of the bottom layer there are coiled-dragon column reliefs, with scales, whiskers, and manes still recognizable. Under the eaves of each layer there are several one-bucket-three-capital bracket sets, and relief dragon-phoenix spandrel brackets (queti), with unique modeling; although there is local weathering, the charm remains. Between columns and lintels, mortise-and-tenon structures can be faintly seen. Each layer of the pagoda body is carved with scriptures. According to records, inside the pagoda there is a square hollow column running straight through to the top layer, with stone steps spiraling around it; people can climb along the stone steps to the seventh layer. However, today the door on the front of the first layer has been sealed with stone slabs, so one cannot fully enjoy the pleasure of climbing. Although the eave parts of the entire pagoda body have many defects (the higher up, the more severe the damage; the pagoda finial has been completely destroyed), it uses stone construction to present to later generations the unique Southern Song timber construction methods such as one-bucket-three-capital and dragon-phoenix spandrel brackets, and can be called an architectural specimen of Southern Song stone pagodas. Bao'en Temple Pagoda has experienced over 800 years of vicissitudes; today it only accompanies the mountains, plants, and trees, and befriends white clouds and flying birds. Even though the scriptures are blurred and the Buddha statues are damaged, it has its own Chan (Zen) meaning, hard to put into words; one can only get a hint by approaching it and savoring it carefully.

projects.name: 宝城寺
projects.address: 荣昌县昌元街道宝城寺村
projects.content_zh: 宝城寺隐藏在荣昌县昌元街上的一个党校内，找到它时里面正在进行维修，我们有幸提前一睹现状。进去后发现满地的碎石，一片混乱，以至于让人几乎无暇去关注它原本的格局。宝城寺始建于南宋绍兴年间，传统四合院布局，但朝向却是坐西南朝东北。现仅存明代藏经楼一座，以及清代前殿、后殿和右厢房，占地面积约2500平方米。藏经楼保存得很完整，看起来定是经过多次修缮了。一楼一底，共2层，高9.6米，四周有回廊。台基为须弥座样式，前部3级台阶。面阔五间，进深五间，抬梁式梁架。檐下有如意大斗拱4攒。重檐歇山式屋顶，翼角起翘明显。内外柱子柱础均为覆盆式。沿楼后方有一木制旋转楼梯可登至二层，楼内结构完整。相比之下，寺内其他部分的状况就凄惨多了。后殿原为悬山式，六架椽屋，面阔五间，有前廊。如今前廊尚在，殿前柱子和柱础也还完好，但其余部分已经过较大改造。右厢房仅留存有抬梁式木构架，屋顶已不见。前殿为一硬山顶式建筑，内部为穹形天花顶，可见部分梁架结构上用了天然弯木，看上去倒有几分趣味。整体结构虽有些破损，但尚可辨认。希望这残破光景能在这次修复中得到改善。但这样的修复到底能还原多少真实，又会虚构出多少历史，我们不得而知。
projects.content_en: Baocheng Temple is hidden inside a party school on Changyuan Street, Rongchang County; when we found it, repairs were underway inside, and we were fortunate to get a glimpse of its current state in advance. After entering, we found碎石 all over the ground, a scene of chaos, so much so that people almost had no time to pay attention to its original layout. Baocheng Temple was first built during the Southern Song Shaoxing era, with a traditional siheyuan layout, but its orientation is facing northeast from the southwest. Now only one Ming dynasty Scripture Depository Tower remains, as well as the Qing front hall, rear hall, and right wing room, covering an area of about 2,500 sq m. The Scripture Depository Tower is very well preserved and must have been repaired many times. One floor plus one mezzanine, totaling 2 stories, 9.6m high, with surrounding corridors. The platform base is in the xumizuo (Sumeru pedestal) style, with 3 steps at the front. It is 5 bays wide and 5 bays deep, with a beam-lifting frame. Under the eave there are 4 clusters of ruyi (wishful) large bracket sets. It has a double-eave xieshan-style roof, with obvious upturned wing corners. The column bases of both inner and outer columns are of the inverted-basin style. Behind the tower there is a wooden spiral staircase that can climb to the second floor; the structure inside the tower is complete. In comparison, the condition of other parts of the temple is much more miserable. The rear hall was originally of overhanging-gable style, with six rafter bays, 5 bays wide, and a front porch. Today the front porch still exists, and the columns and column bases in front of the hall are also intact, but the rest has been greatly modified. The right wing room only retains the beam-lifting timber frame, and the roof is gone. The front hall is a flush-gable-roof building, with a domed ceiling inside; visible parts of the beam frame structure use naturally curved timber, which looks somewhat interesting. Although the overall structure is somewhat damaged, it can still be辨认. It is hoped that this dilapidated scene can be improved in this restoration. But how much truth such a restoration can restore, and how much history it will fabricate, we do not know.

projects.name: 彭氏民居（彭瑞川庄园）
projects.name_en: Dwelling of Peng Family (Peng Ruichuan Manor)
projects.address: 巴南区南泉镇白鹤林村南500米
projects.content_zh: 我们都知道山西的乔家大院，其实，在重庆巴南的南泉街道白鹤村，也有一处传统的民居建筑群，被称作彭家大院，这便是彭氏民居，或称彭瑞川庄园。彭氏民居始建于清道光二年(1822年)，道光十年(1830年)竣工。民居前有花溪河，后靠樵坪山，符合传统风水理论的选址特征。整个大院占地面积5320平方米，建筑面积约3860平方米。民居采用传统多重合院布局，中轴线上依次排列前厅、过厅、上厅，院内存天井12个，大小房间77间。整个建筑群采用小青瓦屋顶，地面青石板铺就，四周环绕5～7米高的砖石围墙与封火墙维护。此处建筑规模较大，形制完整，保存良好，是重要的民居建筑样本。彭氏祖籍江西，清初迁往四川，宗系内曾出过礼部尚书等高官。彭瑞川生活在清末，善于经商，资产丰厚，于道光二年(1822年)选址白鹤林，建造彭家大院。后因世事变迁，家道中落，彭氏一族也不再聚居于此。彭氏家族没落后，彭氏民居因其规模与气势而成为众多政府机构的驻所，如国民党中央政治大学研究部，中共南方局所创立的西南学院，以及新中国成立后的西南革命大学等。此后多年，此处一直被用作学校，直至2002年，彭氏民居划归重庆市巴南区文物保护管理所管理，才得到更多关注，近年来也成为多部影视作品的拍摄地。
projects.content_en: We all know the Qiao Family Compound in Shanxi; in fact, in Baihe Village, Nanquan Subdistrict, Banan District, Chongqing, there is also a traditional residential building complex, called the Peng Family Compound — this is the Peng Family Dwelling, or Peng Ruichuan Manor. The Peng Family Dwelling was first built in the 2nd year of Daoguang (1822), Qing, and completed in the 10th year of Daoguang (1830). In front of the dwelling there is the Huaxi River, and behind it leans Qiaoping Mountain, conforming to the site-selection characteristics of traditional fengshui theory. The entire compound covers an area of 5,320 sq m, with a building area of about 3,860 sq m. The dwelling adopts a traditional multiple-courtyard layout; on the central axis are sequentially arranged the front hall, passage hall, and upper hall; within the courtyard there are 12 courtyards (tianjing) and 77 rooms large and small. The entire building complex uses small grey-tile roofs, with floors paved with bluestone slabs, surrounded by 5-7m-high brick-stone enclosure walls and fire-sealing walls for protection. The buildings here are large in scale, complete in form, and well preserved, being an important sample of residential architecture. The Peng family ancestral home was Jiangxi; they moved to Sichuan in the early Qing, and within the clan there once were high officials such as the Minister of Rites. Peng Ruichuan lived in the late Qing, was good at business, with abundant assets; in the 2nd year of Daoguang (1822), he selected the site at Baihelin and built the Peng Family Compound. Later, due to changes in the world, the family fortunes declined, and the Peng clan no longer lived together here. After the Peng family declined, the Peng Family Dwelling, due to its scale and momentum, became the residence of many government institutions, such as the Research Department of the Central Political University of the Kuomintang, the Southwest Academy founded by the Southern Bureau of the Communist Party of China, and the Southwest Revolutionary University after the founding of New China, etc. For many years thereafter, this place was continuously used as a school; until 2002, when the Peng Family Dwelling was transferred to the management of the Cultural Relics Protection and Management Office of Banan District, Chongqing, it received more attention, and in recent years it has also become a filming location for many film and television works.

projects.name: 江公享堂
projects.address: 江津区几江街道办事处石狮子街
projects.content_zh: 江公享堂始建于明成化年间，位于江津区中心，3路公共汽车直达。江公享堂是江津人明代辅相江渊的府第。建筑合院布局，坐南朝北，面阔21米，通进47米，大门竖匾江公享堂，大门两侧有楹联北极勋臣府，西川相国家，是明成化帝朱见深为褒奖江渊功劳钦题。清末一场大火将江公享堂的建筑损毁殆尽，如今院内只有青石地面为明代遗物，其余都是近年重建。现有建筑为砖木石结构，悬山式屋顶，部分构件上刻有仿明代风格的浮雕。如今的江公享堂开放作为老年活动中心，内部时常举办社区活动，颇受附近居民欢迎。
projects.content_en: Jiang Gong Xiangtang (Jiang's Memorial Hall) was first built during the Ming Chenghua era, located in the center of Jiangjin District, directly reachable by Bus Route 3. Jiang Gong Xiangtang was the mansion of Jiang Yuan, a Ming dynasty auxiliary prime minister from Jiangjin. The building has a courtyard layout, facing north from the south, 21m wide and 47m deep. The main gate has a vertical plaque reading Jiang Gong Xiangtang; on both sides of the main gate there is a couplet: Mansion of the Meritorious Minister of the North Pole, Home of the Prime Minister of Western Sichuan — personally inscribed by Emperor Chenghua Zhu Jianshen of Ming to reward Jiang Yuan's merits. A great fire at the end of Qing destroyed the buildings of Jiang Gong Xiangtang completely; today only the bluestone floor inside the courtyard is a Ming relic, and the rest were rebuilt in recent years. The existing buildings are of brick-timber-stone structure, with overhanging-gable roofs; some components are carved with reliefs imitating Ming style. Today's Jiang Gong Xiangtang is open as a senior activity center; community activities are often held inside, quite popular with nearby residents.

projects.name: 石门大佛寺摩崖石刻
projects.name_en: Cliffside Statues of Dafo Temple in Shimen
projects.address: 江津区石门镇白坪村(原凉亭村)东100米处
projects.content_zh: 石门大佛寺是一处以佛教水月观音造像为主体的古寺院，由宋代开凿的观世音造像、寺院建筑等构成。观世音坐像依山崖凿出，通高13.5米，为我国现存最大的以观音为供奉主尊的石造像。造像容貌端庄，服袖精美，辅以贴金彩绘，风格独特。寺院坐北向南，由月台、寺门、像阁与左右厢房等组成，主体建筑为覆盖观音造像的木结构像阁。像阁坐北面南，七重飞檐，逐层缩进，角檐飞挑，极为生动。像阁规模宏大，气势高昂，正面面对万里长江，气宇轩昂。像阁大约始建于宋，历代修葺，现存建筑经过近年整修，展现出清初建筑风格特征。除此而外，寺内存有清同治八年(1869年)重修大佛寺碑一通，以及摩崖题刻若干。石门大佛寺造像尺度宏大，雕刻精美，像阁建筑保存完整，与山势佛像相互协调，是展现中国传统佛教造像与像阁建筑相互关系的重要范例。
projects.content_en: Shimen Dafo (Great Buddha) Temple is an ancient temple complex with the Buddhist Water-Moon Guanyin statue as the main subject, composed of the Guanyin statue chiseled in Song dynasty, temple buildings, etc. The seated Guanyin statue was chiseled against the cliff, with a total height of 13.5m, being the largest existing stone statue in China with Guanyin as the main enshrined deity. The statue has a dignified appearance and exquisite sleeves, supplemented by gilded paintings, with a unique style. The temple faces south, composed of the moon platform, temple gate, statue pavilion, and left and right wing rooms, etc.; the main building is the timber-structure statue pavilion covering the Guanyin statue. The statue pavilion faces south, with seven layers of flying eaves, tapering inward layer by layer, with corner eaves flying outward, extremely vivid. The statue pavilion is large in scale and high in momentum, facing the Ten-Thousand-Li Yangtze River on the front, with an imposing bearing. The statue pavilion was approximately first built in Song, repaired through dynasties; the existing building has been renovated in recent years, showing the architectural style characteristics of the early Qing. In addition, inside the temple there is one stele of Rebuilding Dafo Temple from the 8th year of Tongzhi (1869), Qing, as well as several cliffside inscriptions. The statues of Shimen Dafo Temple are grand in scale and exquisitely carved; the statue pavilion building is completely preserved, coordinating with the mountain terrain and the Buddha statue, being an important example showing the relationship between traditional Chinese Buddhist statues and statue-pavilion architecture.

projects.name: 利济桥
projects.address: 重庆市江津区朱杨镇境内板桥场
projects.content_zh: 利济桥又名万古桥，当地人称其板桥。清朝乾隆末年(1765年)，乡人筹资修建，清道光六年(1826年)竣工落成。此桥为五孔石拱桥，横跨溶溪河上。桥长84米，宽8.8米，高13.2米。两侧石栏有各种图案花纹，桥面中部镶嵌着传说中的神仙石。当年乡民集资建桥，到了铺砌最后一块桥面石的时候，却找不到合适的石头。此时，一个貌似乞丐的人开口对面一位老大娘家的坝子里有合适的石头，大家顺道寻去，果然找到合适的石块。正要抬走时，老大娘说这是当年所收留的乞丐打造的，他说需要留下二两银子才能搬走石块。于是乡民们买下了石块，也算是对大娘善行的报答。大桥终于凭此石块得以完工。利济桥两桥头，原有两座石牌坊，一侧还有一座文昌庙，可惜这些建筑在文革中均已损毁不存。
projects.content_en: Liji Bridge, also called Wangu (Eternal) Bridge, is called Banqiao (Plank Bridge) by locals. In the late Qianlong era of Qing (1765), villagers raised funds to build it, and it was completed in the 6th year of Daoguang (1826), Qing. This bridge is a five-arch stone bridge, spanning the Rongxi River. The bridge is 84m long, 8.8m wide, and 13.2m high. The stone railings on both sides have various patterns and designs; in the middle of the bridge deck is inlaid the legendary Immortal Stone. When villagers raised funds to build the bridge that year, when it came to paving the last bridge-deck stone, they could not find a suitable stone. At this moment, a person resembling a beggar spoke up, saying that there was a suitable stone in the courtyard of an old lady's home opposite; everyone went along the way to look, and indeed found a suitable stone block. Just as they were about to carry it away, the old lady said this was made by a beggar she had taken in that year, and he said that two taels of silver needed to be left before the stone could be moved away. So the villagers bought the stone block, which can also be regarded as a repayment for the old lady's good deeds. The bridge was finally completed thanks to this stone block. At both ends of Liji Bridge, there were originally two stone archways, and on one side there was also a Wenchang (God of Literature) Temple; unfortunately, these buildings were all destroyed and no longer exist during the Cultural Revolution.

projects.name: 龙崖城
projects.address: 南川区马嘴乡三泉镇马嘴村西3.5公里
projects.content_zh: 龙崖城遗址地处金佛山风景区北面马嘴山上，海拔约1784米，地势险峻，易守难攻，自古以来就是兵家必争之地。南宋时期的龙崖城是宋军抗蒙的重要堡垒，几经征战，御蒙功绩几可与合川钓鱼城齐名。遗址平面形似马颈，东西宽1.5公里，南北长2.5公里，总面积约3.75平方公里。城内遗存有城门、石阶、水井、垛墩、射孔。城门建造在两块突出的巨石之上，为石砌的圆形拱门，门楣上方的条石额上，刻着蟠龙岩3个大字。城墙虽残存不多，但仍可看出其依势而建，高居山顶，气度非凡。城内仍保留有10米见方天池一口，应为当年屯兵蓄水之用。龙崖城虽已破败，但其险绝之处仍然展现建筑与自然相互结合的鬼斧神工之妙，硝烟已没入荒草之中，唯有石头与题刻仍然歌颂着历史。
projects.content_en: The Longya (Dragon Cliff) Fortress ruin is located on Mazui Mountain, north of the Jinfo Mountain Scenic Area, at an altitude of about 1,784m, with steep terrain, easy to defend and difficult to attack, and has been a contested military stronghold since ancient times. Longya Fortress in the Southern Song period was an important stronghold for the Song army against the Mongols; after several battles, its merits in resisting the Mongols were almost as famous as Diaoyu Fortress in Hechuan. The ruin plane resembles a horse neck, 1.5 km wide east-west and 2.5 km long north-south, with a total area of about 3.75 sq km. Inside the city there remain city gates, stone steps, wells, merlon piers, and arrow slits. The city gate was built on two protruding huge stones, as a stone-built circular arch gate; on the dressed-stone lintel above the gate opening are engraved the three large characters Panlong (Coiled Dragon) Rock. Although little of the city wall remains, one can still see that it was built according to the terrain, perched high on the mountaintop, with extraordinary bearing. Inside the city there still remains a Heavenly Pond about 10m square, which should have been used for storing water for the garrison in those days. Although Longya Fortress has fallen into ruin, its precipitous places still show the miraculous craftsmanship of combining architecture with nature; the smoke of gunpowder has sunk into the weeds, and only stones and inscriptions still sing praises of history.
